_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401883136.overall: Leganés are 18th, one point above the drop zone, with one point from their last seven league games and no league win since 20 September; Luis Carrión's only win since replacing Rubén Albés is Tuesday's narrow Copa del Rey victory at Trival Valderas. Burgos are third and unbeaten in four after coming from behind to beat Celta Fortuna 2-1, but are without the injured Jon Karrikaburu and David González and the internationals Kevin Appin and Bruno Iribarne. New since the last view: Gonzalo Romero Freixas referees, Burgos have Llabrés and Saúl del Cerro back in training, and Leganés are missing players on international duty, with Ismaël Gharbi still out.

goals.text: The numbers now say 1.8 goals, down from 2.0. I still lean higher: Leganés have conceded 23 in 13 games and must chase this at home, and Sergio Francisco admits Burgos keep conceding early, though they have come back from behind repeatedly. Carrión's Leganés are, in Francisco's words, more attacking but less balanced than under Albés.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean a little higher: Leganés should have most of the ball at Butarque under Carrión's more combinative approach, and Francisco says Burgos will try to press them back into their own half, so both ends should see set pieces. Nothing in this week's news changes that.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards, already high, and I lean a little higher. Leganés are a nervous side near the drop zone with Francisco Montero banned after a red, and Burgos plan to press high and win the ball back in Leganés's half, which brings fouls. Romero Freixas is confirmed as referee; I found no recent card figures for him, so this lean rests on the context.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots. I keep a slight lean lower: Burgos are missing two forwards (Karrikaburu, Iribarne) and Francisco is talking about clean sheets rather than an open game. Leganés should take most of the attempts, as they did with 17 against Albacete, but 12.5 for Burgos looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target and I leave it there. Leganés have scored only 11 goals in 13 games and Morata is on three, while Burgos are efficient rather than prolific, with Curro Sánchez on four and the Forés goal that beat Celta Fortuna.

401883114.overall: Castellón are second with the best defence in the division (five conceded in 12 games) but have not played a league game since 1 November after their match with Eibar was postponed; they did win a Copa del Rey tie against Conquense. New since the last view: they lose Matías Orozco (suspended and away with his national team), Amir Saipi and Rodrigo Rêgo to international duty, so Pablo Hernández must rebuild his midfield around Diego Barri, with Álvaro Martín or Jari Vlak in Orozco's role. Valladolid have won two in a row but are without the suspended Iván Alejo (fifth yellow), the injured Latasa and Guille Bueno, and Homam and Balboa, who are with their national teams. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I still lean lower: Castellón have let in five goals in 12 league games and Valladolid are missing Latasa, Alejo, Balboa and Homam. The one change pushing the other way is that Castellón lose Orozco as the shield in front of their defence, so I would not go much lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and I stay there. Castellón keep the ball (6,747 passes in 12 games by LaLiga's count, against Valladolid's 5,462 in 13) and use the width, but a Valladolid side without Alejo and Balboa is unlikely to win many at the other end.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. I lean a little higher: LaLiga's figures show Valladolid on 37 yellows and four reds against Castellón's 22 and two, and a home side chasing a possession team usually commits the fouls. Castellón's reshuffled midfield without Orozco may also have to stop more counters than usual. No referee has been named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. I lean lower: LaLiga counts Valladolid at 135 shots in 13 games and Castellón 121 in 12, both near ten a game, and Valladolid are short of attackers. Castellón's game is about control, not volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean lower for the same reasons: a Castellón defence that has conceded five league goals all season and a Valladolid attack missing Latasa, Alejo and Balboa. Castellón's main threat is Israel Suero, October's player of the month with six goals.

401883134.overall: Real Sociedad II (Sanse) drew 0-0 at Sabadell on Monday, a result that lifted Jon Ansotegi's side out of the relegation zone; they hit the bar and had a goal ruled out for offside. Sporting's attack is badly depleted: Juan Otero is suspended after his red card against Valladolid, and two reports agree Nicolás Larcamón is also without Alejo Sarco (muscle problem), Antonio Casas, Konrad de la Fuente, César Gelabert, Pablo García and Manu Rodríguez. Sarco and Casas share the club's scoring lead with Guille Rosas on three goals; Andrés Ferrari is back after eight months out but not fully fit. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I have changed my lean from higher to lower: Sporting are without Otero, Sarco and Casas, three of their main forwards, and have scored only 14 in 13 games. Sanse's last game was a 0-0 in which they missed clear chances.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and I stay there. Sporting keep the ball (5,966 passes in 13 games by LaLiga's count) and Sanse like to attack down the right through Díaz, their top assister with five, so corners should come at both ends.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards. I still lean higher: LaLiga has Sanse on 231 fouls committed in 13 games, the most of any team in this round's previews I checked, and both sides have 37 yellows and two reds. Sanse took three more yellows at Sabadell on Monday.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. I have moved from same to lower: Sporting's weakened forward line makes their volume less likely, and LaLiga counts both teams under ten shots a game this season (128 for Sanse, 122 for Sporting). Ferrari may play some minutes, but he is short of fitness.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Sporting's top scorers are missing, and Sanse put few efforts on target in their 0-0 at Sabadell. Gorosabel and Astiazaran, Sanse's top scorers, have three goals each.

401883118.overall: Leaders Almería (29 points, 24 scored and 10 conceded) host an Andorra side playing for the first time since the 2 November collision between their goalkeeper Jesús Owono and Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel, who died the next day. Coach Carles Manso said on Thursday the dressing room is still affected and the players have psychological support; Owono has not returned to training, and several reports agree his sanction has not yet been decided, so a replacement goalkeeper will play. Changed since the last view: the site no longer lists Lautaro De León or Efe Akman as suspended, and one report says Almería's Lopy is out and Chirino doubtful. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I still lean a little lower: Almería's last three league games were tight (1-0 at Girona, 1-1, 2-2) and they concede under a goal a game. Andorra's emotional state is the hardest thing to read; a stand-in goalkeeper is the main reason not to go lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners and I leave it. Both teams pass a lot (over 6,000 passes each by LaLiga's count), so Andorra may not simply sit deep, but Almería at home should still win most of the corners. The two effects broadly cancel out.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, with Andorra expected to take 3.6. I lean lower: in their first match since the tragedy, I expect a careful game and a lenient tone, and Almería (25 yellows, the fewest of the two) have little reason to make it physical. Andorra's 205 fouls committed in 12 games are the risk to this lean.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean lower: Almería's win at Girona came from about 12 shots per side and LaLiga counts them at 130 shots in 13 games, ten a game. Andorra are more willing shooters (147 in 12), but a squad that has barely trained normally for a fortnight may not keep that up.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, high for this division. I lean lower: Almería's recent games have been controlled rather than open, and Miguel de la Fuente (eight goals) tends to need few chances. If Andorra's replacement goalkeeper looks shaky, Almería may test him more, which is the main risk.

401883135.overall: Mallorca have not played in the league since beating Cádiz on 2 November because their game at Andorra was postponed, so Luis García's side arrive rested, sixth and with a game in hand. Córdoba beat Ceuta 3-0 last time out, with Diego Percan (six league goals) scoring twice. I found little fresh team news for this match this week, so the view rests mainly on form and LaLiga's season figures; no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I have moved from higher to same: Mallorca's league games average under two goals (15 scored, 7 conceded in 12), while Córdoba's average more than three (22-22 in 13). Adrián Fuentes (seven goals) against a leaky Córdoba defence pulls one way, Mallorca's tight defence the other.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. I keep a slight lean higher: Córdoba build a lot through crosses and have taken 154 shots in 13 games by LaLiga's count, the kind of attacking that wins corners even away, and Mallorca will have plenty of the ball at Son Moix.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. I lean a touch higher: LaLiga has Córdoba on 43 yellows, two reds and 208 fouls committed in 13 games, and they finished at Celta Fortuna with nine men two games ago. With no referee named yet, I would not go far above six.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots, with 15.0 for Mallorca. I have moved from same to lower: LaLiga counts Mallorca at only 109 shots in 12 games, among the fewest in the division, so their share looks high even at home. Córdoba should get their usual volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target, which fits two sides with reliable finishers in Fuentes and Percan. Mallorca's low shot volume and Córdoba's open games roughly cancel out, so I lean neither way.

401883115.overall: Real Oviedo won 2-1 at Cádiz in round 13 (Estanis Pedrola and Ilyas Chaira scoring), and the last view reported, from one source, that Raúl González has replaced Julián Calero as coach, making this his home debut; I could not confirm that with a second source this week. Girona, relegated last season, are eighth on the same 21 points after two 1-0 defeats, the latest at home to Almería. I found little fresh team news for this match, and no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals, down from 2.5. I lean higher: Oviedo's last four league games had three, five, four and three goals, and Girona have the division's strongest forwards on paper in Vladyslav Vanat and Yáser Asprilla (five goals each), though the site lists both as injured and only expected back around now. A home side keen to impress pushes the same way.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean slightly higher: Girona will push to end a two-game losing run with wide players such as Carles Pérez, and Oviedo have been one of the higher-volume shooting sides (155 shots in 13 games by LaLiga's count).

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards. I lean a bit higher: LaLiga has Oviedo on 43 yellows in 13 games, one of the highest totals in the division, and Girona picked up three first-half yellows against Almería and a red at Zubieta in their last two games.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots. I have moved from same to slightly lower: LaLiga counts Oviedo at 155 shots in 13 games and Girona 138, a combined rate a little below the site's figure, and Girona's attempts have dipped in their two defeats.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target and I stay there. Girona's forwards have not scored in two games, and Oviedo, without Chris Ramos, have a centre-back, Carlos Domínguez, as top scorer with five.

401883113.overall: This is Tenerife's first match since striker Jesús de Miguel died on 3 November, a day after colliding with Andorra's goalkeeper at the Heliodoro; their game at Granada was postponed, so the emotional context outweighs anything in the numbers. Álvaro Cervera's side had drawn four in a row before that, while bottom club Ceuta (five points, 30 goals conceded) lost 3-0 at Córdoba last time out and, per one earlier report, have a new coach in Sergio Lobera. I found little fresh team news for this match this week, and no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and I stay there. Ceuta concede more than two a game, which points up, but Tenerife have been a draw team and have scored only 15 in 12 games. An emotionally heavy day is hard to read either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners and I leave it. Tenerife should have more of the territory against a side that has lost five in a row, but the site already gives them the larger share, and Ceuta are likely to try to stay compact.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. I lean lower: in the first game at the Heliodoro since De Miguel's death, I expect both teams to avoid flashpoints, and Tenerife are among the cleaner sides (28 yellows in 12 games by LaLiga's count). Ceuta's 35 yellows are the main risk to this lean.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.7 shots. I have changed my lean from higher to lower: LaLiga counts Tenerife at only 94 shots in 12 games, the lowest rate of any team I checked this round, so even against the league's worst defence their 11.9 looks high. Ceuta shoot more (142 in 13) but have scored only ten goals.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. I have moved from higher to same: Ceuta's defence has been breached 30 times and Enric Gallego has eight goals, but Tenerife's low shot volume holds me back from going higher.

401883116.overall: Granada have won five league games in a row under Pacheta but have not played in the league since 1 November because their home game with Tenerife was postponed. Las Palmas have won two straight under Albert Sánchez, the latest 2-0 at home to Eldense with both goals (Álex Suárez and Betancor) in stoppage time, per one match roundup. I found little fresh team news this week; no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I have moved from lower to same: Granada's run was built on narrow wins, but their league games average close to three goals (20-14 in 12) and Las Palmas's just over three (19-21 in 13). Nothing in the news points clearly either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners and I keep it there. Granada are happy without the ball (4,574 passes in 12 games by LaLiga's count, against 5,955 for Las Palmas), so their 5.2 may be a little high, but Las Palmas should get more than 3.9 if they have most of the ball.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and I see no clear push either way. LaLiga has Granada on just 22 yellows and no reds in 12 games and Las Palmas on 34 and two, which the site's split already reflects.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots, with Granada expected to take 14.4. I lean slightly lower: Granada win through efficiency rather than volume, and LaLiga counts Las Palmas at only 106 shots in 13 games. Two weeks without a league game may also blunt Granada's sharpness.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Granada had few efforts on target in their win at Elda, and Las Palmas needed stoppage time to break down Eldense last week. Jesé is Las Palmas's top scorer with four.

401883117.overall: Eibar are fourth but have not played since a 1-1 draw with Almería on 31 October, after their trip to Castellón was postponed, and have one league win in their last five. Cádiz are 20th and have lost two in a row under Borja Jiménez, the latest 1-2 at home to Oviedo with a late Urko Izeta header. I found little fresh team news this week, so the view rests mainly on form and LaLiga's season figures; no referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I have moved from lower to same: Eibar keep games tight with little of the ball, but their league games average close to three goals (21-14 in 12) and Cádiz's about two and a half. The site's figure already sits below both teams' averages.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, with 5.4 for Eibar. I lean slightly lower: Eibar pass less than most (4,806 passes in 12 games by LaLiga's count) and rarely build the sustained pressure that wins corners, even at home.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean higher: LaLiga has Cádiz on 42 yellows in 13 games, and a side in the relegation zone after two defeats will have to fight for every second ball. Jokin Aranbarri has also asked his players to be more aggressive, so Eibar's 1.9 looks low.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with 17.5 for Eibar. That looks high: LaLiga counts Eibar at 121 shots in 12 games and Cádiz at 111 in 13, both around ten a game or fewer. Two weeks without a league game adds to the case for a slower match.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean lower in line with the shots: Eibar scored one goal or none in each of their last three league games, and Cádiz have been blunt away. Antoñito is Cádiz's top scorer with five.

401883137.overall: Javi Calleja's Eldense have lost three league games in a row without scoring, the latest 2-0 at Las Palmas to two stoppage-time goals. Sabadell drew 0-0 at home to Real Sociedad II on Monday and are 13th, four points off the play-offs; they are without Urri (suspended), Peque and Nicholas Gioacchini, one of their top scorers. Changed since the last view: LaLiga's figures show Sabadell are not a possession side and foul a lot, which turns my cards lean. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.7 goals and I agree with a low figure. Eldense have not scored in three league games and Sabadell's games average under two goals (12-11 in 13). The site is already low, so I do not go lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I have moved from higher to same: Eldense like the ball, but LaLiga counts Sabadell at only 4,320 passes in 13 games, so this is less of a two-way territorial battle than I thought. Nothing points clearly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards. I have changed my lean from lower to higher: LaLiga has Sabadell on 225 fouls committed in 13 games, far more than they receive, and 39 yellows, while Eldense have 35 yellows. A low-scoring game between two sides needing points should keep the tackles coming.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. I have changed from higher to lower: LaLiga counts Eldense at 125 shots and Sabadell at 139 in 13 games each, and Sabadell are missing Gioacchini. Eldense's run without a goal suggests they are not creating much.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.2 shots on target and I leave it. Both teams create more than they convert: Sabadell drew a blank against Sanse on Monday and Eldense have not scored in three games.

401883305.overall: Early view: Albacete have won three in a row under Joseba Etxeberria, the latest 3-1 at Leganés, where a Leganés goal was disallowed after VAR spotted Morata's elbow on Jesús Vallejo, but they are still 21st. Celta Fortuna, Celta's reserve side, are 16th after a 2-1 defeat at Burgos and arrive with a long absence list, including three suspensions (Adrià Capdevila, Enrique Ribes, Hugo López). I found little fresh team news this week; lineups and the referee will be added closer to the Monday-night kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, which fits the context: Celta Fortuna's league games average more than three goals (19-25 in 13) and they will field a patched-up side again. Against that, Albacete have scored only 13 in 13 and are without José Corpas, so I hold at the site's figure.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with 6.3 for Albacete. I lean lower: Etxeberria's Albacete have been winning by scoring and defending, not by dominating, and Celta Fortuna pass more (5,515 passes to Albacete's 4,739 by LaLiga's count), so they should have more of the ball than the split suggests.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards. I lean higher: Albacete press high under Etxeberria, Corpas was sent off recently, and Celta Fortuna have 37 yellows and three players already banned for accumulation. A Monday-night game between 21st and 16th should be scrappy.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. I lean lower, mainly on Albacete's side: LaLiga counts them at 113 shots in 13 games, under nine a game, so 16.2 at home does not match how they play. Celta Fortuna (119 in 13) can contribute their share.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. I lean lower with the shots: Albacete's wins have come from few attempts, and Celta Fortuna rely heavily on Álvaro Marín (eight goals) with Óscar Marcos, their joint second scorer, reported injured by one source.

401883112.overall: Early view: A game between 18th and 17th, 11 days away. Andorra's first games after the Tenerife tragedy will shape this one; goalkeeper Jesús Owono faces a ban of four to 12 games under the disciplinary code, per one report, while Efe Akman's one-match yellow-card ban should already be served at Almería. Leganés's Francisco Montero should likewise have served his ban against Burgos, and Luis Carrión needs results quickly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leganés have conceded eight goals in Carrión's three games (1-1, 4-3, 1-3), and Andorra are likely to have a stand-in goalkeeper with Owono suspended. Both sides sit near the drop zone and need wins, which tends to open games up late.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and I stay there. Leganés's possession game (about two-thirds of the ball against Albacete) should give them more than the 3.8 the site has, but that is likely to come out of Andorra's 5.6 rather than add to the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. Leganés have had several suspensions lately and the stakes are high at the bottom, but Andorra will be careful after a month under scrutiny, so I hold at about six until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots, with 17.5 for Andorra. I lean lower: that split looks lopsided against a Leganés side that keeps the ball and took 17 shots in its last game, and Andorra's attack may still be without Lautaro De León if his ban runs on. I expect a more even, lower total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target, with 6.4 for Andorra. I lean lower for the same reason: Andorra's home share looks too high for this matchup. Leganés's own accuracy has been poor (one goal from 17 shots against Albacete, plus Morata's missed penalty).

401882299.overall: Early view: Sabadell, who like to dominate the ball (66 per cent and 25 shots at Albacete), host a Granada side that has won five league games in a row with efficient, low-possession football. Granada's postponed game with Tenerife still has to be rescheduled, and Óscar Sanz should be back for Sabadell after his ban. Both teams play in round 14 first, so this view will move.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and I agree with a low total. Granada have three clean sheets in their last five league games and Sabadell average about a goal a game at both ends. Sabadell holding the ball against a Granada side happy to wait suggests a slow, low-scoring game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. I lean higher: Sabadell's habit of keeping the ball and shooting often (25 attempts at Albacete) should earn more corners than their 5.1, and Granada were content to let Eldense have the ball and the pressure that came with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, with 3.2 for Sabadell. I lean lower: the side with most of the ball usually commits fewer fouls, and Sabadell will be that side. Granada may pick up a few for slowing the game, but a total near five looks more likely.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots, with 17.1 for Sabadell, which matches their style. Granada were outshot 13-8 in their last game and still won, so 9.5 for them is fair. I see no reason to move the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target and I leave it. Sabadell's volume comes with modest accuracy, and Granada take few but clean chances (Alcaraz's header and Owen Emeka's late finish at Elda). Worth revisiting after both sides' round-14 games.

401883108.overall: Early view: A relegation six-pointer between 19th and 20th. Real Sociedad II (Sanse) host Sporting first; Cádiz, who have won one of their last five league games, go to Eibar in round 14. Borja Jiménez won his debut against Ceuta but has lost both games since, so the pressure on both sides should be high by kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean a little higher: Sanse's home games have been open (2-4 against Almería, 2-3 against Granada), and Cádiz have scored in all three games under Jiménez, including a late Urko Izeta header at home to Oviedo.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and I keep it. Sanse should have more of the ball at home, as they did against Girona, and Cádiz push hard in second halves when behind, as they did against Oviedo. Nothing suggests a big swing either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards. I lean higher: Sanse committed 27 fouls and received six yellows against Girona, and a bottom-of-the-table game where neither side can afford to lose should be tense from the start.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots, with 16.9 for Sanse. I lean slightly lower: Sanse took 14 shots against ten-man Girona, so nearly 17 against Cádiz looks generous, and six-pointers between nervous sides often slow down.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, which fits two teams who score a fair amount but not efficiently. I hold here until both have played in round 14.

401882301.overall: Early view: Second-placed Castellón, who visit Valladolid first, have the best defence in the division and have beaten Sporting 4-0 and Tenerife 5-0 at Castalia. Eldense under Javi Calleja host Sabadell first and had lost their last two league games without scoring before their round-13 trip to Las Palmas. Matías Orozco, listed by the site as suspended, should have served his ban at Valladolid.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, almost all of them Castellón's. I stay close to that: Castellón can run up scores at home (4-0, 5-0) but also grind out narrow results, and Eldense have gone two league games without a goal, so the total depends almost entirely on how ruthless the hosts are.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. I lean higher: Pablo Hernández's side use the full width of the pitch from back to front and should spend long spells in Eldense's half, which pushes their 5.6 up. Eldense want the ball under Calleja, but at Castalia they are unlikely to keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, with 3.1 for Eldense. I lean lower: Eldense have one of the cleaner records in the division (28 yellows and no reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), and Castellón win the ball back through possession and quick recovery rather than by fouling.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots and I agree. Castellón will take most of them; Eldense managed 13 at home to Granada but will get far fewer at Castalia. Nothing in the news moves the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Castellón's forwards (Israel Suero six goals, Ousmane Camara four) are efficient and the site already gives them the bulk; I keep the figure until the round-14 news is in.

401883107.overall: Early view: Tenerife play Ceuta first in their emotional return after the death of Jesús de Miguel, so this view will be revisited. They had drawn four in a row under Álvaro Cervera before the tragedy, and Mallorca are also draw-prone (four draws in 12), with their own postponed game at Andorra still to be given a new date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals and I lean lower still: Mallorca's last three away league games ended 1-1, 1-1 and 0-0, and Tenerife's run before the tragedy was four draws in a row, three of them 1-1. Adrián Fuentes is the one player who can break a tight game open.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners and I keep it. Neither team has been dominant in recent weeks and both have been content to take draws, so there is no sign of a lopsided game that would push the count up.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Mallorca's 3.5 looks a little high for the away side, but with no referee named and Tenerife's mood after the Ceuta game unknown, I hold at the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.0 shots, a low figure that fits two cautious sides. I see nothing yet to move it; Tenerife's first game back against Ceuta will say more about their attacking intent.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with the goals: Mallorca's away games have been short of clear chances (a 0-0 at Girona and two 1-1s), and Tenerife lean heavily on Enric Gallego's eight goals.

401882300.overall: Early view: Córdoba, 10th, host an Oviedo side that will be playing only its second game under Raúl González, who one report says replaced Julián Calero on 9 November. Oviedo have one of the best away records in the division (13 points), while Iván Ania's Córdoba have won three of their last four league games and score regularly at El Arcángel.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already high, and I agree. Oviedo's away games have been lively (2-1 at Cádiz, 2-2 at Almería, 2-1 at Ceuta) and Córdoba have scored in each of their last four league games, so a low-scoring game would be the surprise.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with 7.3 for Córdoba, which suits a team that attacks through crosses (Fran Escribá made stopping them his priority). I would not go higher than the site because Oviedo, strong away, will not simply sit back.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards. Córdoba ended a recent away game with nine men and Raúl has asked Oviedo for unconditional commitment, so the case for a high figure is there; I hold rather than go higher until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots, very high for this division. I lean lower: Oviedo's best away results have been compact ones (they led 2-0 at Cádiz and then held on), and Raúl's first weeks in charge are likely to put structure first, which caps the volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean slightly lower with the shots: Córdoba's crossing game produces many attempts, but headers from crosses often miss the target, and Oviedo's attack is without Chris Ramos (cruciate injury).

401882298.overall: Early view: Sporting, seventh, return to El Molinón after losing 1-2 to Valladolid there despite 20 shots, and should have Juan Otero back once his ban is served at Real Sociedad II. Las Palmas, under Albert Sánchez since late October per one report, have Jesé and Sandro Ramírez available. Both play in round 14 first.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Sporting's last four league games averaged three goals, and Las Palmas's last four had five, one, three and four. Sporting's home attack, with Otero back, should be stronger than it was against Valladolid.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean higher: Sporting had 63 per cent of the ball and 20 shots in their last home game, the kind of dominance that piles up corners, and Nicolás Larcamón's side should take a similar approach here.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. Las Palmas collect cards steadily (32 yellows and two reds in 12 games per LaLiga's figures), which the site already reflects, and this is not a derby or a high-risk fixture, so I see no reason to move it.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. I lean higher: Sporting took 20 on their own against Valladolid at El Molinón, and Las Palmas under their new coach have played open games (3-2 at Oviedo). A total in the high twenties is plausible.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target and I keep it. Sporting's volume has not turned into accuracy (one goal from 20 shots last time), so I do not follow the shots lean all the way.

401883109.overall: Early view: Girona, relegated from LaLiga last season, have lost two in a row 1-0 but still have the most attacking quality in the division (Vanat, Asprilla, Stuani, Carles Pérez). Eibar are fourth and play with less of the ball than anyone, per one report; their postponed game at Castellón still has to be rescheduled and could add a midweek fixture before this one.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean higher: Girona's home games have included a 5-1 against Celta Fortuna and a 2-0 against Andorra, and Eibar's last three away league games had two, four and four goals. Girona's finishing should recover after Vanat hit the post against Almería.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. I lean higher: Eibar concede possession by design, so Girona should spend long spells in their half, and Girona's wide players (Carles Pérez, Asprilla) give them the crossing and shooting that earn corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. Girona collected three first-half yellows against Almería and Jokin Aranbarri wants an aggressive Eibar, but Girona usually control home games, so I hold at the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, with 18.1 for Girona, which fits a home side facing a team that gives up the ball. Girona's recent shot counts were low (eight with ten men, 12 against Almería), but Eibar's style should give them more room, so I keep it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Girona's quality should turn volume into accuracy, but Eibar's deep defending forces efforts from distance, so I see no clear lean.

401883304.overall: Early view: Celta Fortuna, 16th, have a long injury list (five players named by one report) but should get Joel López, Enrique Ribes and Adrià Capdevila back once their yellow-card bans are served at Albacete. Valladolid have won two in a row under Fran Escribá but are without Juanmi Latasa, Guille Bueno, De Rooij and Dani Pérez, and Iván Alejo's fitness after limping off in Gijón is uncertain.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already high, and I stay there. Celta Fortuna's games have been open (4-1, 1-5, 2-2 and 1-2 in recent weeks) and Valladolid's last two had seven and three goals, but Valladolid's missing striker Latasa stops me going higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, with Valladolid expected to win more than the hosts. That fits a patched-up Celta Fortuna side spending time defending, and I see no news to change it.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. I lean higher: LaLiga's figures show Valladolid with 34 yellows and four reds in 13 games, one of the heavier records in the division, and three Celta Fortuna players have already reached five yellows. Two open sides tend to produce cards in transition.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots and I keep it. Celta Fortuna took 17 at home to Córdoba and Valladolid 15 at Gijón, both consistent with the site's split.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Valladolid's attack is without its main striker, and Celta Fortuna's 17 shots against Córdoba brought two goals, so their volume does not always mean accuracy.

401883111.overall: Early view: Burgos, third, are strong at El Plantío and Sergio Francisco wants control rather than an open game, though Jon Karrikaburu is out with a hamstring tear. Albacete have won three in a row under Joseba Etxeberria (they host Celta Fortuna first), but José Corpas should still be suspended here (a three-match ban, per one report) and Higinio Marín went off injured at Leganés.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Burgos's last three home league games ended 2-1, 1-1 and 1-0, and Francisco has said he does not want an end-to-end game. Albacete win with few chances and could be without Higinio Marín.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners and I keep it. Burgos should have more of the ball at home, but Albacete under Etxeberria press high rather than sit deep, so the territory should not be completely one-way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, low for this division. I lean higher: Albacete's high press commits fouls, Burgos describe themselves as the hardest-running team in the league, and Corpas's recent red shows Albacete's edge. Five or six looks more likely than four.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots. I lean lower: Albacete took only five shots against Sabadell and 12 at Leganés, and Burgos's controlled home games are not shot-heavy. The site's 10.3 for Albacete looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean lower in line with the shots and goals: Burgos's home wins have been narrow, and Albacete's goals have come from few efforts (both goals against Sabadell went in off opponents).

401883110.overall: Early view: Bottom club Ceuta (five points, 30 goals conceded) host leaders Almería in the last game of round 15. One report says Sergio Lobera returned to Ceuta as coach on 8 November, so this would be his second league game; Almería host Andorra first, and Marcos Luna, who limped off at Girona, should have served his yellow-card ban by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, with 1.4 for Ceuta. I lean lower: Ceuta have scored once in their last three league games and Almería's recent league games have been tight (1-0, 1-1, 2-2). Almería should be favourites, but a high-scoring game needs Ceuta to contribute more than they have been.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with 6.0 for Ceuta. I lean lower: the bottom side winning six corners at home to the leaders looks generous, even if Lobera wants Ceuta to keep the ball more. Almería's share should be higher and Ceuta's lower, with a slightly smaller total.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. A desperate home side against the leaders points up, but a new coach usually starts by demanding discipline, so I hold at the site's number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, with 18.9 for Ceuta. I lean lower: Ceuta have not shown that kind of volume (they failed to score at Córdoba or at home to Sporting), and Almería's games are more controlled, with 12 shots each at Girona.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. I lean lower with the shots: Ceuta's attack has been blunt and Almería's recent wins have been narrow. Miguel de la Fuente, the league's top scorer, is the likeliest source of efforts on target.

401882297.overall: Early view: Albacete have turned a dreadful start around under Joseba Etxeberria, who replaced Alberto González in early October, with three straight wins including 3-1 at Leganés, but they are still 21st. Tenerife have drawn four in a row and are dealing with the death of striker Jesús de Miguel after the 2 November match with Andorra. Corpas should be back from his three-match ban by round 16, and Dani Martín's ban should be served against Ceuta on 15 November, so the brief's absence list will likely be out of date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean slightly higher: Albacete have scored seven in their last three under Etxeberria's high-pressing, vertical set-up but still have the second-worst defence (24 conceded), and Tenerife's away games have averaged over three goals. Tenerife's run of 1-1 draws keeps me from going far above the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean a little lower: Álvaro Cervera's Tenerife are happy without the ball (26% possession and no corners against Andorra), and Etxeberria's Albacete attack fast in transition rather than camping in the final third, as at Leganés where they had five corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. I lean higher: Albacete picked up six yellows at Leganés with Etxeberria's aggressive pressing, and Tenerife had three yellows and Dani Martín's red against Andorra. A relegation-threatened home side chasing a fourth straight win adds to the fouling.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.8 shots. I lean lower: Tenerife produce very few shots (five against Andorra) and lean on Enric Gallego, who has scored around half their goals, while Albacete took only 12 at Leganés even in a 3-1 win.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.3 shots on target. I see nothing to move it: Albacete were efficient at Leganés (five on target from 12) and Tenerife put two of five on target against Andorra, which fits a total close to the site's number.

401883106.overall: Early view: Almería are top on 29 points after a 1-0 win at Girona and are unbeaten at home (five wins, one draw) under Xavi García Pimienta, with Miguel de la Fuente the division's top scorer. Sporting are seventh but lost 2-1 at home to Valladolid, had a long injury list before that game and saw Juan Otero sent off. Marcos Luna's yellow-card ban should be served against Andorra on 14 November, so he should be available here.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean lower: Sporting's away games have averaged about 2.3 goals and they have won four of six on the road by staying compact, and Almería's last two matches finished 1-1 and 1-0. Almería at home are the likelier scorers, but a big total needs Sporting to open up.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. I lean slightly lower: García Pimienta's Almería build through the middle and took only two corners at Girona and three at Eibar, and Sporting's nine corners against Valladolid came with 62% of the ball, which they are unlikely to have at the leaders' ground.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. Sporting were booked heavily and had Otero sent off against Valladolid, but that was a high-risk home game; Almería picked up three yellows at Girona and two at Eibar. That leaves me close to the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Recent games support it: Girona-Almería had 26 shots, Eibar-Almería 30 and Sporting-Valladolid 35, so a total in the high 20s looks right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Almería had only three on target at Girona and one at Eibar, and many of the shots in these teams' games end up blocked, so I would expect fewer than ten on target.

401883105.overall: Early view: Cádiz are 20th and on their third coach of the season, Borja Jiménez, who took over in late October; they won his debut against Ceuta but then lost 2-1 at Mallorca and 2-1 at home to Oviedo despite creating more. Córdoba are tenth under Iván Ania after a 3-0 win over Ceuta, though one preview listed five injured players. This Andalusian meeting carries real pressure for Cádiz, who have only two home wins.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Córdoba's games are open (22 scored and 22 conceded, and their away games average over three goals), while Cádiz's home games have averaged just over two; the two pull in different directions, so I stay near the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners. That looks right: Córdoba won 11 corners against Ceuta and attack wide, and Cádiz under Borja Jiménez pushed hard enough against Oviedo to win six, so both sides should contribute.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Cádiz-Oviedo produced nine yellows, Córdoba had Isma Ruiz sent off for two yellows and Alex banned for violent play after their trip to Celta Fortuna, and a regional game with Cádiz fighting relegation should be tense.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots. Cádiz took 15 against Oviedo and Córdoba 14 against Ceuta, and both teams commit players forward, so a total close to the site's number fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Cádiz got only four of their 15 shots on target against Oviedo, with six blocked, and their finishing has been the main problem all season.

401883104.overall: Early view: a top-four meeting, with Eibar fourth on 23 points from 12 games and Burgos third on 24 after a late 2-1 win over Celta Fortuna. One report (4 November) says Eibar lost both left-backs, Juan Bernat (torn hamstring) and Imanol García de Albéniz (torn calf), and have Unai Elgezabal out with an ankle sprain. Eibar also have a postponed league game at Castellón and a Copa tie to fit in, so the schedule could be tight by late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals. I lean higher: Eibar's home games have averaged nearly three goals, Burgos keep scoring late (Álex Forés in the 86th minute last time), and Eibar's patched-up back line without Bernat and García de Albéniz is a weakness.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. I lean higher: Burgos won 10 corners against Celta Fortuna under Sergio Francisco, and Eibar's makeshift full-backs could invite pressure down the flanks, while Eibar themselves had 20 shots and five corners against Almería.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. Eibar had three yellows against Almería and Burgos only one against Celta Fortuna; it is a big game at a tight ground, but neither side has been especially card-prone lately, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots. I lean higher: Eibar had 20 shots against Almería and Burgos 19 against Celta Fortuna, and both like to shoot from volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Eibar's volume has not turned into accuracy (four on target from 20, eight blocked, against Almería), while Burgos had six on target last time, so I stay close to the site's number.

401882296.overall: Early view: Eldense, coached by Javi Calleja since September, drew 0-0 at Las Palmas on Monday and have scored only 13 goals in 13 games. Girona are eighth under Quique Álvarez but have lost their last two 1-0 without scoring, to Real Sociedad B and Almería. Girona have the better side, but recent form points to a tight game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean lower: Eldense average about a goal a game, Girona have been shut out in their last two, and Girona's away games have averaged just over two goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Girona won seven corners against Almería and should have more of the ball here, while Eldense won only one at Las Palmas; together that fits the site's number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards. I lean higher: Eldense were booked six times and committed 21 fouls at Las Palmas, Justin Smith already reached five yellows earlier in the season, and Girona picked up five yellows against Almería.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.3 shots. I lean lower: Girona's club data show them averaging 10.6 shots a game and Eldense 9.9, and Eldense managed only six at Las Palmas.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Eldense put one shot on target at Las Palmas and Girona three against Almería, and neither attack is in good form.

401883103.overall: Early view: Granada have won five in a row under Pacheta and have a game in hand, after their match with Tenerife was postponed following Jesús de Miguel's death. Ceuta are bottom with 5 points, have lost five straight and have taken one point from six away games, conceding 18. The main question is how many Granada score.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Granada's winning run has been built on tight scores (1-0, 2-0, 2-1, 2-0), but Ceuta concede three a game away from home, so the two balance out near the site's number, with Granada doing most of the scoring.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. I lean higher: Córdoba won 11 corners against Ceuta last week, and Granada at home against the bottom side should spend long spells in Ceuta's half; their set pieces are a weapon too, as Rubén Alcaraz's header at Eldense showed.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards. I lean slightly lower: Ceuta took only two yellows in their 3-0 defeat at Córdoba, and one-sided games where the favourite controls the ball tend to produce fewer bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots. Ceuta are not passive (12 shots at Córdoba) but give a lot away, so a total in the high 20s fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: Córdoba-Ceuta had 12 shots on target, and Ceuta's defence (30 conceded, 18 of them in six away games) lets opponents get clean shots away.

401883101.overall: Early view: Las Palmas are on their third coach, Albert Sánchez, appointed on 29 October; he won 3-2 at Oviedo in his first game and then drew 0-0 with Eldense. Andorra are 18th and in an emotional position after their goalkeeper Jesús Owono was involved in the collision that killed Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel; their 8 November game with Mallorca was postponed at the club's request. The bans listed for Owono, Lautaro De León and Efe Akman should be served at Almería on 14 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Las Palmas' home games have averaged about two goals, and the 0-0 against Eldense showed a side still learning Sánchez's ideas. Andorra's away games are more open, which stops me going much lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. I lean lower: Las Palmas won only four corners against Eldense despite 61% possession, and Andorra under Carles Manso keep the ball (74% at Tenerife) but took just three corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. I lean higher: Andorra are among the most-booked sides in the division (40 yellows and two reds in 12 games), with Diego Alende, Marc Domènech and Akman all on five or more yellows.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.0 shots. I lean lower: Las Palmas took nine shots against Eldense and Andorra 11 at Tenerife even with most of the ball, so neither side generates big volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean lower: Las Palmas had three on target against Eldense and Andorra four at Tenerife.

401883102.overall: Early view: Leganés are 17th and have not won since Luis Carrión replaced Rubén Albés in October (a draw with Mallorca, then 4-3 and 3-1 defeats), and they concede a lot. Sabadell, back in professional football this season, are 12th with one of the league's tighter defences but score very little away from home. Javi Montero's red-card ban should be served against Burgos on 13 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals. Leganés' defence is leaky (23 conceded), but Sabadell have scored only four goals in seven away games and one preview said they have lost joint top scorer Nicholas Gioacchini to a cruciate ligament injury, so I stay close to the site's low number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Leganés under Carrión dominate the ball at home (63% and nine corners against Albacete), and Sabadell sit deep away, so most corners should come from the home side, with a total near the site's number.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. I lean higher: Leganés took five yellows and a straight red against Albacete, three of their players (Pulido, Kechta and Marvel) have already reached five yellows, and the relegation pressure on Carrión's side is growing.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots. The total looks fair, although I would expect most of the shots from Leganés (17 against Albacete) rather than Sabadell, whose away attack has been thin.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Leganés put seven on target against Albacete, with Álvaro Morata their main threat despite missing a penalty, and Sabadell create little, so I stay with the number.

401882295.overall: Early view: two of the best defences in the division meet, with Mallorca sixth (7 conceded, five wins from six at home) and Castellón second (5 conceded in 12, the best away record). Both had their round 13 game postponed after Jesús de Miguel's death; Castellón, his former club, asked for theirs to be called off, and Mallorca still have the Andorra game to fit in. Matías Orozco's ban should be served at Valladolid on 14 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals. I lean slightly lower: Castellón have conceded only five goals all season and four away, while Mallorca have let in three at home, so a 1-0 or 1-1 type of game looks most likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. I found nothing that points either way on corners for these two, so I stay with the site's number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. Mallorca are card-prone (36 yellows and a red in 12 games) and Castellón coach Pablo Hernández was furious with the referee after Orozco's red at Burgos, but the site's number already reflects a busy game for the referee.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.1 shots. Both teams can control games, Castellón with their 4-0 over Sporting and Mallorca at home, so a total in the mid 20s fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. I lean lower: both defences limit clear chances, and Castellón in particular rarely let opponents get shots on goal.

401883303.overall: Early view: Oviedo are ninth under Julián Calero after a 2-1 win at Cádiz, though they were outplayed on chances there, and one report said striker Chris Ramos tore a cruciate ligament in September. Celta Fortuna are 16th, lost 2-1 at Burgos with only one shot on target and have four players on five yellows; three of them should serve bans at Albacete on 16 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean lower: Oviedo's home games have averaged only two goals, and without Chris Ramos their attack relies on wide players such as Ilyas Chaira and Estanis. Celta Fortuna's defence is weak (25 conceded), so Oviedo should still score.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Celta Fortuna gave up 10 corners and won none at Burgos, which supports a high home share, so the total looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. I lean higher: Celta Fortuna had four yellows at Burgos and four players have reached five yellows already, and Oviedo took five yellows at Cádiz.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots, which looks too high. Oviedo took 12 shots at Cádiz and Celta Fortuna only six at Burgos, so I expect something in the mid 20s.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. I lean lower: Oviedo had four on target at Cádiz and Celta Fortuna one at Burgos, and Oviedo's striker shortage limits their output.

401883100.overall: Early view: Valladolid are 11th under Fran Escribá and won 2-1 at Sporting on Sunday, their first away win of the season, though one preview listed Juanmi Latasa, Guille Bueno, De Rooij and Dani Pérez as injured. Real Sociedad B are 19th and were playing at Sabadell on Monday night. Iván Alejo's yellow-card ban should be served against Castellón on 14 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean higher: Valladolid's home games have averaged over four goals (5-0, 2-3 and 4-3 among them), and Real Sociedad B's away games average around three and a half.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners. Valladolid won six corners at Sporting with only 38% of the ball and should have more of it at home, so I see no reason to move from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. Valladolid were booked three times at Sporting and I found nothing unusual about Real Sociedad B's discipline, so I stay with the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.0 shots. Valladolid took 15 shots at Sporting even with little of the ball, and Real Sociedad B play open games, so a total around 30 is reasonable.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: Valladolid put six of 15 on target at Sporting, and their home matches have been high-scoring.

401882293.overall: Early view: Burgos are third and have the best home record in the division by points (five wins, two draws, one defeat), with Sergio Francisco's side winning several games late. Cádiz are 20th and have not won away all season (two draws, three defeats), although Borja Jiménez's side created plenty in the 2-1 home defeat to Oviedo.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly higher: Burgos' home games have averaged 2.6 goals and Cádiz's away games over three, and Cádiz are creating more chances under their new coach.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. I lean higher: Burgos won 10 corners against Celta Fortuna at El Plantío and push a lot of players into the box, and Cádiz will spend long spells defending.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. Burgos had one yellow against Celta Fortuna and Cádiz four against Oviedo; nothing points clearly away from the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. I lean slightly higher: Burgos took 19 shots at home last time, and Cádiz had 15 against Oviedo, even if they will shoot less away.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.3 shots on target. Burgos had six on target against Celta Fortuna and Cádiz four against Oviedo, which fits the number.

401883099.overall: Early view: second against first. Castellón have conceded one goal in five home games under Pablo Hernández and have a game in hand, while leaders Almería have not lost in the league since their first two games under García Pimienta. Both sides' current bans (Orozco, Marcos Luna) should be served in round 14, and Castellón may also have their postponed home game with Eibar rescheduled around this date.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, which looks high. I lean lower: Castellón's home record is 12 scored and only one conceded, Almería's away games have averaged two goals, and top-of-the-table meetings tend to be cautious.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Almería take few corners away (two at Girona, three at Eibar) but Castellón at home should make up for that, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards. The stakes are high and Castellón were angry about refereeing at Burgos, but Almería have been disciplined in recent away games (two or three yellows), so I stay near the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots. Almería's recent away games had 26 and 30 shots in total, and Castellón create plenty at home, so the number looks reasonable.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. I lean lower: Castellón allow almost nothing at home, and Almería put only three on target at Girona and one at Eibar.

401882291.overall: Early view: Sabadell are unbeaten at home (three wins, two draws) and built on defence, but one preview said they lost joint top scorer Nicholas Gioacchini to a cruciate ligament injury. Eibar are fourth with a good away record (four wins in six) but, according to one report, are without both left-backs, and they have a postponed league game and a Copa tie to fit in.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals. I lean higher: Sabadell's home games have averaged 2.4 goals and Eibar's away games three, and Eibar's defensive injuries make a very low total less likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Eibar won five corners and took 20 shots against Almería, and Sabadell are strong at home; I found nothing that clearly moves the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards. Sabadell have already had Édgar González and Óscar Sanz banned for five yellows, which shows a combative side, but that is in line with the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with 19 for Sabadell. I lean lower: Sabadell have scored only 12 goals all season and, without Gioacchini, are unlikely to shoot that often even at home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Eibar's shooting has been inaccurate (four on target from 20 against Almería) and Sabadell's attack is thin.

401882292.overall: Early view: a bottom-of-the-table game between Ceuta (22nd, 5 points, five straight defeats) and Albacete (21st), who have won three in a row under Joseba Etxeberria. Corpas should be back for Albacete after his three-match ban, and a win for either side would matter a lot in the relegation fight.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Ceuta's home games average about 2.6 and Albacete's away games three, but relegation six-pointers are often tense, so I stay with the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Ceuta won five corners even in a 3-0 defeat at Córdoba and should push at home, while Albacete prefer quick transitions; I see no clear reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. I lean higher: Albacete picked up six yellows at Leganés with Etxeberria's pressing, Ceuta's Carlos Hernández is on four yellows, and a game between the bottom two should be fiercely contested.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, with 19 for Ceuta. I lean lower: Ceuta took 12 shots at Córdoba and have scored only six goals at home, and Albacete took 12 in their win at Leganés.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with the lower shot count, although Albacete have been efficient (five on target from 12 at Leganés).

401883098.overall: Early view: Córdoba are tenth under Iván Ania and strong at home (four wins in six), most recently 3-0 against Ceuta with two goals from Diego Percan. Las Palmas are 13th under Albert Sánchez, their third coach of the season, and their away games have been very open (24 goals in six).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean higher: Las Palmas' away games have averaged four goals and Córdoba's home games over three, and both defences have conceded more than 20.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Córdoba won 11 corners against Ceuta and attack wide at home, while Las Palmas won only four against Eldense, so most corners should go to Córdoba with a total near the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards. Córdoba had a second-yellow red and a violent-conduct ban after their game at Celta Fortuna, but only three yellows against Ceuta, so I stay with the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots. Córdoba took 14 against Ceuta and Las Palmas' open away games add volume, so the number looks fair.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target. I lean slightly higher, in line with my goals view: Córdoba had seven on target against Ceuta and Las Palmas concede plenty away.

401882294.overall: Early view: Andorra are 18th and still have their postponed home game with Mallorca to play; how the squad, and goalkeeper Jesús Owono in particular, recover from the death of Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel is hard to judge from here. Oviedo are ninth and have a good away record (four wins in seven) under Julián Calero. The bans in the brief for Owono, De León and Akman should be served at Almería on 14 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean higher: Andorra's home games have averaged three and a half goals and Oviedo's away games over three, with both defences conceding regularly.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. Andorra keep the ball (74% possession at Tenerife) but did not turn it into many corners, and I found nothing else to move the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Andorra are among the most-booked teams in the division (40 yellows and two reds in 12 games), and Oviedo took five yellows at Cádiz, with Carlos D. already on five.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots. I lean lower: Andorra took only 11 shots at Tenerife despite dominating the ball, and Oviedo had 12 at Cádiz.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With open games on both sides but modest shot volume, I stay near the site's number.

401883097.overall: Early view: Girona are eighth under Quique Álvarez and strong at home (16 scored, 7 conceded), but they have lost their last two without scoring. Valladolid are 11th and just won their first away game of the season at Sporting, though one preview listed several injuries, including striker Juanmi Latasa. Iván Alejo's ban should be served in round 14.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Girona's home games average nearly three goals but their attack has stalled lately, and Valladolid's away games average about 2.4, so I stay close to the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. I lean higher: Girona won seven corners against Almería, and Valladolid are happy to defend deep away (38% possession at Sporting).

cards.text: The numbers say 6.1 cards. Girona took five yellows against Almería and Valladolid three at Sporting, which fits the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.7 shots. Girona took 14 against Almería and Valladolid 15 at Sporting, so the number looks right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Girona managed only three on target against Almería and have not scored in two games.

401883302.overall: Early view: Celta Fortuna are 16th and their home games are open (13 scored, 13 conceded in seven), while Mallorca are sixth under Luis García and very tight away (seven goals in six away games, four of them draws). Celta Fortuna's squad also depends on what the Celta first team needs, and one preview listed four injured players.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean slightly lower: Mallorca's away games have averaged just over one goal, and they should control this game, even though Celta Fortuna's home matches are usually open.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. I found nothing that points clearly either way, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Mallorca average three yellows a game (36 in 12), and Celta Fortuna have four players who reached five yellows, so both sides pick up plenty of bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. I lean slightly lower: Mallorca's away games are slow and controlled, and Celta Fortuna managed only six shots at Burgos.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean lower: Celta Fortuna had one on target at Burgos, and Mallorca's away games rarely produce many clear chances.

401883096.overall: Early view: a relegation game between Real Sociedad B (19th, 11 points) and Leganés (17th, 12 points), who have not won since Luis Carrión took over in October. Leganés have a poor away record (five scored, 14 conceded in seven). Javi Montero's red-card ban should be served long before this one.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leganés concede two a game away, and Real Sociedad B's recent matches have been open (1-4, 2-4 and 2-3 among them).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I found nothing that points clearly either way, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.5 cards, already a high figure. Leganés are card-prone (five yellows and a red against Albacete, three players on five yellows), which supports the number rather than pushing it higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, with 16.9 for Real Sociedad B. I lean lower: the reserve side have scored only six goals in six home games, so that home share looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower, mainly because Real Sociedad B's home attack has been weak.

401882290.overall: Early view: Sporting are seventh under Nicolás Larcamón but lost 2-1 at home to Valladolid, had a long injury list before that game, and an earlier report said the board was backing him despite concern about the start of the season. Granada have won five in a row under Pacheta and have a good away record (four wins in seven). Juan Otero's red-card ban should be served by this date unless it is a long one.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Sporting's home games have averaged about two goals and Granada's away games nearly three, which averages out close to the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. I lean slightly higher: Sporting won nine corners against Valladolid with 62% of the ball, and Granada are happy to sit back away and look for set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. I lean higher: Sporting had four or five yellows and a straight red against Valladolid at El Molinón, and they will be under pressure to respond against a team in form.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. Sporting took 20 against Valladolid, while Granada won at Eldense with only eight, so the total looks about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Granada win games with few shots on goal, and Sporting put six on target against Valladolid.

401883095.overall: Early view: Tenerife are still playing in the shadow of striker Jesús de Miguel's death after the 2 November match with Andorra; Álvaro Cervera's side have drawn four in a row and their home games have been low-scoring. Eldense, under Javi Calleja, drew 0-0 at Las Palmas on Monday and have scored only four goals in seven away games. Dani Martín's ban should be served against Ceuta on 15 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean lower: Tenerife's home games have averaged two goals and Eldense's away games under two, with the 0-0 at Las Palmas the latest example.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. I lean lower: Tenerife won no corners against Andorra and Eldense only one at Las Palmas, and neither side keeps the ball for long spells in the final third.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. I lean higher: Eldense picked up six yellows and committed 21 fouls at Las Palmas, and Tenerife had three yellows and a red against Andorra.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.4 shots. I lean lower: Tenerife took five shots against Andorra and Eldense six at Las Palmas, so neither side produces much volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Tenerife had two on target against Andorra and Eldense one at Las Palmas.

401933535.overall: Early view: a one-off Eastern Conference Wild Card, No. 8 Orlando against No. 9 Cincinnati, with a draw after 90 minutes going straight to penalties and the winner meeting Supporters' Shield winners Nashville in a best-of-three. Orlando lean on Antoine Griezmann (14 goals and 8 assists in 18 games, October/November Player of the Month) but have Robin Jansson out after foot surgery, Tyrese Spicer out with a foot injury at the last check, and six players away this week, including Braian Ojeda in Japan on 17 November and Maxime Crepeau and Justin Ellis playing on 16 and 17 November. Cincinnati have conceded 75 goals, are short at centre-back (Hagglund concussion, Malatini leg, Hadebe off injured against Nashville), and Kevin Denkey plays for Togo in Lome on 17 November; the season series was a 6-2 Cincinnati win in May and a 1-1 draw in Orlando in August with Griezmann playing.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, built on two defences that leak: Cincinnati conceded 75, the third-most in MLS, and the August meeting in Orlando still ended only 1-1. I lean a little lower because a single knockout game with no extra time usually starts cagey, Orlando's last two games produced five goals in total (0-4 at Charlotte, 1-0 against New England), and Orlando lose Spicer's pace while Denkey and Ojeda arrive back from long trips two days before kick-off. Over 2.5 still looks right; four or more needs an early goal to open it up.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners, split almost evenly. Cincinnati's 3-4-1-2 pushes both wing-backs high and Orlando will attack the space behind them, which fits a normal count rather than a big swing either way. Nothing in this week's news moves it, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and lean under 4.5, but I lean higher. Cincinnati picked up five yellows in the Decision Day loss to Nashville (Nwobodo, Evander, Gidi, Smith and Bucha), Evander and Miazga were both booked in the August draw in Orlando, and Crepeau was booked for time wasting against New England. Win-or-go-home stakes, tired legs after the international break and a likely chase late on add to it.

shots.text: The site expects 29 shots, which is a lot for a knockout game. I lean lower: Orlando are without Spicer and will have several players back from national-team trips only a day or two before, and Cincinnati's patched-up centre-back group may make Pat Noonan less willing to throw both wing-backs forward from the start.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. I lean lower, in line with the goals: Orlando scored once in their last two games, and I expect fewer clear chances in a tight one-off game with travel-weary players on both sides. Griezmann, Denkey and Evander can still test Crepeau and Roman Celentano, so around nine looks fair.

401933555.overall: Early view: a winner-take-all Wild Card at Lumen Field, with the winner facing top seed Vancouver; a draw after 90 minutes goes straight to penalties. Seattle squeezed in with a 2-1 win over LAFC despite being outshot 24-5, and are without Pedro de la Vega, Yeimar Gomez Andrade and Nikola Petkovic, with Jordan Morris worth watching after he went off after 24 minutes on Decision Day. Real Salt Lake went 5-2-1 down the stretch and have Sergi Solans (15 goals); the site lists JuanMa Sanabria as banned after his Decision Day yellow, which I could not confirm in club or league reports.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean a little lower: Pablo Mastroeni set Real Salt Lake up in a 5-4-1 on Decision Day, Seattle's attack is thinner without de la Vega and possibly Morris, and the last playoff meeting between these two, in 2021, finished 0-0. RSL have scored in eight straight league games, so a 1-1 or 2-0 fits better than a shootout.

corners.text: The site expects 11.1 corners, with 6.4 for Seattle. I lean lower: Seattle won just two corners against LAFC and played on the break, and with de la Vega out and Morris a doubt they have fewer wide runners to win them. RSL took six against the Galaxy, so I see something nearer nine than eleven.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and lean under 4.5. I lean higher: RSL were booked four times in their must-win game against the Galaxy (Henry, Sanabria, de Fougerolles, Solans) and Seattle collected three late yellows protecting their lead over LAFC. A knockout game between old playoff rivals should carry at least that much edge.

shots.text: The site expects 29.3 shots, roughly even. I lean lower because neither side has been a high-volume team lately: Seattle had five shots against LAFC and relied on Andrew Thomas's saves, and RSL's back five is built to limit chances. RSL did take 20 shots against a Galaxy side chasing the game, so this depends on who scores first.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with fewer shots overall: Seattle put three on target on Decision Day, and a cautious RSL away from home is unlikely to repeat the nine they managed against the Galaxy in Utah.

401933733.overall: Early view: Game 1 of a best-of-three, with No. 3 New England hosting No. 6 Philadelphia; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. Marko Mitrovic's Revolution won both league meetings 2-1 but finished with two straight defeats, and Dor Turgeman (12 goals) and Ilay Feingold play for Israel in Hungary on 17 November, four days before kick-off. Philadelphia, under interim coach Ryan Richter according to MLSsoccer.com, ended a four-game winless run with a 4-1 win over Toronto led by Cavan and Quinn Sullivan.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean a little lower: both meetings this season finished 2-1, New England scored once in their last two games, and Turgeman and Feingold will have had little time to recover from the Israel trip. Matt Turner, who played every minute of the season, gives New England a reliable last line in what should be a careful opener.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners, slightly more for Philadelphia. I found nothing on either side's set pieces or wide play that moves this, and Carles Gil's delivery keeps New England dangerous from dead balls, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. There is playoff history here (New England won in 2020, Philadelphia in 2023, both in Round One), but I found nothing on discipline or the referee that pushes it either way, so I stay close to the number.

shots.text: The site expects 26.4 shots with Philadelphia taking 16.9 of them, which looks heavy for an away team. Philadelphia did fire 19 at Toronto, but New England beat them twice this season and will not sit back at home in Game 1; I see a more even split and a slightly lower total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Turner made 140 saves this season, the second most in MLS, so New England do allow shots on goal, while Philadelphia's front line of Damiani and the Sullivans was sharp against Toronto. That supports the number, so I stay with it.

401933732.overall: Early view: No. 2 FC Dallas host No. 7 Portland in Game 1, with a draw after 90 minutes going to penalties. Eric Quill's Dallas scored a club-record 62 goals and came from behind to beat Colorado 3-1 on Decision Day, while Marti Cifuentes's Portland arrive on four straight wins but conceded 61 in the season. Portland won 2-1 in Frisco in September and the teams drew 2-2 in Portland.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals and I lean slightly higher. Both meetings this season produced goals (2-2, then a 2-1 Portland win in Frisco), Dallas have Petar Musa, who had 22 goals by late October, and Portland concede freely even while winning. A playoff opener can start slowly, but these two attacks are the stronger units on the pitch.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners split evenly. I found no team news or style notes that point either way for corners, so I stay with the number; ten is a fair middle for two attacking teams.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, under 4.5. Portland knocked Dallas out of the playoffs in 2015 and 2018 and Dallas won the 2020 meeting, so there is some history, but I found nothing on discipline or the referee that pushes this either way.

shots.text: The site expects 25.4 shots, with only 11.1 for Portland. I lean higher: Portland out-created Charlotte by a wide margin in late October and have scored freely during their four-game winning run, and Dallas at home with Musa and Joaquin Valiente (13 assists) should keep their own volume up.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. I lean slightly higher in line with the goals: Portland's defence lets opponents get shots away, and Dallas's 62-goal attack is efficient, so I expect both keepers, including Portland's James Pantemis, to be busy.

401933739.overall: Early view: No. 2 Inter Miami host No. 7 Columbus in Game 1 at Nu Stadium; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties.
