Miami scored 80 league goals and Messi won a second straight Golden Boot, but under Kily Gonzalez they threw away a 3-0 lead against Charlotte on Decision Day, and MLSsoccer.com notes their home record is worse than their away one. Columbus, under interim coach Laurent Courtois, won eight of their last nine (24 goals for, 10 against) and came from behind three times to win 4-3 in Chicago.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals, which is very high, but the news backs it. Miami's last game finished 3-3 and Columbus's 4-3, Miami have the league's most productive attack with Messi and Suarez not called up in November, and Columbus have scored 24 in nine. I stay with the number rather than going higher because playoff openers usually start tighter.

corners.text: The site expects 8.4 corners and I lean lower. Miami won only two corners against Charlotte despite having most of the ball (and scored from both), because they build through Messi and De Paul in the middle rather than crossing; Columbus took four in Chicago. A low count fits both.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, most of them on Miami. Miami committed 14 fouls against Charlotte and Columbus had Tapia and Rodriguez booked in Chicago, which fits the number; with no referee named yet I stay close to it.

shots.text: The site expects 27.3 shots. I lean lower: both teams are efficient rather than high-volume, with Miami scoring three from 11 shots against Charlotte and Columbus four from 11 in Chicago. I expect quality chances rather than a flood of attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Fewer shots does not mean fewer on target here: both Decision Day games had a high share on goal, and Messi, Suarez, Tapia and Brais Mendez rarely waste chances, so I stay with the number.

401933730.overall: Early view: No. 4 Chicago host No. 5 Charlotte in Game 1, their first playoff meeting; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. Gregg Berhalter's Fire scored 65 goals but conceded four at home to Columbus on Decision Day and are missing Sam Rogers, Robin Lod and Mauricio Pineda (all lower-body injuries). Charlotte arrive in form with two 4-0 wins and a comeback from 3-0 down to draw 3-3 at Inter Miami, and Allan Saint-Maximin should be back after the red-card ban that kept him out of that game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals and I lean higher. Chicago's last game finished 3-4 without centre-back Sam Rogers, and Charlotte have scored 11 in their last three, with Pep Biel (13 goals, 17 assists) and Liel Abada in form. MLSsoccer.com has pointed to Charlotte's more open style, so both sides scoring looks likely.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners, most for Chicago. Chicago took six against Columbus and Charlotte only one at Miami, which matches the site's split, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Chicago were booked three times against Columbus, while Charlotte committed only six fouls at Miami; Saint-Maximin's recent red card is a reminder of his temper but not a pattern for the team. I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The site expects 30.7 shots with almost 21 for Chicago, which looks too high. Chicago had 14 shots against Columbus and are without midfielders Lod and Pineda, and Charlotte score from few chances (three goals from nine shots at Miami). I expect a high-scoring but not shot-heavy game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 on target. Chicago put six of 14 on goal against Columbus and Charlotte forced six saves while scoring three at Miami, so a high on-target count fits even with fewer total shots; I stay with the number.

401933728.overall: Early view: No. 3 St. Louis host No. 6 LAFC in Game 1; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. St. Louis won the US Open Cup and set a 21-game unbeaten record under first-year coach Yoann Damet, but then lost four straight before a stoppage-time 1-0 win at Houston in which they were outshot 23-13. LAFC are under interim coach Xavi Tamarit after Marc Dos Santos left in late September, scored a club-low 52 league goals, went 3-7-7 on the road and are without Hugo Lloris, Aaron Long and Timothy Tillman.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and I lean lower. LAFC scored the fewest league goals in their history and managed one goal from 24 shots at Seattle, while St. Louis had one shot on target at Houston and scored little during their four-game losing run. Denis Bouanga (18 goals) and Son Heung-min are the main threat, but a 1-0 or 1-1 fits better.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners. I lean higher: LAFC won 12 corners at Seattle while dominating the ball, and St. Louis conceded nine to Houston on Decision Day while defending. If LAFC have long spells of possession again, the count should climb.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. St. Louis committed 13 fouls at Houston without a booking, and Sergi Palencia, booked at Seattle, is listed by the site as banned; I could not confirm whether regular-season yellows carry into the playoffs. Nothing else points either way, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 29.4 shots, with 17.1 for LAFC. I lean higher: LAFC took 24 at Seattle and Houston took 23 against St. Louis, so St. Louis are currently allowing a lot of attempts, and the hosts will have to push forward at home too.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 on target. LAFC put eight of 24 on goal at Seattle and St. Louis one of 13 at Houston, so volume is not turning into accuracy for either side; I stay close to the number despite expecting more shots.

401933738.overall: Early view: No. 4 San Jose host No. 5 Houston in Game 1, the first home playoff game at PayPal Park; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. Bruce Arena's Quakes (57 goals for, 51 against) lost 3-1 at Minnesota on Decision Day, with Timo Werner still working back to full fitness and Niko Tsakiris (13 assists) away with the US under-23s in Spain until 17 November. Ben Olsen's Houston have faded but have Jonathan Bond (12 clean sheets) and Guilherme (16 goals, 10 assists), and the two league meetings ended 0-0 and 1-0 to San Jose.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean lower. The two meetings this season produced one goal in total, Houston scored and conceded only 43 in 34 games, and Bond kept 12 clean sheets. Preston Judd (17 goals) is San Jose's main threat, but a tight game fits this pairing.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners, most for San Jose. San Jose won only two at Minnesota while Houston won nine against St. Louis, which argues against the split more than the total, and San Jose's centre-backs Munie and Roberts scoring nine between them shows they make dead balls count. I stay with the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. San Jose were booked three times at Minnesota and Houston once against St. Louis; with no referee named and no history of bad blood between these two, I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 26.9 shots with 16.1 for San Jose. I lean lower: San Jose had eight shots at Minnesota, Werner is short of full fitness and Tsakiris returns from Spain a week before the game, while Houston's season (43 scored, 43 conceded) points to few clear chances.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target and I lean lower, in line with the goals. Houston put only six of 23 shots on target at home to St. Louis and San Jose three at Minnesota, so accuracy has been a problem for both.

401933727.overall: Early view: Game 2 in Columbus on Friday 27 November, six days after Game 1; if Miami win in Florida, Columbus must win to force a decider, and a draw goes to penalties. Columbus won eight of their last nine league games under interim coach Laurent Courtois, though Miami had gone eight regular-season meetings without losing to Columbus as of late September. This view will change a lot with the Game 1 result.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Both sides are scoring freely (Columbus 24 in their last nine, Miami 80 for the season) and a team behind in the series has to open up, which supports a high number; I stay close to it but would not go higher until I see how Game 1 plays out.

corners.text: The site expects 8.3 corners. I lean lower for the same reason as in Game 1: Miami build through Messi and De Paul in the middle and won only two corners against Charlotte, and Columbus took four in Chicago. A home crowd may push Columbus wider, but not by much.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean a little higher: a second meeting in six days carries more edge, especially if Columbus are facing elimination at home, and Miami committed 14 fouls against Charlotte in their last game.

shots.text: The site expects 26.0 shots. Both teams have been efficient rather than shot-heavy (each took 11 shots on Decision Day and scored three or four), so I lean slightly lower, though a Columbus side chasing the series could push the count up late.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Gonzalo Tapia and Brais Mendez have been finishing well for Columbus and Miami's attack is the league's best, so I see no reason to move away from the number.

401933737.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Bank of America Stadium on Saturday 28 November (12:30 pm ET); if Chicago win Game 1, Charlotte must win to force a decider, and a draw goes to penalties. Charlotte beat Orlando 4-0 at home in late October and have Pep Biel (13 goals, 17 assists) and a returning Allan Saint-Maximin, while Chicago are without Rogers, Lod and Pineda. The view will be updated after Game 1.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. Charlotte's home form (4-0 against Orlando) and Chicago's leaky Decision Day defence support a high number, and whichever side trails the series will have to attack; I stay with the number until Game 1 is played.

corners.text: The site expects 10 corners, split evenly. Charlotte at home should take more than the single corner they had at Miami, while Chicago took six against Columbus; that evens out close to the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards and lean over 3.5. I lean a little higher for the second meeting in six days, with Saint-Maximin back from a red-card ban and Chicago booked three times in their last game; a close series usually gets more physical in Game 2.

shots.text: The site expects 28.6 shots, with 16.6 for Chicago away. That looks high for a Chicago side that had 14 at home to Columbus and is missing Lod and Pineda in midfield, so I lean lower overall.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 on target. Both sides have been hitting the target often (Chicago six of 14 against Columbus, Charlotte forcing six saves and scoring three at Miami), so I stay with the number.

401933724.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Shell Energy Stadium on Saturday 28 November (1:30 pm local), four days after Game 1 in San Jose; a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. Houston's home league games were low-scoring (19 scored, 15 conceded in 17) and the August meeting here ended 0-0. Guilherme is Houston's main outlet, while San Jose rely on Preston Judd and their goal-scoring centre-backs.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I lean lower. Houston's home games this season averaged about two goals in total, the August meeting here was 0-0, and Jonathan Bond tied the club record with 12 clean sheets.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners. I lean higher: Houston won nine corners at home to St. Louis while pressing for a goal, and San Jose conceded eight at Minnesota, so a Houston side at home should win plenty.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. There is little history of bad blood between these two, Houston were booked once on Decision Day and San Jose three times, so I stay with the number until the referee is named.

shots.text: The site expects 25.8 shots. Houston took 23 shots at home to St. Louis, so their home volume is real even when the goals do not come, and I lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 on target and I lean lower. Houston put only six of those 23 shots on target against St. Louis and San Jose managed three at Minnesota, so accuracy rather than volume is the problem for both.

401933723.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Subaru Park on Saturday 28 November (4:30 pm ET); if New England win Game 1, Philadelphia must win to force a decider, and a draw goes to penalties. New England won 2-1 at Subaru Park on 24 October, ending Philadelphia's 15-match unbeaten run, so the site's strong home lean for Philadelphia rests on their wider form more than on this matchup. The view will be refreshed after Game 1.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Both league meetings ended 2-1 and Philadelphia scored four against Toronto in their last home game, which fits a total around three; I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10.6 corners, heavily for Philadelphia. Philadelphia at home should have more of the ball, but New England won there in October; I found nothing that moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean slightly higher for Game 2: the teams will have met twice in a week, one of them may be facing elimination, and Philadelphia's Jovan Lukic and Ben Bender were both booked against Toronto.

shots.text: The site expects 29.6 shots, with 21.1 for Philadelphia. That is a lot against a New England side that beat them at Subaru Park a month earlier; Philadelphia did take 19 against Toronto, but I lean lower on the total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 on target. Matt Turner made the second-most saves in MLS this season, so New England do let shots reach goal, and the Sullivans and Bruno Damiani were sharp against Toronto; I stay with the number.

401933726.overall: Early view: Game 2 at BMO Stadium on Saturday 28 November (5:30 pm PT), five days after Game 1; a draw goes to penalties. LAFC have struggled to turn pressure into goals under interim coach Xavi Tamarit (nine goals in six games since 1 October), while St. Louis were outshot 23-13 in their last league game. The site lists Sergi Palencia as banned, but a one-match ban would cover Game 1 only.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, with LAFC expected to score 1.8. LAFC are much stronger at home (9-4-4 against 3-7-7 away), but they still scored a club-low 52 in the league and nine in six games under Tamarit, so I lean a little lower.

corners.text: The site expects 11.0 corners with 7.2 for LAFC. I lean higher: LAFC won 12 corners at Seattle when they had most of the ball, and at home against a St. Louis side that conceded nine at Houston they should pin the visitors back for long spells.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. Palencia should be available again if his ban covers only Game 1, and I found nothing else on discipline or the referee, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 31.9 shots, with LAFC taking almost 22. That is very high, but LAFC took 24 at Seattle and St. Louis allowed 23 at Houston, so the number has support; I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. I lean slightly lower because LAFC's volume has not turned into accuracy (eight of 24 on target at Seattle) and St. Louis had one shot on target in their last game.

401933721.overall: Early view: Game 2 at Providence Park on Saturday 28 November (7:30 pm PT), a week after Game 1 in Frisco; a draw goes to penalties. Portland drew 2-2 with Dallas here in the regular season and won four in a row to finish under Marti Cifuentes, while Dallas scored a club-record 62 goals. If Dallas win Game 1, Portland must win to force a decider, which should open the game up.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals and I lean slightly higher. The league meeting here finished 2-2, Portland conceded 61 goals in the season even while scoring freely, and Dallas have Musa, Valiente and Kaick after scoring three against Colorado.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners, more for Portland at home. I found nothing on either team's wide play or set pieces that moves this, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. There is playoff history between these clubs (three series since 2015), but I found no recent discipline news or referee information, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 25.7 shots. Portland have been creating a lot during their winning run (they out-created Charlotte by a wide margin in October) and Dallas attack well, so I lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 on target. I lean slightly higher with the goals: both defences have conceded plenty and both attacks have scorers in form, Ariel Lassiter and Kristoffer Velde for Portland and Kaick for Dallas.

401933718.overall: Early view: a Game 3 at SeatGeek Stadium on Wednesday 2 December, only played if the series is level at 1-1; kick-off time is still to be set and a draw after 90 minutes goes to penalties. It would be the third meeting in ten days, four days after Game 2 in Charlotte, with Chicago likely still without Rogers, Lod and Pineda. This view is very provisional and will be rebuilt from the first two games.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, the same as Game 1. I lean a little lower for a winner-take-all third game: the teams will know each other well after two meetings, legs will be heavy four days after Game 2, and a conference semifinal place tends to make both sides careful until someone scores.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners with most for Chicago at home. A deciding game could see Chicago push more, but I have nothing specific to go on, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher for a third meeting in ten days with elimination on the line; Chicago were booked three times in their last league game and Saint-Maximin was sent off at Orlando in October.

shots.text: The site expects 30.7 shots, with almost 21 for Chicago. Even in a decider that looks high for a Chicago side without Lod and Pineda that had 14 shots against Columbus, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 on target. I lean slightly lower for a tense decider where defences are likely to sit deeper, though both attacks have been accurate recently.

401933716.overall: Early view: Game 3 at Toyota Stadium on Wednesday 2 December, only played if the series is 1-1, with the kick-off time still to be set; a draw goes to penalties. Portland would face a long trip from Providence Park four days after Game 2, which helps Dallas. These two drew 2-2 and Portland won 2-1 in Frisco in the regular season.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. These are two of the West's more open teams, which pushes the total up, but a decider after a long trip for Portland, in the third meeting in under two weeks, tends to slow things down; the two effects roughly cancel, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners. Without news on wide players or set pieces I stay with the number, though Dallas pressing at home for the series could push it slightly up.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards and lean under 4.5. I lean higher for a third game in under two weeks with a conference semifinal at stake; tired legs late on and frustration carried over from the first two games tend to bring more fouls.

shots.text: The site expects 25.4 shots. I leaned higher for Game 1 because of Portland's attacking form, but their travel and short rest before a decider in Texas should take some energy out of their game, so I stay with the number here.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. Musa for Dallas and Lassiter and Velde for Portland keep the quality high, but a cautious decider should not push it higher, so I stay with the number.

401933720.overall: Early view: Game 3 at Nu Stadium on 1 or 2 December (Columbus list either date), only played if the series is 1-1, with kick-off still to be set; a draw goes to penalties. Columbus would travel south five days after hosting Game 2, and Miami's home record has been weaker than their away record this season according to MLSsoccer.com. This view will be rebuilt from the first two games.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals. A winner-take-all third game is usually tighter than the openers, and two coaches, Kily Gonzalez and Laurent Courtois, who have just faced each other twice will plan more carefully, so I lean slightly lower while still expecting goals from Messi and Suarez.

corners.text: The site expects 8.4 corners. As in the earlier games, Miami's central build-up produces few corners (two against Charlotte), so I lean a little lower.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. A third meeting in 11 days with elimination at stake should carry more fouls and bookings than the series opener; Miami committed 14 fouls against Charlotte, and Columbus had two players booked in their 4-3 win in Chicago.

shots.text: The site expects 27.3 shots. Both teams have been efficient rather than shot-heavy, and a decider should be more guarded, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target. I stay close to it: fewer shots in total, but Messi, Suarez, Tapia and Mendez all finish well, so the share on target should stay high.

401933719.overall: Early view: Game 3 at Gillette Stadium on Wednesday 2 December, only played if the series is 1-1; kick-off is still to be set and a draw goes to penalties. New England won both league meetings 2-1, but Philadelphia knocked them out in Round One in 2023. It is a short trip for Philadelphia, but both sides would be four days on from Game 2.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower for a decider between teams that will have met twice in 11 days: both league games were tight 2-1s, Matt Turner has been a constant in goal for New England, and neither side will want to chase the game early.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners. I found nothing on either side's set pieces or wide play that moves the total, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean higher for a winner-take-all third game between clubs with recent playoff history; by then both sides will carry plenty of grievances from the first two meetings.

shots.text: The site expects 26.4 shots, with 16.9 for Philadelphia away. In a decider at Gillette I expect fewer shots and a more even split, as I did for Game 1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. A cagey decider usually means fewer clear chances, so I lean slightly lower, even though Turner faced a lot of shots on target during the season.

401933715.overall: Early view: Game 3 at PayPal Park on Wednesday 2 December, only played if the series is 1-1, with kick-off still to be set; a draw goes to penalties. Houston would fly back to California four days after hosting Game 2. The two league meetings ended 0-0 and 1-0, and both clubs' seasons point to tight games.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean lower: these teams produced one goal in two league meetings, Houston's defence and Bond's 12 clean sheets are their strength, and a decider between two careful sides rarely opens up early.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners with most for San Jose. In a decider San Jose at home should have more of the ball and the corners that come with it, which matches the site's split; I have nothing to move the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. I lean a little higher for a third meeting in eight days with a semifinal place on the line; San Jose were booked three times in their last league game.

shots.text: The site expects 26.9 shots. Werner's fitness and the short turnaround weigh on San Jose, and Houston are a low-event team, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 on target. Both teams have struggled to hit the target lately (Houston six of 23 against St. Louis, San Jose three at Minnesota), so I lean lower.

401933735.overall: Early view: Game 3 at Energizer Park on Wednesday 2 December, only played if the series is 1-1, with kick-off still to be set; a draw goes to penalties. LAFC would fly in from Los Angeles four days after Game 2, and they went 3-7-7 on the road in the league. St. Louis beat Columbus on penalties to win the US Open Cup, so a shootout would hold no fears for them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean lower: LAFC's club-low 52 goals and poor road form, St. Louis's slump in front of goal, and the caution of a decider all point to a low-scoring game.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners. LAFC win a lot of corners when they control the ball (12 at Seattle) and St. Louis have been conceding territory, so I lean higher, as I do for Game 1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. A third meeting in nine days with a semifinal at stake should bring more fouls than the opener, so I lean a little higher; Sergi Palencia, listed as banned by the site, should be available again by then.

shots.text: The site expects 29.4 shots. LAFC's travel and short rest may take some edge off their pressure, which offsets the high volumes both teams allowed in their last games, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 on target. Both teams have struggled to turn shots into efforts on goal, and nothing points to that changing in a decider, so I stay with the number.

401884736.overall: Early view: Bayern are top on goal difference and unbeaten in the league, but Vincent Kompany is still recovering at home from meningeal irritation (assistant Aaron Danks has led the team since late October) and Manuel Neuer went off at half-time in Mainz with a foot problem, so Jonas Urbig is likely in goal. Köln have won one of their last seven league games and lost the Rhine derby; with Thijs Dallinga out for the season and Ragnar Ache a doubt, their threat leans on Saïd El Mala. Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz are both training again and could return here.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.5 goals, with 3.7 for Bayern. I lean a little lower: Köln have scored only 10 in nine games and are without Dallinga, so 0.8 for them looks generous, and Bayern's first game back after an international break, with Kompany's return still open, may not be at full speed. Bayern should still clear three at home.

corners.text: The site expects 10.9 corners, 7.2 of them Bayern's. I lean slightly higher: Bayern had about 81% of the ball in Mainz and Köln, short of a target man, are likely to sit deep and clear crosses behind. Michael Olise drives at defenders from wide all game, and a returning Díaz would add another winger.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean higher because Köln collected six yellow cards in the derby against Leverkusen and seven were shown in their 1-1 at Union, a pattern of chasing and fouling that fits an evening spent without the ball in Munich. Bayern rarely take more than one or two, and the referee is not yet known.

shots.text: The site has 32 shots, 21.8 for Bayern and 10.3 for Köln. Bayern's part fits their season (184 shots in their first eight games, about 23 per game), but ten for Köln at the Allianz Arena looks high for a side that managed ten at home in the derby and has lost its main striker. I lean a touch lower overall.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.5 on target, 9.3 from Bayern. Bayern had seven on target by the 72nd minute in Mainz, so their share is reasonable, but Köln's 3.2 looks generous given their blunt attack without Dallinga. I lean slightly lower, mostly on the Köln side.

401884732.overall: Early view: Union have tightened up under Mauro Lustrinelli after conceding 17 goals in their first four games, but they were toothless at Freiburg (no shots in the first half) and still lack a reliable striker. Leipzig have won all five home games under Martín Demichelis yet have taken only three of their 18 points away from home, and they have Champions League football the following week.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Union were unbeaten in four league games before Freiburg while conceding only twice, playing from a deeper block, and Leipzig have been far less convincing away than at home. Union's own attack, seven goals in nine, is the main reason to expect a modest total.

corners.text: The site expects 9.2 corners. Leipzig should have most of the ball, which usually produces corners against a low block, but Union offered almost nothing going forward at Freiburg, so their own share may be small. These two effects roughly cancel, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. I lean a little higher: Julian Schuster called games against Union 'always very physical', and seven yellow cards were shown when Köln visited the Alte Försterei recently. A Union side near the bottom, at home against a Leipzig team that counters quickly, is likely to commit tactical fouls.

shots.text: The site has 25.1 shots, 11.4 for Union. That home figure looks high for a side that had no shots at all in the first half at Freiburg and has struggled to find a striker, with Andrej Ilic, Oliver Burke and Emmanuel Latte Lath all short of form or fitness earlier this autumn. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 on target. With Union's attack blunt and their plan built on keeping the score low, I expect fewer, and Leipzig away have not been as sharp as their 23-2 home goal record suggests. I lean slightly lower.

401884735.overall: Early view: Leverkusen want the ball and press high under Carles Martínez, but they had lost three of four competitive games before winning the derby in Köln and have conceded 17 league goals. Paderborn are unbeaten in four league games, sit compact in a 3-3-2-2 and have a goalkeeper in form in Nahuel Noll. Leverkusen also have Europa League football to manage around this round.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean higher: Leverkusen scored at least twice in each of their first ten competitive games under Martínez and their league games have produced 37 goals in nine, partly because their defence has been loose (four conceded at home to Stuttgart). Paderborn are hard to beat but scored twice against Frankfurt last time out.

corners.text: The site expects 11.4 corners, 8.2 for Leverkusen. That already reflects a possession side against a deep back five, and Leverkusen had almost 60% of the ball in Köln. Paderborn are not purely passive (they finished strongly with the ball at Gladbach), so I see no reason to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I lean higher because Leverkusen's games have been card-heavy lately: eleven yellows in the derby and seven in the first hour against Stuttgart. Paderborn picked up three at Gladbach and coach Ralf Kettemann was booked against Frankfurt.

shots.text: The site has 31.8 shots, 21.6 of them Leverkusen's. Leverkusen took 15 in the derby and Paderborn's back five blocks a lot, so more than 20 for the hosts feels high, while Paderborn's 10.2 is generous for a side with eight league goals. I lean a little lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 on target. Leverkusen's finishers (Patrik Schick, Aleix García from free kicks) should test Noll often, and Paderborn hit the bar and scored twice against Frankfurt, so I stay close to the number.

401884731.overall: Early view: Gladbach are bottom with one league win, have Ko Itakura suspended after his red card in Hamburg, and captain Tim Kleindienst is still working back from a muscle tear under Alexander Blessin, who replaced the sacked Eugen Polanski in September. Dortmund are unbeaten with the league's best defence, but Serhou Guirassy has a thigh strain and Carney Chukwuemeka went off injured against Elversberg. With a Champions League trip to Arsenal three days later, Niko Kovač may rotate.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower: Dortmund's league games average under three goals (16 scored, 7 conceded) and Kovač's side tends to control games rather than chase a big margin, while Gladbach lose Itakura and are likely still without Kleindienst. Gladbach do concede often, which is why I do not go far below the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.2 corners split evenly. Dortmund should have more of the ball but have scored only two set-piece goals and often build patiently rather than cross, and Gladbach at home will try to press early. Nothing points clearly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. I lean slightly higher: Gladbach's frustration has shown in their discipline, with Itakura's second yellow in Hamburg and bookings for throwing the ball away and an arm in an opponent's face against Paderborn. Dortmund collected three yellows even in a routine home win over Elversberg.

shots.text: The site has 28.2 shots, 13.5 for Gladbach. That looks high against the league's tightest defence for a home side likely to be without Kleindienst and relying on Shuto Machino and teenager Wael Mohya. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. With Guirassy doubtful, Dortmund perhaps rotating before Arsenal and Gladbach short of a finisher, I lean a little lower. Felix Nmecha, who scored twice against Elversberg with late runs from midfield, is Dortmund's likeliest source of efforts on target if Guirassy is out.

401884734.overall: Early view: Two sides level on 12 points whose games have been open: Frankfurt have conceded 20 in nine under Adi Hütter and Hoffenheim's league games have produced 33 goals. Frankfurt are without right-back Elias Baum, suspended after his yellow-red card at Paderborn, and Hoffenheim are missing several defenders, including Albian Hajdari and Valentin Gendrey, while also juggling European football.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already high. I lean slightly higher: Frankfurt's games average almost four goals, and both back lines are weakened, Frankfurt without Baum and Hoffenheim without Hajdari, Gendrey and Robin Hranac. Hütter's teams press aggressively, which produces chances at both ends.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners. Both teams attack through the middle as much as the flanks, Frankfurt with Can Uzun and Farès Chaïbi, Hoffenheim with two strikers in Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle, so I see no reason to move far from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. I lean slightly lower: Hoffenheim have been disciplined lately, with one booking at Bremen and none in the win over Schalke. Frankfurt's recent cards came in tense finishes (Baum sent off at Paderborn, Hütter booked against Hamburg), but without a derby edge this looks like an average game for bookings.

shots.text: The site has 28.3 shots, split almost evenly. Both sides take plenty of shots, and Hoffenheim's patchy finishing (one shot on target at Bremen despite more of the ball) affects accuracy more than volume. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 on target. I lean a little higher because both defences are depleted and Frankfurt have conceded 20 goals in nine, so opponents regularly hit the target against them. Jonathan Burkardt, with two goals at Paderborn, and Younes Ebnoutalib give Frankfurt two finishers in form.

401884728.overall: Early view: Promoted Elversberg sit seventh under Vincent Wagner, have scored four against both Gladbach and Mainz and are dangerous from set pieces, but captain Lukas Pinckert went off with a knock at Dortmund. Freiburg are third with their best-scoring start in club history and dominated Union last time, though Julian Schuster rotates heavily around Conference League games.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean slightly higher: Elversberg's league games have produced 35 goals in nine, and they score from free kicks and corners (two of their four against Mainz). Freiburg concede little (10 in nine), but their attack has been the most productive in the club's history at this stage.

corners.text: The site expects 9.9 corners, 5.7 for Freiburg. I lean higher: Freiburg had around two thirds of the ball against Union and win corners through Niklas Beste's and Vincenzo Grifo's crossing, and Elversberg push for corners because they score from them.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. Freiburg typically pick up two or three (three at Augsburg, two against Union) and Elversberg had one player booked at Dortmund plus their coach. Nothing here points away from the number.

shots.text: The site has 28 shots, 15.9 for Freiburg. That is plausible for a Freiburg side that dominates possession, and Elversberg's 12 at home fits their attacking approach, so I see no strong reason to move it either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 on target. In line with my goals view I lean slightly higher: Elversberg's finishing has been sharp in their four-goal games and Freiburg have forwards in form in Igor Matanović and Yuito Suzuki.

401884729.overall: Early view: Promoted Schalke are 17th and have not scored in a home league game this season, and Miron Muslić is waiting on news of goalkeeper Loris Karius and Robin Gosens after both were hurt in a collision at Hoffenheim. Stuttgart arrive on two straight league wins but with Angelo Stiller among several injured regulars and a Champions League match in the following week.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: all five of Schalke's league goals have come away from home, and their games have produced only 16 goals in nine, the fewest in the league. Stuttgart scored just once against Bremen in their last outing.

corners.text: The site expects 10.5 corners, 6.1 for Stuttgart. Stuttgart's wing-backs push high in their 3-4-2-1 and Schalke will defend deep, which supports the number, but Schalke's home attack creates little pressure of its own. I stay close to it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. I lean slightly higher: a Schalke side fighting relegation in front of a full Veltins Arena will be aggressive, and Stuttgart's game at Leverkusen produced seven yellow cards in an hour. Schalke themselves took two bookings in each of their last two games.

shots.text: The site has 27.9 shots, 12.7 for Schalke. Schalke did create a lot at Hoffenheim (expected goals above 2.5), but at home they have been blunt, and Stuttgart may manage the game with Champions League football days later. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. With Schalke yet to score at home and possibly without Gosens, whom one injury tracker lists out until mid-December with a knee problem, I expect fewer on-target efforts from the hosts. Stuttgart's Ermedin Demirović and Deniz Undav should provide most of the total.

401884733.overall: Early view: Two sides heading the wrong way: Augsburg are winless in seven league games under Manuel Baum despite scoring in every match, and Mainz lost four of their last five in all competitions before the break. Mainz have taken nine of their ten points away from home, though, which makes this trip more promising for Urs Fischer's side than the table suggests.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: Augsburg's league games have produced 40 goals in nine (joint-most in the league) and Mainz's 37, with Mainz scoring most of theirs away through Phillip Tietz, Sheraldo Becker and Benedict Hollerbach. Both defences concede freely, Mainz nine in three games in late October.

corners.text: The site expects 9.8 corners. Augsburg's wing-backs give them width at home and Mainz's pace-based counters do not produce many corners, but nothing in the recent games points clearly away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. I lean slightly higher: Fischer has talked about a 'slightly nasty' style, Stefan Posch was sent off at Elversberg, and a meeting of two sides under pressure tends to be scrappy. Augsburg have been fairly clean lately (no bookings against Freiburg), which stops me going much higher.

shots.text: The site has 31.7 shots. Mainz away rely on quick transitions rather than long spells of pressure, so their 13.8 looks high, and Augsburg's 17.9 is generous for a side that has been outplayed in several recent games. I lean a little lower on volume, while still expecting goals.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 on target. That fits my higher goals view: Augsburg's Michael Gregoritsch and Kade have both scored recently and Mainz's Tietz leads their line, while both defences let opponents get shots away. I stay level.

401884730.overall: Early view: The Nordderby comes with Bremen sixth after their best start since 2018/19 under Daniel Thioune, built on Niclas Füllkrug's league-leading nine goals and a habit of scoring late. Hamburg beat ten-man Gladbach 3-1 to end three straight competitive defeats, but have lost four of five away games and Merlin Polzin's squad is thin; one injury tracker lists Miro Muheim, scorer of three long-range goals, out until late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Hamburg's poor away record and 20 goals conceded point up, but derbies are often cagey and Bremen were held scoreless at Stuttgart despite 13 shots. I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners, 5.6 for Bremen. I lean slightly higher: 14 of Bremen's 17 goals have come after half-time and they push hard late on, which tends to produce a run of corners, while Hamburg defending a lead or a draw will clear wide.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already high because of the derby. Bremen took three yellows in each of their last two games and Hamburg four at Frankfurt, which supports a busy afternoon for the referee, but the number already reflects that, so I stay level.

shots.text: The site has 31.2 shots, 19.6 for Bremen. Bremen took 13 at Stuttgart and their attack runs mostly through Füllkrug, so nearly 20 at home looks high, even against a side that has lost four of five away. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 on target. In line with fewer shots I lean slightly lower, although Hamburg's long-range shooters (Muheim if fit, and Albert Grønbæk, who scored from distance against Gladbach) can test the keeper from anywhere.

401884720.overall: Early view: Bremen host the bottom side five days after the Nordderby. The brief lists Ko Itakura as missing, but his yellow-red ban is a one-match suspension to be served against Dortmund, so he should be available; Gladbach also hope to have captain Tim Kleindienst back from his muscle tear by then. Bremen's goals tend to come late, 14 of their 17 after half-time.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean higher: Gladbach's league games have averaged over four goals (12 scored, 25 conceded) and Bremen's about 3.6, with Füllkrug scoring in seven straight games before the defeat at Stuttgart. Bremen's habit of scoring late adds to the case.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners. Bremen should have more of the ball, but Gladbach under Blessin defend with a back three and look to counter through Wael Mohya, which does not add corners on its own. I see nothing that moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean slightly higher: Bremen have taken three bookings in each of their last two games, and Gladbach's frustration has cost them yellows and a red recently. A bottom side chasing points away from home usually adds a couple of late cautions.

shots.text: The site has 31.6 shots, 18.6 for Bremen. Against a defence that has conceded 25, that home volume is reasonable, and Gladbach's 13 is fair if Kleindienst returns. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.7 on target, which is high. Bremen took 13 shots at Stuttgart without scoring and Gladbach have struggled to test keepers without Kleindienst, so I lean slightly lower even while expecting goals.

401884721.overall: Early view: Köln have won one of their last seven league games and are short of strikers, with Thijs Dallinga out for the season and Ragnar Ache a doubt, so much depends on Saïd El Mala and his brother Malek. Elversberg have been the most impressive of the promoted sides under Vincent Wagner, with open games and goals from set pieces.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Köln's games have been low on goals (24 in nine) while Elversberg's have been high (35 in nine), and the number sits between the two. I stay with it.

corners.text: The site expects 11.4 corners, 7.4 of them Köln's. That is a lot for a side that had 41% of the ball and ten shots in the derby; even at home against a promoted side, I lean lower on Köln's share.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean higher: Köln took six yellows in the derby and were part of a seven-card game at Union, with Linton Maina booked in both, a sign of a team that defends by fouling when under pressure.

shots.text: The site has 29.5 shots, 19.0 for Köln. With their main strikers out, 19 attempts looks high for Köln, who managed ten against Leverkusen. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 on target. Fewer Köln shots would normally mean fewer on target, but Elversberg finish efficiently and the El Mala brothers have scored in each of Köln's last two league games, so I stay level.

401884722.overall: Early view: Bayern visit Hamburg days after a Champions League matchday, with Vincent Kompany's return from illness not yet confirmed and Manuel Neuer injured, so Jonas Urbig should be in goal. Hamburg have won three of four home league games and score spectacular long-range goals, but Merlin Polzin's squad is thin and Bayern have scored 29 in nine.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, 2.8 for Bayern. Bayern's scoring rate supports it and Hamburg have scored at home, but a Bayern side coming off a European midweek may rotate and manage the game. I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10 corners, six of them Bayern's. Bayern pin teams back for long spells (around 80% of the ball in Mainz), and Hamburg are likely to defend in numbers and clear wide, so I lean higher on Bayern's share.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Hamburg picked up four yellows at Frankfurt, while Bayern are rarely booked more than twice, and nothing in the news points away from an average count.

shots.text: The site has 33.5 shots. Bayern's 22.2 matches their season average, but Hamburg's 11.3 is high against a side that allowed Mainz a single shot on target, the stoppage-time goal. I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.6 on target. Bayern's accuracy, with Harry Kane also leading the league in assists, keeps their share high, and Hamburg's long-range shooters can test Urbig from distance. I stay level.

401884723.overall: Early view: Mainz have one point from five home league games, against nine from four away, and lost four of their last five in all competitions before the break. Union have become harder to beat since a chaotic start under Mauro Lustrinelli but have scored only seven goals in nine, so this has the look of a scrappy, physical game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean lower: Mainz have been far more dangerous away than at home, and Union's recent league games have been tight, built on a deep block with little attack. The Union that conceded 17 in its first four games has not been seen since early October.

corners.text: The site expects 9.8 corners, 5.9 for Mainz. Mainz will have to make the game against a Union side that sits deep, which supports their share, while Union's own corners come rarely. I stay close to the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. I lean higher: Fischer wants a 'slightly nasty' style, Mainz had Stefan Posch sent off at Elversberg, and Union's games have been physical, with seven yellows when Köln visited Berlin. Both sides are under pressure in the lower half.

shots.text: The site has 27.2 shots. Union managed no shots in the first half at Freiburg and have no settled striker, so their 10.6 away looks high, and Mainz's home displays have been poor. I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 on target. With Union rarely testing goalkeepers and Mainz's best attacking work coming on the counter away from home rather than in front of their own fans, I lean slightly lower.

401884719.overall: Early view: A meeting of two promoted sides with the lowest-scoring league games in the division: Schalke's nine matches have produced 16 goals and Paderborn's 19. Paderborn are unbeaten in four under Ralf Kettemann and well organised, while Schalke have scored all their league goals away from home but may be without Robin Gosens and possibly goalkeeper Loris Karius after their collision at Hoffenheim.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.6 goals, which is very low. I lean slightly higher: Schalke's attack works better on the road (all five league goals away, and expected goals above 2.5 at Hoffenheim), and Paderborn scored twice at home against Frankfurt last time. A goalless draw is possible, but two goals feels more like the middle.

corners.text: The site expects 10.4 corners, 6.1 for Paderborn. Both sides have used back threes with wing-backs, which produces crosses, and nothing in the news points away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.4 cards, which looks low for a game near the bottom. Paderborn took three yellows at Gladbach and Kettemann was booked against Frankfurt, and Schalke have collected two in each of their last two games. I lean higher.

shots.text: The site has 28.6 shots. Neither side has a high-volume attack, and Paderborn's 0-0 at Gladbach was a typical low-volume game for them, so I lean slightly lower on volume while expecting the few chances to be decent ones.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 on target. Paderborn keep opponents to few clear chances (11 conceded in nine) and Schalke's attack is unsettled, so I lean slightly lower.

401884726.overall: Early view: Stuttgart had their worst start under Sebastian Hoeneß but won their last two league games, including 4-2 at Leverkusen, and this comes a few days after a Champions League matchday. Frankfurt's games average close to four goals and they concede often; the brief lists Elias Baum as missing, but his one-match ban will have been served against Hoffenheim, so he should be available.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Frankfurt's leaky defence and Stuttgart's attack (Ermedin Demirović, Jamie Leweling, Deniz Undav) point up, but Stuttgart looked tired after their last European trip and beat Bremen only 1-0. These pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 10.3 corners. Stuttgart attack through wing-backs and Frankfurt press high, which tends to give a steady flow of corners at both ends, but nothing suggests a big move from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean higher: Stuttgart's game at Leverkusen had seven yellows in the first hour, and Frankfurt had Baum sent off and Adi Hütter booked in their last two games. Two pressing sides tend to produce fouls in midfield.

shots.text: The site has 30.4 shots. Stuttgart's game at Leverkusen produced 36 attempts by the 82nd minute and Hütter's Frankfurt play at high intensity, so I lean higher on volume.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 on target. That fits two sides with in-form finishers, Demirović for Stuttgart and Jonathan Burkardt for Frankfurt, and I see no reason to move it.

401884724.overall: Early view: Third against fourth, one point apart. Freiburg have their best-scoring start in club history under Julian Schuster and have conceded only ten, while Leipzig have won every home game but taken only three points away. Both clubs play in Europe that week (Freiburg in the Conference League, Leipzig in the Champions League), so rotation is likely.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leipzig's league games have produced 40 goals in nine (joint-most in the league) and Freiburg have scored 20, a club record at this stage. Leipzig's poor away form has included a 6-1 defeat at Bayern, so their trips have not been low-scoring affairs.

corners.text: The site expects 8.8 corners. I lean higher: Freiburg had around two thirds of the ball against Union and rely a lot on Niklas Beste's and Vincenzo Grifo's deliveries, while Leipzig's wide players Antonio Nusa and Brajan Gruda attack defenders one against one.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. Freiburg usually take two or three bookings and Leipzig have been fairly clean (one booking against Augsburg), so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site has 26.2 shots. Two attacking sides near the top, with Freiburg dominating the ball at home and Leipzig shooting often, point to slightly more than the number, so I lean higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 on target. Rotation after European games could blunt both attacks, which balances my higher shot view, so I keep this close to the number.

401884725.overall: Early view: Augsburg's league games have produced 40 goals in nine, joint-most in the division, and they have scored in every match despite going seven without a win under Manuel Baum. Hoffenheim under Christian Ilzer should be favourites at home but are likely coming off a European midweek, with several defenders out until December or January.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean higher: Augsburg score in every game but concede plenty (five at Leipzig), and Hoffenheim's defence is missing Albian Hajdari, Valentin Gendrey and Robin Hranac. Hoffenheim's own league games average close to 3.7 goals.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners. Hoffenheim play with two strikers and Augsburg with wing-backs, which keeps corners around average, and I find nothing that moves the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean lower: Hoffenheim took one booking at Bremen and none against Schalke, and Augsburg had no bookings against Freiburg and two at Leipzig. Neither side has been card-prone lately.

shots.text: The site has 33.2 shots, which is high. Hoffenheim's volume and accuracy dipped at Bremen, and European fatigue could slow them, so I lean slightly lower on volume while still expecting goals.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 on target. Augsburg's defensive record means opponents usually hit the target, and Hoffenheim have two finishers in Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle, so I stay level.

401884727.overall: Early view: Dortmund have the league's best defence and are unbeaten, but they play at Arsenal in the Champions League five days earlier. Leverkusen, likely coming off a European game that week, have been inconsistent under Carles Martínez and concede often. Serhou Guirassy should be back from his thigh strain by then if his recovery goes to plan.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Dortmund's league games are usually tight (23 goals in nine) while Leverkusen's are open (37 in nine), and the number sits between them. I stay with it.

corners.text: The site expects 9.6 corners. Leverkusen keep the ball for long spells and Dortmund are comfortable defending deep, as they did against Bayern, which tends to produce corners for the visitors. I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean higher: Leverkusen's recent games have been card-heavy (eleven yellows in the derby, seven in an hour against Stuttgart) and this is a top-five meeting after a draining European week. Dortmund had three players booked against Elversberg.

shots.text: The site has 27.2 shots. Dortmund limit opponents well and do not need many shots themselves, and both sides may be tired after midweek, so I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 on target. Leverkusen's loose defence gives Dortmund chances, while Dortmund's deep defending keeps Leverkusen's efforts from good areas to a minimum; these balance out, so I stay level.

401884718.overall: Early view: Bayern should have more of their injured players back by early December, with Jamal Musiala and Luis Díaz both expected to return after the break, though Serge Gnabry is out for the rest of the year and one injury tracker lists Manuel Neuer out until January. Paderborn have conceded only 11 in nine games, one of the better records in the league, and goalkeeper Nahuel Noll has been in good form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. I lean slightly higher: Bayern have scored 29 in nine, including seven against Union and six against Leipzig, and with Musiala and Díaz back their attack should be deeper. Paderborn defend well, but rarely face this level of pressure.

corners.text: The site expects 11.6 corners. Paderborn defend with a back five and Bayern will have most of the ball, so I lean slightly higher; in that kind of game Bayern's corners pile up from blocked crosses and shots.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards. Paderborn have been booked regularly (three at Gladbach, plus coach Ralf Kettemann against Frankfurt), and teams chasing Bayern's passing commit tactical fouls, so I lean a little higher.

shots.text: The site has 36.8 shots, 27.2 for Bayern. That Bayern figure is well above their season rate of about 23 per game, so even against a deep side I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.6 on target, ten of them Bayern's. Paderborn block a lot of shots with five defenders in a crowded box, so I lean slightly lower, though Bayern should still dominate this count.

401884712.overall: Early view: Union host Hamburg in a game between two sides who have struggled for goals: Union have scored seven in nine and still lack a reliable striker, Hamburg ten. Hamburg have lost four of five away games, while Union have become much harder to break down since their poor start under Mauro Lustrinelli.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean lower: Union's recent league games have been low-scoring, built on a deeper block, and Hamburg have scored only ten all season. The main route to a higher total is Hamburg's defence, which has conceded 20.

corners.text: The site expects 9.3 corners. Union at home will push more than they do away, while Hamburg's attack relies on long-range shots rather than crosses, so I see no reason to move far from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards. I lean slightly higher: seven yellows were shown when Köln visited the Alte Försterei, and Hamburg took four at Frankfurt. Two sides in the lower half meeting in December is rarely a calm game.

shots.text: The site has 25.9 shots. Union had no first-half shots at Freiburg and Hamburg's thin squad has limited options in attack, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 on target. With both attacks among the weakest in the league by goals scored, I lean slightly lower.

401884716.overall: Early view: Leverkusen host the bottom side the week after their trip to Dortmund, and both teams' league games have averaged more than four goals. The brief lists Ko Itakura as missing, but his one-match ban will have been served against Dortmund, and Gladbach hope to have Tim Kleindienst back, though they took one win from their first nine games under two coaches.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. I lean higher: Leverkusen's games and Gladbach's have both produced 37 goals in nine, with Gladbach conceding 25. Carles Martínez's side scored at least twice in each of its first ten competitive games.

corners.text: The site expects 10.4 corners. Leverkusen's possession game against a Gladbach side likely to sit deep in a back three or five should produce plenty of corners for the hosts, so I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already high. Leverkusen's games have been card-heavy and Gladbach's frustration has shown, but the number already reflects both, so I stay level.

shots.text: The site has 31.6 shots. That is a lot, but Leverkusen at home against a defence that concedes nearly three a game should get there, and Gladbach's share depends on whether Kleindienst is back. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 on target. In line with my goals view I lean slightly higher: Gladbach's defence lets opponents hit the target often, and Leverkusen have Patrik Schick, who scored in the derby, in form.

401884713.overall: Early view: A meeting of 14th and 15th, both on nine points. Augsburg have scored in every league game but conceded 20 and are winless in seven, while Köln are missing Timo Hübers and Ellyes Skhiri until January and Thijs Dallinga for the season.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean slightly higher: Augsburg's games average more than four goals, and Köln's defence is without Hübers. Köln's own low-scoring games pull the other way, which is why I do not go far.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners. Neither team has a strong pattern of dominating territory, and I find nothing in the news to move the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards. Köln's discipline is the main factor: six yellows in the derby and a seven-card game at Union. Augsburg are cleaner, but a six-pointer near the drop zone adds tension, so I lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The site has 30 shots. Köln's attack without its strikers has been low on volume (ten in the derby), so their 14.4 looks high. I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 on target. Augsburg's front line, with Michael Gregoritsch and Kade both scoring recently, should test the keeper often, which offsets Köln's weaker attack. I stay level.

401884717.overall: Early view: Leipzig have won all five home league games with a 23-2 goal difference under Martín Demichelis. Mainz are an odd case among the struggling sides, poor at home but strong away (nine of their ten points on the road), though they lost four of their last five in all competitions before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean higher: Leipzig average more than four goals a game at home and Mainz have scored most of their goals away, through Phillip Tietz, Sheraldo Becker and Benedict Hollerbach. Mainz's defence conceded nine in three games in late October.

corners.text: The site expects 9.8 corners. Leipzig dominate the ball at home (about 65% against Augsburg) but often score before corners pile up, and Mainz counter rather than cross. I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Urs Fischer has described Mainz's style as 'slightly nasty' and Stefan Posch was sent off at Elversberg, so I lean slightly higher, even though Leipzig themselves are rarely booked.

shots.text: The site has 28.9 shots. That fits a dominant Leipzig at home and a Mainz side that gets chances on the break, so I stay level.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.4 on target. In line with my goals view I lean slightly higher: Leipzig's attack (Rômulo, Christopher Nkunku, Brajan Gruda) has been ruthless at home, scoring five against Augsburg.

401884715.overall: Early view: Two European sides from the south-west. Freiburg have been the more consistent under Julian Schuster, with only ten conceded in nine, while Hoffenheim's results under Christian Ilzer have swung, from 3-0 against Leverkusen to 0-2 at Bremen with one shot on target, and they have several defenders out until December or January.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Freiburg's tight defence pulls the total down and Hoffenheim's depleted back line pulls it up, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.4 corners. Freiburg dominate possession at home and cross a lot through Niklas Beste and Vincenzo Grifo, so I lean slightly higher on their share.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. Hoffenheim have been disciplined lately (one booking in their last two league games) and Freiburg average two or three, so I lean slightly lower.

shots.text: The site has 27.1 shots. Both teams take a fair number of shots, and I find nothing to move the number much either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 on target. Freiburg have scored a club-record number of goals for this stage and Hoffenheim's two-striker system gets shots away, so I lean slightly higher.

401884714.overall: Early view: Two of the league's more open sides: Frankfurt's games average almost four goals, and Bremen often score late, with Niclas Füllkrug the league's top scorer on nine. The brief lists Elias Baum as missing, but his one-match ban will have been served against Hoffenheim, so he should be available.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean higher: Frankfurt have conceded 20 and scored 15, and Bremen's games have produced 32 goals, with no team taking more points from losing positions. Late goals are a feature of both, as Jonathan Burkardt's stoppage-time equaliser at Paderborn showed.

corners.text: The site expects 9.8 corners. Bremen's late pushes add corners, but Frankfurt rely more on quick vertical attacks than crossing, so overall I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean slightly higher: Bremen took three yellows in each of their last two games, and Frankfurt had Baum sent off and Adi Hütter booked in recent weeks.

shots.text: The site has 29 shots. Bremen took 13 at Stuttgart and Frankfurt's pressing creates shots at both ends, which is in line with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 on target. With two attacks in form (Füllkrug for Bremen, Burkardt and Younes Ebnoutalib for Frankfurt) and two defences that concede, I lean slightly higher.

401884711.overall: Early view: The Revierderby, with promoted Schalke near the bottom and yet to score in a home league game this season, against a Dortmund side built on the league's best defence. Derby intensity should push the card count up, but both teams' games point to few goals.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals. Schalke's home attack has not scored and Dortmund's games are usually tight, while derbies can break open late; nothing pushes me away from the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.7 corners, 5.6 for Dortmund. Schalke will defend deep and Dortmund will have the ball, which fits the number, so I stay level.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. I lean higher because this is the Revierderby: Schalke at home will be aggressive, and Dortmund had three players booked even in a calm home win over Elversberg.

shots.text: The site has 24.7 shots. Schalke have been blunt at home and Dortmund tend to control games without piling up attempts, so I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 on target. Schalke's home finishing and Dortmund's control point to few clear chances, so I lean slightly lower.

401884710.overall: Early view: Elversberg have scored four against both Gladbach and Mainz and add set-piece goals from Felix Keidel and Maurice Krattenmacher, so they are dangerous at home. Stuttgart are in the Champions League and had a long injury list in early November, including Angelo Stiller, though several were expected back after the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean slightly higher: Elversberg's games have produced 35 goals in nine and Stuttgart's 30, with Stuttgart conceding three at home to Gladbach and two at Leverkusen. Both sides attack more than they defend.

corners.text: The site expects 11.5 corners, 6.8 for Stuttgart. That Stuttgart share is high for an away side, and Elversberg have been willing to attack at home rather than sit deep, so I lean lower.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. Elversberg had one player booked at Dortmund and Stuttgart's card count has depended on the opponent, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site has 32.9 shots, which is high. Stuttgart's 18.7 away looks generous for a side that may rotate around Champions League football, so I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 on target. Two sides with efficient finishing (Elversberg's set pieces, Stuttgart's Ermedin Demirović and Jamie Leweling) keep this close to the number despite my lower shot view.

401876395.overall: Early view: a bottom-two meeting between Troyes (17th, 8 points) and Le Havre (18th, 2 points), the first league game after the break. Le Havre suspended coach Didier Digard after the 5-1 home loss to PSG and lost 0-2 to Lorient in interim coach Jair Karam's first game, so who is on their bench by 20 November matters. Troyes have the league's weakest attack (7 goals) but had steadied with a 2-0 win over Le Mans and a narrow 1-0 loss at PSG.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Troyes have scored only 7 times in 10 games and Le Havre failed to score against Lorient, while Troyes' defence has tightened (two clean sheets before a 1-0 loss at PSG in which keeper Konate made seven saves). A tense six-pointer like this tends to be cagey, so 1-0 or 1-1 type scores look more likely than an open game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. I lean a little higher: Statz season averages put Troyes 4th in the league for corners won (5.7 a game) and Le Havre 7th (5.3), and Le Havre take a lot of shots for a bottom side. Neither side will be content with a draw, which should keep both pushing for set pieces.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean higher: this is a direct relegation fight, Le Havre are 5th for fouls (14 a game), and a club in turmoil with an interim or brand-new coach is still chasing its first win. Troyes picked up two late yellows even in a tight 1-0 at PSG.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. I lean slightly higher: Le Havre average about 16 shots a game despite their results and Troyes about 13, and both need the win. Expect plenty of efforts from range rather than many clear chances.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. I see no reason to move it: Troyes rank 16th for shots on target (3.3 a game) and Le Havre's volume rarely turns into quality, as the blank against Lorient showed. Volume up, accuracy low, so the total should land near the site's figure.

401876398.overall: Early view: PSG arrive top with seven straight league wins, but Ousmane Dembele, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes were injured for their last match and Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is out long term; they host Roma in the Champions League four days later, so some rotation is possible. Nice (6th) have won four of their last five league games under Olivier Pantaloni, including 5-2 against Rennes and 2-0 at Angers, but are without Antoine Mendy and Laurent Abergel, with Moise Bombito doubtful.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: PSG's attack is thinner without Dembele and Kvaratskhelia, Ferran Torres went into the Troyes game seven matches without a goal, and PSG needed a Zabarnyi goal to edge Troyes 1-0 despite 73% of the ball. Nice have scored 15 in 10 and will look to counter, which points to a 2-1 or 2-0 type game rather than a rout.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. That looks about right: PSG win 5.5 corners a game and Nice 5.7, but Nice will spend long spells without the ball here. PSG had only five corners in their 73%-possession win over Troyes, so a big total is not a given.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. I lean slightly lower: per Statz PSG commit the fewest fouls in the league (6.5 a game) and Nice are 16th (9.9), so neither side plays a stop-start game. Unless the referee appointment changes the picture, two or three bookings feels like the right range.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots. I lean lower: PSG lead the league with 19.3 shots a game, but a makeshift front line and an eye on Roma could trim that, and Nice average only about 12. PSG managed 15 shots against Troyes, well under their average.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, which is high. I lean lower: PSG average 7.8 on target and Nice 4.0, and Nice usually get fewer looks against top sides. Ten or eleven is more realistic unless PSG field their full first-choice attack.

401876399.overall: Early view: Monaco have not won in five league games (the latest a 1-1 at Le Mans in which they were outshot 19-5), yet Filipe Luis' side has won every Conference League game and travels to Hearts five days after this. Auxerre under Will Still are 14th with the league's worst defence (24 conceded), though almost all of that damage has come away from home, and they lost 1-0 at home to Paris FC before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I stay close to that: Monaco's attack has stalled (13 goals in 10 games), but Auxerre have leaked most of their 24 goals on the road, including 5-1 at Strasbourg and 4-1 at Rennes. Those two trends roughly cancel out, and Cameron Archer (six league goals) gives Auxerre a real outlet on the break.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. I lean lower: Monaco rank 12th for corners won (4.1 a game) and Auxerre won just one corner in their home loss to Paris FC. Monaco's slow build-up has produced few spells of sustained pressure lately.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean higher: per Statz Auxerre commit the most fouls in Ligue 1 (16.3 a game) and made 24 against Paris FC, collecting three yellows. If Monaco's wide players run at them, more bookings for the visitors look likely.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. I lean lower: Monaco average only 11.7 shots a game (14th) and managed five at Le Mans, and Auxerre average 11.1 (16th). Monaco should shoot more at home against a weaker side, but probably not enough to reach the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Monaco's 4.2 a game and Auxerre's 4.5 sum to under nine, and Auxerre only got two on target against Paris FC. Monaco were also described as wasteful in front of goal in their last Conference League win.

401876403.overall: Early view: Lens (11th) come out of the break on two league defeats, to Lille and Marseille, and with the scars of a 9-1 Champions League loss to Como; they travel to Leipzig three days after this game, so Yannick Cahuzac may rotate. Toulouse (12th, level on 13 points) bounced back from a 2-0 loss at Marseille by beating Strasbourg 3-1 under Jens Berthel Askou.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I see no strong reason to move: Lens score most of their league goals at Bollaert (about 10 of 17) but have conceded 15 and looked fragile in Europe, while Toulouse score and concede roughly 1.5 a game. Lens' injury list up front (Odsonne Edouard doubtful, Abdallah Sima out as of early November) is the one thing that could pull it lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean higher: Lens are 2nd in the league for corners won (5.8 a game) and Toulouse took seven against Strasbourg. Toulouse carry a set-piece threat too, with Mark McKenzie heading in a Cristian Casseres corner last time out.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean slightly higher: Toulouse commit the second-most fouls in Ligue 1 (15.8 a game) and picked up three yellows against Strasbourg, and Lens are 7th for fouls. Four or five bookings feels more likely than three.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Season averages agree (Lens 12.9, Toulouse 12.6 a game), so I stay put. Any Lens rotation before Leipzig could shave a couple off, but Toulouse's direct play should keep the visitors' count up.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean higher: Lens are 4th for shots on target (5.4 a game) and had six against Marseille, and Toulouse average 4.7. Both goalkeepers should be kept busy.

401876402.overall: Early view: second hosts fifth in a meeting of two of the league's three best defences (Lille 7 conceded, Lyon 9). Davide Ancelotti's Lille won 2-1 at Rennes before the break but host Bayern Munich four days later, while Lyon lost 2-0 at Brest and play Lillestrom in the Europa League on the Thursday after, so both may manage minutes.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean lower: Lille have kept five clean sheets and conceded only seven, Lyon have conceded nine, and both coaches have European games next. Lyon are also without Pavel Sulc (out until January) and may still be easing Lois Openda back from a leg injury.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. I lean lower: Lille win only 3.6 corners a game (14th) and had two at Rennes, and Lyon average 4.6. Lyon did win eight at Brest with 69% of the ball, so the total depends on how much possession Lille concede.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. That looks fair: Lille picked up three yellows at Rennes and Tanguy Nianzou was sent off against Lens earlier in the season, but Lyon are a low-foul side (11.6 a game). Nothing points strongly either way before the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. I stay close to it: season averages (Lille 11.4, Lyon 12.8) suggest a little more, but games between well-organised defences like these tend to be tight. Lille had only eight shots in their win at Rennes.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. I lean lower: Lyon managed just two on target from 10 shots at Brest, Rennes managed two against Lille, and both defences protect the box well. Seven or so feels more likely.

401876396.overall: Early view: Strasbourg (13th) have lost five of their last six league games and one report says coach Hugo Oliveira is under strong pressure, so a change on the bench during the break cannot be ruled out. Brest (9th) are in good form under Julien Lachuer after 2-0 wins at Lorient and at home to Lyon, though Raphael Le Guen is out for months and Brendan Chardonnet's calf problem was expected to keep him out for up to two weeks from early November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean a little higher: Strasbourg's games have produced 40 goals in 10 (18 for, 22 against), and Brest score 1.8 a game with Ludovic Ajorque leading the line. corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. I lean lower: per Statz Strasbourg win the fewest corners in Ligue 1 (2.5 a game) and had one at Toulouse, and Brest play a direct, low-possession game (one corner against Lyon). Neither side builds the sustained pressure that racks up corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. I lean higher: Brest are 4th for fouls (14.2 a game), and a home side on a bad run with a coach under pressure is prone to frustration. Strasbourg collected three yellows at Toulouse.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. I lean higher: Brest average 16.1 shots a game (4th) and Strasbourg 12.6, and Strasbourg's defence gives up plenty. An open game with both sides needing points fits a higher count.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean higher: Brest are 3rd for shots on target (5.7 a game) and had six against Lyon, and Strasbourg average 4.9. Ten or so looks more likely than eight.
