401888244.overall: Early view: Fenerbahce (6th) have a new coach in Emre Belozoglu, who replaced Ismail Kartal and started with a 5-0 win at Corum, days after the club beat Liverpool 3-2 in the Champions League. Selcuk Inan's Kocaelispor are level on 19 points, have conceded only nine goals in eleven games and took seven points from their last three, and their chairman called them favourites for this one. Marco Asensio was injured and Archie Brown suspended for the Corum trip, so Fenerbahce's team news needs rechecking.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean lower: Kocaelispor's matches have averaged two goals, their last home game was 0-0 with Rizespor, and Inan's side defends compactly. Fenerbahce are the league's top scorers with 29, but they lost 2-1 at home to Goztepe on 2 November, so goals against an organised defence have not always come easily.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Fenerbahce will have most of the ball against a low block, which tends to produce corners, while Kocaelispor rely on counters and their own set pieces; the split may be more one-sided than 4.9 to 4.6, but the total looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and I lean higher. A big-club visit to Kocaeli usually brings tactical fouls on the break and protests, and Belozoglu was referred to the disciplinary board over remarks about referees in his last weeks at Kasimpasa, so the touchline may be lively too.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots. Kocaelispor's games are low-event and they rarely open up, so I lean lower; Fenerbahce will shoot plenty, but 14 home shots for Kocaelispor look generous for a team that has scored 13 in eleven games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. With Kocaelispor packing the box and creating little, I lean slightly lower, with most efforts on target likely to come from Mason Greenwood and Irfan Can Kahveci, who shared four goals at Corum.

401888243.overall: Early view: Goztepe (10th) won four league games in a row, including 2-1 at Fenerbahce, before Basaksehir beat them 2-1 in Izmir. Promoted Erzurumspor (12th) under Serkan Ozbalta have lost their last two, 3-1 at home to Corum and 2-1 at Rizespor, and have scored only ten goals in eleven games. This is a first read and will be updated with team news, which is thin for both sides so far.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I lean slightly higher. Goztepe's eleven games have produced 41 goals, with Juan, Henrique and Armstrong all scoring recently, and Erzurumspor conceded three at home to Corum in their last home match.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.2 corners. Neither side's recent games point to a big change, and with Erzurumspor likely to sit in against an in-form visitor, I keep it close to eight.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Nothing specific moves this: no suspensions are reported on either side and there is no rivalry to speak of, so around four looks fair until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, with Goztepe taking slightly more. That suits a game where Goztepe's attack meets a home side that has been leaking chances, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. I lean a little higher in line with goals: Goztepe have scored 22 in eleven and Erzurumspor have conceded 17, so the visitors in particular should test the keeper often.

401888248.overall: Early view: Kasimpasa (5th, unbeaten in four) lost coach Emre Belozoglu to Fenerbahce and appointed Alfred Schreuder until the end of the season; this is his first home league game, after two weeks to work with the squad over the break. Alanyaspor under Joao Pereira have lost four in a row, including 5-0 at Genclerbirligi and 2-0 at home to Trabzonspor, and have scored once in their last three games.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and I lean slightly lower. Alanyaspor have scored nine all season and one in their last three, so most of the goals have to come from Kasimpasa, who won 2-0 at Gaziantep with both goals in the first 20 minutes and then managed the game.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Kasimpasa should have most of the ball, as Trabzonspor did in Alanya when they gave Alanyaspor almost no possession, but there is nothing specific to push the total up or down.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Kasimpasa picked up two yellows at Gaziantep and Alanyaspor are a frustrated side on a losing run, but neither has shown a recent pattern of heavy bookings, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.2 shots. I lean lower because ten away shots look generous for an Alanyaspor team that has been pinned back in recent weeks, and a new coach's first home game is often a controlled one.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Alanyaspor rarely test the keeper at the moment, so I expect most of the efforts on target from Kasimpasa's Haris Hajradinovic and Adrian Benedyczak and a total slightly under the number.

401888246.overall: Early view: Besiktas (4th) went into the break on a 3-0 win over Genclerbirligi, with Dusan Vlahovic on nine league goals and Leandro Trossard creating, but captain Orkun Kokcu is suspended after his latest yellow card. Konyaspor (15th) under Ilhan Palut have scored six goals in eleven games, have not won away and lost 1-0 at Samsunspor in their last match. Fabio Miretti, hurt against Crystal Palace, is targeting a return for this game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals and I lean a touch lower. Konyaspor's games have produced just 20 goals in total, and without Kokcu, whose return was credited with lifting Besiktas's passing and tempo, Vincenzo Italiano's side lose their main playmaker; a Hurriyet columnist also flagged their away attacking as the area that still needs work.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Besiktas had about 70% of the ball in the first half against Genclerbirligi and should dominate possession again, which produces corners, while Konyaspor threatened from headers at Samsunspor; I stay near the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. Konyaspor are a side under pressure (Enis Destan had a red card at Samsunspor reduced to a yellow after a VAR check) and Wilfred Ndidi was booked in the second minute last time out, so around five seems right.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.8 shots and I lean higher. Besiktas keep the ball and shoot often, with Trossard and Vlahovic combining for three goals last week, and Konyaspor's low block tends to invite many attempts from outside the box rather than clear chances.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. More shots from distance against a packed defence do not mean many more on target, and Konyaspor rarely trouble keepers, so I keep it near eight.

401888249.overall: Early view: Trabzonspor (2nd, three points behind) have won all six league games under Thomas Reis, the latest 2-0 at Alanyaspor, though they lost 1-0 at home to Freiburg in the Conference League. Eyupspor are bottom with three points and a 3-30 goal difference, and coach Mustafa Dalci admitted after the 2-0 home loss to Kocaelispor that things are not going well. Trabzonspor's long-term absentees include Ruslan Malinovskyi and Batagov.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and I lean slightly higher. Eyupspor have conceded 30 goals in eleven games, including five at Amed, and Trabzonspor have scored 26 while conceding only eight, so the risk is a heavy home win rather than a tight game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Trabzonspor gave Alanyaspor almost no possession last week and should do the same here, so nearly all corners should be theirs; Eyupspor's 3.6 looks high, but Trabzonspor's own share could be bigger, so the total holds.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards and I lean lower. One-sided games like this rarely produce many bookings, and Trabzonspor have little need to foul when they control the ball the way they did in Alanya.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots. I expect Trabzonspor to take well over their 17.2 and Eyupspor fewer than 10.2, since Eyupspor have scored three all season, so the total ends up near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Paul Onuachu, Salah and Muci should test the keeper often against the league's weakest defence, but Eyupspor's own contribution will be small, so I stay close to ten.

401888370.overall: Early view: Basaksehir (8th) under Nuri Sahin have scored seven in their last two games, 5-2 against Samsunspor and a comeback 2-1 at Goztepe with goals from Selke and Edin Visca. Corum (9th) lost 5-0 at home to Fenerbahce before the break, but the club president publicly backed coach Burak Yilmaz, whose side had taken nine points from the previous four games. Corum's Berat Ayberk Ozdemir is out for six to eight weeks with a calf strain.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, which is high but fits these sides: Corum's eleven games have produced 42 goals and Basaksehir's 36. Corum may tighten up after the 5-0, but they scored three at Erzurumspor two weeks earlier, so they will create chances too, and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Basaksehir should have more of the ball at home while Corum look to counter, which fits the 4.9 to 3.8 split, and I have nothing that moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Corum's Gokhan Sazdagi had to sit out the Fenerbahce game after a yellow-card build-up, but this is a Monday-night mid-table game with no rivalry, so I stay near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots and I lean a little higher. Basaksehir's attack is in form, and Corum are more likely to come out and try to answer the heavy defeat than to sit in, which tends to open up both ends.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With both sides scoring freely this season that looks about right, and I would not move it until the lineups are known.

401888241.overall: Early view: a Friday-night meeting of two sides in trouble: Alanyaspor (13th) had lost four straight under Joao Pereira by the break, and Konyaspor (15th, 8 pts) have one of the league's weakest attacks and no away win this season. Both play the weekend before (Alanyaspor at Kasimpasa, Konyaspor at home to Besiktas), so the mood here will depend on those results.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals and I lean lower. These two have scored 15 goals between them in 22 league games, Konyaspor have lost four of their five away games, and Alanyaspor have one goal in their last three, so a nervy, low-scoring game looks more likely than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Alanyaspor should push at home and Konyaspor can be dangerous from crosses (they hit the bar with headers at Samsunspor), so there is no strong reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards and I lean slightly higher. With both sides near the relegation places the tackles will be fierce; Konyaspor picked up two yellows and had a red overturned at Samsunspor, and Alanyaspor's run has left them frustrated.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.5 shots. Neither side creates much at the moment, and Pereira said his team effectively did not turn up for the first half of their loss at Kocaelispor, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. With two blunt attacks I lean slightly lower; Konyaspor have scored six all season, which points to few efforts that really test a keeper.

401888240.overall: Early view: Rizespor (11th) finally won at home on 8 November, 2-1 against Erzurumspor, and coach Recep Ucar hopes it starts a better run; they are without midfielder Can Bozdogan after ankle surgery. Kasimpasa (5th) have lost only once all season and will be in their second league game under Alfred Schreuder, after hosting Alanyaspor.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean slightly lower. Kasimpasa have drawn five of eleven and their games average about 2.5 goals, Rizespor's about 2.6, and a new coach usually starts by making his team harder to beat.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners with Rizespor taking more at home. That fits a home side that has to chase results, and I have nothing that moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. No suspensions or flashpoints are reported for either side, so I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots. I lean lower: Rizespor's 16.3 looks a lot for a side that has scored 13 in eleven, and a Kasimpasa team settling under Schreuder is more likely to keep the game tight than trade chances.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. In line with my lower shots view I expect around eight, with Kasimpasa's Benedyczak and Hajradinovic the most likely to test the keeper.

401888236.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between Samsunspor (17th) and Genclerbirligi (14th). Samsunspor finally won under Nenad Bjelica (1-0 against Konyaspor) but have conceded 26 and are missing Celil Yuksel with a grade 2 muscle injury; they visit Galatasaray the week before. Genclerbirligi's Diabate and Metehan Baltaci, listed as missing here, should have served their one-game bans against Gaziantep, so their status needs rechecking.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I lean slightly higher. Samsunspor have conceded 26 in eleven, including five at Basaksehir, and Genclerbirligi showed in their 5-0 against Alanyaspor that they can score in bunches, while their own defence has let in 21.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Samsunspor at home should do more of the attacking, and nothing in either side's recent games suggests the total is off.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards and I lean higher. Both clubs are fighting relegation, Samsunspor picked up three yellows in their win over Konyaspor, and Genclerbirligi had a man sent off and another banned for yellows in their last game before the break.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots. Samsunspor at home and Genclerbirligi on the counter should make for a fairly open game, which fits the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. With both defences leaky I would not go lower, but neither attack is reliable enough to push it clearly higher, so I stay near nine.

401888368.overall: Early view: Gaziantep (16th) have not won at home all season (two draws, four defeats, three goals scored) and lost six league games in a row before parting with Orhan Ak; a new coach is likely to be in place by then. Amed (3rd) have scored 28 and lost only 4-3 at Galatasaray, and Samuel Ballet, who missed that game through a red-card ban, may be back.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and I lean lower. Amed can score two or three, but Gaziantep have managed three goals in six home games, so the 1.3 expected from them looks high and the total more likely lands around three.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Amed's set-piece threat (six corners at Galatasaray) is balanced by Gaziantep needing to attack at home, so I stay close to the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already a high line. Amed's recent bookings (three at Galatasaray, plus Ballet's ban) and a desperate home side fit that, so I stay with it.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.6 shots, 13.7 of them Gaziantep's. I lean lower because Gaziantep's home attack has barely functioned, and their recent chances have come in short spells rather than sustained pressure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Amed should provide five or so, but I expect fewer from Gaziantep than the 4.4 forecast, so I lean slightly lower.

401888367.overall: Early view: Corum (9th) under Burak Yilmaz play in games full of goals (21 scored, 21 conceded) and were beaten 5-0 at home by Fenerbahce before the break. Kocaelispor (7th) under Selcuk Inan have the opposite profile, conceding only nine in eleven and taking seven points from their last three. Both play the weekend before, Corum at Basaksehir and Kocaelispor at home to Fenerbahce.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and I lean slightly lower. Kocaelispor's games have averaged two goals and they won 2-0 at Eyupspor without conceding, and I expect their organisation to matter more than Corum's open style.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. Corum should have more of the ball at home against a side happy to defend, which fits the split, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. There are no reported suspensions or rivalries here, so I keep it near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots and I lean a little lower. Kocaelispor limit opponents and take few shots themselves, so Corum's 14.1 looks like the ceiling rather than the middle.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Against a well-drilled Kocaelispor back line I expect Corum to struggle for clean chances, so slightly lower.

401888242.overall: Early view: Eyupspor are bottom with one win and three goals in eleven games under Mustafa Dalci, and they are already well adrift. Basaksehir (8th) under Nuri Sahin have won three of their last four, scoring seven in the last two, and host Corum six days earlier.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Eyupspor's expected 1.0 looks high for a side with three goals all season, but Basaksehir's 1.8 looks low against a defence that has conceded 30, so the total stays about the same, mostly from the away side.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Basaksehir should dominate the ball, which pushes their share up and Eyupspor's down, leaving the total close to nine.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and I lean lower. Basaksehir should control the ball and have little reason to foul, and no suspensions or flashpoints are reported for either side.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. I expect more from Basaksehir than 13.2 and fewer from Eyupspor than 11.5, so the total is about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target and I lean slightly lower, because Eyupspor's 4.0 looks generous for a team scoring fewer than one goal every three games.

401888238.overall: Early view: Fenerbahce (6th) are the league's top scorers with 29 and started the Emre Belozoglu era with a 5-0 win at Corum; they are also in the Champions League, where they beat Liverpool 3-2 on 4 November, so midweek rotation is possible. Promoted Erzurumspor (12th) under Serkan Ozbalta have scored ten goals in eleven games and lost their last two. Fenerbahce's absences (Asensio injured, Archie Brown suspended for Corum) need checking nearer the time.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. Fenerbahce's games have averaged about 3.5 and Erzurumspor have conceded 17, so that is fair; Fenerbahce did lose at home to Goztepe on 2 November, a reminder that their home games are not always one-way.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners and I lean higher. Erzurumspor are likely to defend deep, and a Fenerbahce side with wide threats such as Greenwood and Oguz Aydin should force plenty of corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and I lean lower. A home game against a promoted side that will sit back should be fairly calm, with Fenerbahce on the ball for long spells and little reason for either side to make tactical fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, nearly 20 of them Fenerbahce's. That is a lot, but with Greenwood and Irfan Can in form, Lukaku leading the line and Erzurumspor short of attacking threat, it seems right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Fenerbahce's finishing at Corum was sharp and Erzurumspor will give little back, so around ten fits.

401888239.overall: Early view: Trabzonspor (2nd) have won all six league games under Thomas Reis and have the meanest defence (eight conceded), but they are also in the Conference League, where they lost 1-0 at home to Freiburg. Goztepe (10th) under Stoilov won four in a row, including at Fenerbahce, and had won all four home games before Basaksehir beat them 2-1. Monday-night kick-off in Izmir.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Goztepe's games have been high-scoring (41 goals in eleven), but Trabzonspor have conceded only eight, so the two pull in opposite directions and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Trabzonspor usually control the ball, but Goztepe were confident enough at home to beat their first four visitors, so the split should be fairly even.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards. A strong home crowd against a title challenger usually lifts the count, but neither side has a reported discipline problem, so I keep it near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots and I lean lower. Trabzonspor gave Alanyaspor almost no possession and opponents have struggled to create against them all season, so Goztepe's 16.6 home shots look high.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target. Against the league's best defence I expect Goztepe to manage fewer clear efforts than forecast, so slightly lower.

401888237.overall: Early view: the Istanbul derby, with leaders Galatasaray six points clear of fourth-placed Besiktas. Galatasaray's Rafael Leao (muscle strain) is unlikely to play and Victor Osimhen (knee surgery on 7 November) is a doubt, with reports saying his return could take up to five weeks; Galatasaray also play Aston Villa six days earlier. Besiktas will have Orkun Kokcu back from suspension, and Vlahovic and Trossard are in form under Vincenzo Italiano.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and I lean lower. Derbies tend to be tighter than these teams' usual games, and Galatasaray could be without both Osimhen and Leao, two of their main scorers, so I expect a two- or three-goal game rather than a shootout.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. Besiktas like to keep the ball at home (about 70% in the first half against Genclerbirligi) and Galatasaray have width through Baris Alper Yilmaz and Sallai, so ten looks right.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.9 cards, already a high line that reflects the derby. Galatasaray captain Bardakci was shown a red card after their last derby with Fenerbahce, and Sanchez and Sallai go in one booking from a ban if they stay clean against Samsunspor; I would not go higher until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots and I lean slightly lower. Without Osimhen and Leao Galatasaray lose their most frequent shooters, and they will have played Aston Villa six days earlier, which tends to make a derby more cautious.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. In a tighter derby with Galatasaray's front line weakened, I expect fewer clean efforts, so slightly under the number.

401888231.overall: Early view: Galatasaray host Rizespor four days after the Besiktas derby and four days before the Champions League trip to AEK Athens, so rotation is likely. One report expects Rafael Leao back for this game while others say his strain could keep him out for up to six matches, and Victor Osimhen's return from knee surgery should be close by then. Rizespor (11th) have scored only 13 goals and are without Can Bozdogan.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Galatasaray beat Konyaspor 4-0 and Amed 4-3 in their last two league games and Osimhen may be back, but rotation between the derby and AEK, and Rizespor's low-scoring games (29 goals in eleven), keep me on the number rather than above it.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, mostly Galatasaray's. Against a deep Rizespor that fits; the only doubt is how many first-choice wide players Okan Buruk uses between two big games.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and I lean lower. Galatasaray were not booked at all in their last home game against Amed, and against a deep-lying side the cards are more likely to come from Rizespor chasing the ball than from the hosts.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots. Galatasaray will create a lot at home even with changes, as they did with 17 shots against a far stronger Amed side, so I stay near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Aleksey Batrakov's form and a possible Osimhen return support it, while rotation pulls the other way, so I keep it close to the number.

401888232.overall: Early view: a straight relegation fight between Konyaspor and Gaziantep, level on eight points after eleven games. Ilhan Palut called Konyaspor's display in the 1-0 loss at Samsunspor very bad, and Gaziantep went into the break after six straight defeats and the exit of coach Orhan Ak. Both have two more league games first, so the table may look different by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals and I lean lower. Konyaspor have scored six in eleven and Gaziantep two in their last seven, and in a game neither can afford to lose, caution should win out.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Konyaspor at home should attack down the flanks through Arthur Masuaku and Jean-Luc Dompe, but nothing points clearly away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards and I lean higher. A six-pointer at the bottom with both sides under pressure tends to produce bookings, and Konyaspor had Enis Destan sent off at Samsunspor before VAR reduced it to a yellow.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots. These are two of the league's least productive attacks, and neither will want to leave space behind, so I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. Konyaspor hit the bar and missed headers at Samsunspor rather than forcing saves, and Gaziantep have scored twice in seven games, so slightly lower.

401888365.overall: Early view: Amed (3rd) have one of the league's most productive attacks (28 goals) and beat Eyupspor 5-1 in their last home game before the trip to Galatasaray. Alanyaspor (13th) under Joao Pereira had lost four straight by the break and have scored nine all season. Both have two more league games first, including Amed's trip to Gaziantep, so form and team news can shift.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and I lean slightly lower. Amed should score two or three at home, but Alanyaspor's expected 1.0 looks high for a side with one goal in their last three games, so I see about three in total.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners and I lean higher. Amed won six corners even at Galatasaray and are a set-piece threat, so at home against a side that has spent recent games pinned back they should push the count up.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Amed have collected cards recently (three at Galatasaray and Ballet's red-card ban), but nothing is reported about Alanyaspor's discipline, so I stay near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, 17.6 of them Amed's. Hasi's side took 14 shots even at Galatasaray, so a high home total is realistic, and Alanyaspor's 9.4 is already modest.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Amed's forwards Gift Orban and Mbaye Diagne get on the end of plenty of chances, but Alanyaspor will add little, so I keep it close to nine.

401888234.overall: Early view: Basaksehir (8th) are in form under Nuri Sahin, and Fenerbahce (6th) look a different side under new coach Emre Belozoglu, who won 5-0 at Corum in his first game. Fenerbahce are also in the Champions League and come here after a trip to Kocaelispor and a home game with Erzurumspor, so fatigue and rotation are worth watching.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Both sides' games have averaged well over three goals (Fenerbahce 39 in eleven, Basaksehir 36), and Basaksehir scored seven in their last two, so the number looks about right.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, split evenly. Two attacking sides make that plausible, and I have nothing specific that changes it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. An Istanbul game between a big club and an ambitious home side usually has some edge, but no recent trouble between them is reported, so I stay with the number until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots. With both teams scoring freely and Fenerbahce's Greenwood and Irfan Can in form, that seems right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, which fits two of the league's better attacks; I would only move it once lineups and any Champions League rotation are clear.

401888229.overall: Early view: Erzurumspor (12th) host Kocaelispor (7th) in an early Sunday kick-off. Serkan Ozbalta's promoted side have scored ten in eleven and lost their last two before the break, while Selcuk Inan's Kocaelispor have one of the league's best defences, with nine goals conceded. Both have two more league games first, so form may have moved by then.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals, already low, and I agree with it. Kocaelispor's games have averaged two goals and Erzurumspor score less than a goal a game, so I see a tight, low-scoring match.

corners.text: The numbers say 7.9 corners. Neither side builds much pressure in the final third, so a low count fits.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. No suspensions or rivalries are reported, so I stay near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.9 shots and I lean slightly lower. Kocaelispor allow opponents very little (nine goals conceded all season) and Erzurumspor have created little lately, scoring once in each of their last two games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.2 shots on target. That already reflects two careful sides, so I stay with it.

401888230.overall: Early view: Besiktas host Samsunspor six days after the Galatasaray derby. Vincenzo Italiano's side beat Genclerbirligi 3-0 in their last home game before the break, with Vlahovic scoring twice, and Samsunspor (17th) under Nenad Bjelica have conceded 26 goals, including five at Basaksehir. Besiktas are also in European competition, so rotation around this game is possible.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals and I lean slightly higher. Samsunspor's defence is the second-worst in the league, and Besiktas at home have been convincing, with Trossard setting up three goals against Genclerbirligi.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, mostly Besiktas's. That fits how they play at home, holding the ball and pinning teams back, so I keep it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards and I lean lower. Besiktas should control the game, and Samsunspor's one win under Bjelica came from defending deep and organised rather than fouling high up the pitch.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots, 18.7 for Besiktas. That is consistent with their home dominance (about 70% possession in the first half against Genclerbirligi), so I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Vlahovic, with nine league goals, gets plenty of efforts on target, and Samsunspor will add a few, so I keep it near ten.

401888233.overall: Early view: Genclerbirligi (14th) host bottom side Eyupspor, who have three points and a 3-30 goal difference under Mustafa Dalci. Bernd Storck's team showed what they can do at Eryaman with a 5-0 win over Alanyaspor; Diabate and Metehan Baltaci, listed as missing here, should have served their bans in the Gaziantep game, so their status needs rechecking.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and I lean higher. Genclerbirligi's expected 1.5 looks low against a defence that has conceded 30, and they scored five at home to Alanyaspor, so I see them scoring two or more with little coming back from Eyupspor.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Genclerbirligi should do most of the attacking, which fits the 5.6 to 4.1 split, and nothing moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. Genclerbirligi had a red card and a fifth-yellow ban in the Besiktas game, but this should be a game they control, so I stay near four.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.4 shots. I expect more from Genclerbirligi and fewer from Eyupspor than forecast, which roughly cancels out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Genclerbirligi's attackers should test the keeper often, but Eyupspor's 4.0 looks high for a team with three goals all season, so the total stays close to nine.

401888366.overall: Early view: Trabzonspor host Corum six days after visiting Goztepe, with Conference League football still going. Thomas Reis has won every league game since taking over and Trabzonspor have conceded only eight all season; Corum under Burak Yilmaz score and concede freely (21-21) and lost 5-0 at home to Fenerbahce in their last game before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals and I lean lower. Corum's open games push the number up, but Trabzonspor have conceded eight in eleven, so Corum's expected 1.3 looks high and a two- or three-goal home win is more likely than a shootout.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Trabzonspor should have most of the ball at home while Corum counter, so the split looks right and I keep the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. Nothing reported points to a heated game, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots. Trabzonspor at home create plenty and Corum like to attack, so the volume seems fair even if many of Corum's efforts are likely to be low-quality.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. Against the league's best defence I expect Corum to manage fewer than their 4.4, so slightly lower overall.

401888235.overall: Early view: Kasimpasa (5th) have lost once all season and will be about a month into Alfred Schreuder's time in charge; Goztepe (10th) under Stoilov were on a four-game winning run before losing at home to Basaksehir. It is a Monday-night game and both sides have two more league games before it, so this is a first read.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean slightly higher. Goztepe's eleven games have produced 41 goals, and while Kasimpasa's are lower scoring, they drew 2-2 with Besiktas and won 2-0 at Gaziantep in their last two.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Both sides like to attack and the forecast split is even, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. No suspensions or flashpoints are known this far out, so I stay near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots. Goztepe's games are open and Kasimpasa have attacking players in Hajradinovic, Benedyczak and Kerem Demirbay, so the number looks fair.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. That fits two attacks of similar quality, and I would revisit it once Schreuder's approach is clearer.

401879233.overall: Early view: City come out of the break on three straight league defeats under Enzo Maresca, the latest a 3-1 loss at Forest in which Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol were both taken off injured at half-time. Fulham are unbeaten in four league games under Arbeloa, with 1-1 draws at Villa and against Newcastle. City should still have most of the ball, but the fitness of their centre-backs is the team news to watch.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.2 of them for City. I lean a little lower: City have scored once in their last two league games (1-0 defeat to Brighton, 3-1 at Forest), and Fulham's last two matches both ended 1-1. The risk the other way is City's defence, which conceded twice in the first 18 minutes at Forest and may be without Guehi.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, 6.1 of them for City. I lean higher: after three league defeats City should throw men forward at home, and a Fulham side that has been grinding out draws is likely to defend deep and clear plenty of balls behind. Doku taking on full-backs one-on-one is a regular source of them.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, 2.5 of them on Fulham. I lean slightly lower: Fulham were not booked at all in the 1-1 with Newcastle, and a side defending in a settled low block at the Etihad gives away fewer tactical fouls than one that presses. The referee has not been named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots, 16.4 of them City's. I lean slightly higher: City will be desperate to end a three-game league losing run and Fulham are likely to concede possession, which pushes City's attempts up. Antoine Semenyo is out with a knee injury until December, but Haaland and Cherki still give them plenty of shooters.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I lean a little lower: a deep Fulham block gets bodies in front of many efforts, and City's finishing has been off, with one league goal in two games. An early City goal would change the shape of this.

401879238.overall: Early view: Bournemouth are the form team, with four straight league wins and a winning run in all competitions that continued 2-1 at Ipswich, while Forest sit 16th but arrive lifted by a 3-1 win over Manchester City under Glasner, with Liam Delap scoring twice. Bournemouth are without Alex Toth for months and Alex Scott's thigh problem is still being managed.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean slightly higher: Evanilson is scoring for a Bournemouth side that has won its last four league games, and Forest just put three past City with Delap leading the line. Both attacks arrive in better shape than their defences.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners and I see no strong reason to move. Bournemouth's wide men, Tavernier and Kluivert among them, should win their share at home, and nothing in either team's news shifts the balance.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Bournemouth were booked three times in their win at Ipswich, which fits the site's figure, and Forest's position near the bottom keeps their intensity high. Without a named referee I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26 shots. I lean slightly higher: Marco Rose's Bournemouth play at a high tempo and are full of confidence at home, and Forest showed against City that they will commit players forward. Both sides have been scoring freely in their latest games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, which looks about right. Bournemouth's forwards are finishing well, but Forest held City to a single goal at the City Ground, so I do not move from the site.

401878756.overall: Early view: Villa have conceded seven goals in their last two games, losing 3-0 at Barcelona in the Champions League and then throwing away a 4-2 lead in stoppage time in a 4-4 draw at Old Trafford. Sunderland come in after a 1-0 win over Chelsea, but Granit Xhaka limped off early in that game with a suspected calf problem and his fitness is the main team news.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: Villa's defence has leaked seven in two games, while their attack is scoring, with Jackson, McGinn and Goretzka all on target at Old Trafford. Sunderland scored only from a penalty against Chelsea, but Villa are giving chances away to everyone right now.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. I lean a little higher: Villa should have long spells of pressure at Villa Park against a Sunderland side that beat Chelsea by defending a first-half lead, and without Xhaka on the ball Sunderland may spend even more time in their own half.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, 3.1 of them Sunderland's. I lean higher: Sunderland had six names in the book against Chelsea, including manager Regis Le Bris, and Jules Ahoka, who replaced Xhaka, was booked within 20 minutes. A stretched midfield away from home tends to bring more fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, 16.7 of them Villa's. That looks fair: Villa will dominate the ball at home, but Sunderland just held Chelsea scoreless, which pulls the other way. I keep the site's figure until the team news is clear.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: Villa's forwards are finding the target, with four goals at Old Trafford, and Sunderland's back line is missing Dan Ballard with a hamstring injury.

401879236.overall: Early view: Chelsea have lost four of their 10 league games, the latest 1-0 at Sunderland, and Xabi Alonso said afterwards his side lacked patience and quality in the final third. They are still without Joao Pedro, Reece James, Maxence Lacroix and Jamie Gittens. Leeds come in after beating Tottenham 1-0 with a late Noah Okafor goal.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean lower: Chelsea are missing Joao Pedro, Alonso complained about the final-third quality at Sunderland, and Leeds' last two league games ended 1-0 and 0-2. A tight game looks more likely than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Chelsea will have more of the ball and wide players like Estevao and Neto to win corners, but Leeds kept Tottenham out for 90 minutes last time and are not easy to pin back. I stay close to the site.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards. Chelsea were booked four times at Sunderland, which fits the figure, while Leeds had only two bookings against Tottenham. With no referee named yet, I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots, 14 of them Chelsea's. I lean slightly higher: after a defeat that angered Alonso, Chelsea should push hard at Stamford Bridge, and Leeds are likely to let them have the ball and look for chances on the break. Most of the extra volume would come from the home side.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9 shots on target. I lean lower: Chelsea's problem at Sunderland was the quality of their chances rather than the amount of possession, and they are without Joao Pedro. Lots of efforts from outside the box would keep this figure down.

401879235.overall: Early view: a meeting near the bottom, with Palace last after four straight league defeats and a 12-1 aggregate score in them. One report, from the Telegraph via Sports Mole, says Pierre Sage is on the brink and Thomas Frank is favourite to replace him, so Palace may have a new manager by kick-off. Jean-Philippe Mateta's three-match ban covers this game, and Coventry are missing Haji Wright and several defenders.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Palace have scored once in four league games and are without Mateta, which argues for fewer, but they have also conceded 12 in that run and Coventry will treat this as a game to attack. Those pull against each other, so I stay with the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Coventry should have more of the ball at home, but Palace without Ismaila Sarr and Mateta have few outlets to pin Coventry back, and nothing in the news moves the total much.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.9 cards, which looks low for a game between 17th and 20th. I lean higher: points matter hugely for both, Palace may be under a new manager wanting a reaction, and a nervy relegation game is more likely to bring four bookings than two.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, with Palace expected to take 13.5. I lean lower: Palace have one goal in four league games and are without Mateta and Sarr, so their share looks high. Coventry's attack is also missing Haji Wright.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower for the same reasons: Palace's attack has produced one goal in four games, and Coventry are without their main striker, Wright.

401878754.overall: Early view: Tottenham's three-game league winning run ended with a 1-0 defeat at Leeds, and Roberto De Zerbi is still without Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall and Mykhailo Mudryk; one report has Savinho due back for this game. Ipswich, 14th under Gary O'Neil, lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth before the break.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, two of them Tottenham's. I lean lower: Spurs failed to score at Leeds, several creative players are out with knee injuries and James Maddison's fitness has been a worry. Ipswich's last defeat was only a narrow 2-1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, seven of them for Spurs. That fits a De Zerbi side that keeps the ball against an Ipswich team likely to defend deep, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Spurs had Van de Ven, Porro and Tonali booked at Leeds, plus De Zerbi himself, so they are not shy of cards, but Ipswich picked up only two against Bournemouth. With no referee named, I stay with the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, 19 of them Tottenham's. De Zerbi's teams take a lot of the ball, which supports a high count, but the injuries to Simons and Odobert remove two attacking options. The two effects roughly cancel out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Spurs did not score at Leeds and their attack is thinner than usual, so more of their shots may come from distance or be blocked.

401879232.overall: Early view: Arsenal lead the table with five straight league wins, the latest 1-0 over Hull through Martin Odegaard, but Bukayo Saka is out with a quad injury until December and Max Dowman serves the last game of a three-match ban. William Saliba is back after four months out. Newcastle are 12th under Matthias Jaissle, without Joelinton and Tino Livramento, and have won one of their last five.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly lower: Arsenal's recent wins have been tight, they lose a main source of goals with Saka out, and Newcastle have scored once in their last two league games (0-1 against Everton, 1-1 at Fulham).

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Arsenal are likely to have most of the ball, and without Saka their attacks may lean more on crosses and set pieces, while Newcastle will push forward at home. The site's figure looks about right.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Newcastle's last game brought two late bookings for Schar and Dedic, and Jacob Ramsey returns from a one-match ban for two yellows against Everton. Until the referee is known, I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. I lean slightly lower: Arsenal have been controlling games without many chances at either end, as in the 1-0 over Hull, and Newcastle's attack has been thin, with one goal in two league games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. I lean a little lower: without Saka, Arsenal lose their most dangerous wide player, and Newcastle have managed one goal in two games, so neither side is likely to test the keeper often.

401879234.overall: Early view: Brighton are second after a 1-0 win at Manchester City and a 2-0 home win over Brentford, and they are also in the Champions League this season. Hull are 13th with three draws in their last five and a long injury list, including Eliot Matazo, Matt Targett, Charlie Hughes and Hidemasa Morita. Hull held Arsenal goalless until the 72nd minute, and a similar deep plan is likely here.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: Hull kept Arsenal out until the 72nd minute and have drawn three of their last five, and Brighton's two latest league wins both came with clean sheets. A 1-0 or 1-1 kind of game looks likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 5.2 of them for Brighton. I lean slightly higher: if Hull sit deep again, Brighton will spend long spells around the box and win corners from blocked crosses and shots.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards. I lean higher: Hull had six names in the book at the Emirates, and Brighton were booked four times against ten-man Brentford. A side defending deep for 90 minutes against quick passing tends to pick up yellows.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots, 17 of them Brighton's. That looks fair: Brighton will dominate the ball while Hull's own attempts will be few, so I stay close to the site.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: a packed Hull defence blocks plenty, Hull's own threat is limited with Ilyas Ansah injured, and Brighton are without Kaoru Mitoma and Evan Ferguson.

401878755.overall: Early view: Liverpool won 3-1 at Crystal Palace before the break, but their home form is poor, with five points from their Anfield games, and Dominik Szoboszlai is having tests on a knee problem. Manchester United are 18th after a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, and reports say the club will decide Michael Carrick's future during the break, so United could arrive with a new manager. Carlos Baleba is out for a considerable period.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean higher: United's last two games finished 3-2 against Roma and 4-4 against Villa, and Liverpool scored three at Palace through Mac Allister, Wirtz and Isak. Liverpool have also been vulnerable at Anfield, losing 3-0 to City there.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. Liverpool should have more of the ball, but United's recent games have been end-to-end rather than long sieges, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.7 cards, with United expected to take 3.6. The rivalry adds edge and Liverpool had four players booked at Palace, but United had only one booking in the 4-4 with Villa. The two pull against each other, so I stay with the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, a high figure. Both teams' recent games have been open, which supports it, but a possible change of manager at United could make them more cautious at Anfield. I stay with the site for now.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. I lean slightly higher: United have scored seven and conceded six in their last two games, and Liverpool's front players are in form. Both defences look easier to hit than the numbers assume.

401879237.overall: Early view: Brentford lost 2-0 at Brighton after Igor Thiago was sent off in the 23rd minute, and the brief lists him as missing here; I could not confirm the length of his ban. Everton are sixth after back-to-back wins, the latest 3-1 against Coventry with two goals from Thierno Barry, and Moyes has kept Jack Grealish out of the squad for a breach of club discipline.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: Brentford are likely to be without their main striker Thiago and have won one of their last five, and Everton's away win at Newcastle was a 1-0. A tight game suits both sides' current form.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, split fairly evenly. The game looks balanced, as the win-draw-loss numbers suggest, and nothing in the team news shifts that, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Brentford had Ajer and Schade booked as well as Thiago's red at Brighton, while Everton picked up just one booking against Coventry. With no referee named, I stay close to the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. I lean lower: without Thiago, Brentford lose their focal point up front, and Fabio Carvalho and Antoni Milambo were also out before the break. Everton's 1-0 at Newcastle suggests Moyes is happy to keep away games tight.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower for the same reason: Brentford's main finisher is likely missing and Everton have kept their away games tight. Barry's form is the main threat to this view.

401879225.overall: Early view: a Friday night game at the City Ground between a Forest side that beat Manchester City 3-1 before the break and a Chelsea side that lost 1-0 at Sunderland. Chelsea are still without Joao Pedro and Reece James, while Forest have Nicolo Savona and Nicolas Dominguez out. Both play on 21 November first, so this view will change with those results.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, split evenly. Forest found their scoring touch with three against City, led by Delap, but Chelsea's attack has looked short of quality without Joao Pedro. Those cancel out, so I keep the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Chelsea's wide players and Forest's home push should both produce corners, and nothing in the news points either way yet.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. I lean slightly higher: Chelsea were booked four times at Sunderland, including Caicedo and Colwill, and Forest near the bottom will play with intensity in front of a Friday night home crowd.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.1 shots. Forest's win over City showed they can create at home, but Chelsea will likely have more of the ball, so the site's split looks fair. I will revisit it after the 21 November games.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Chelsea's finishing has lacked sharpness without Joao Pedro, but Forest's forwards were clinical against City, so I stay with the site at this distance.

401879227.overall: Early view: Leeds are ninth under Farke after beating Tottenham 1-0, while Coventry, 17th under Frank Lampard, lost 3-1 at Everton and are missing Haji Wright, Aurele Amenda, Josh Eccles and Luke Woolfenden. Both play on 21 November first, so this view will be refreshed.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly lower: Leeds' last two league games ended 1-0 and 0-2, and Coventry's attack is weaker without Wright. A narrow home win fits the site's 1.6 to 0.9 split.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, which looks low. I lean higher: Leeds should have long spells on the ball at Elland Road, and with wide players such as Gudmundsson and James they should win more than five corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards. Leeds had two bookings against Spurs and Coventry one at Everton, which matches a low figure, so I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, 17.9 of them Leeds'. I lean lower: Leeds needed until the 79th minute to score against Spurs, and with Calvert-Lewin's foot problem their attack lacks a regular focal point, so 18 home shots looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. That looks about right for a Leeds side winning narrowly and a Coventry team without its main striker, so I stay with the site.

401879226.overall: Early view: United's situation could look very different by this game, with reports saying the club will decide Michael Carrick's future during the international break, and they visit Liverpool first. Their games have been wild lately, 3-2 against Roma and 4-4 against Villa. Brentford's Igor Thiago is listed as missing after his red card at Brighton; I could not confirm whether his ban runs this long.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. I lean slightly higher: United have scored seven and conceded six in their last two games, and their midfield is without Carlos Baleba for a long spell. United's defending has been the weak point of their season.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, most of them United's. Nothing in the news points either way yet, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. United had only one booking in the 4-4 with Villa, while Brentford collected three cards, including Thiago's red, at Brighton. That evens out, so I stay with the numbers.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.8 shots, 20 of them United's. I lean lower: 20 home shots is a lot for a team in 18th, and Brentford under Keith Andrews are likely to defend and counter. A possible change of manager also adds doubt to how United will play.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. United's recent games have been full of goals, which supports the figure, even if their total shots may come in a little lower. I stay close to the site.

401878752.overall: Early view: Villa arrive at Portman Road with Champions League football on their schedule and a defence that conceded seven in their last two games before the break. Ipswich, 14th under Gary O'Neil, lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth. Amadou Onana remains out for Villa, and both sides play on 21 November first.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, with Villa expected to score 1.8. I lean slightly higher: Villa conceded seven in two games while scoring four at Old Trafford, and Ipswich at home are likely to have a go at a defence that has been leaking.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, split evenly. Villa rotating around Europe could tilt the ball toward Ipswich, but not by enough to move the total yet.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. I lean slightly lower: Ipswich were booked only twice against Bournemouth, and Villa had a single booking in a frantic 4-4 at Old Trafford. Neither side has been collecting cards lately.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.7 shots. Villa's away games in a busy week can go either way, and Ipswich's attack has a goal threat in Jack Clarke, so I keep the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target, which looks fair. Both attacks have been finding the net, Villa at Old Trafford and Ipswich through Clarke, so I do not move.

401879229.overall: Early view: a Merseyside derby between sixth and fourth, with Everton on back-to-back wins and Liverpool holding the most away points in the league. Liverpool are also in the Champions League and face Manchester United the weekend before, and Dominik Szoboszlai's knee is a worry. Everton have been without Jack Grealish for disciplinary reasons.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Liverpool have been far better away than at home, with three goals at Palace, while Everton have won their last two and Thierno Barry is scoring. Both point to goals, but derbies are often cagey, so I stay with the site.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, six of them Liverpool's. That fits Liverpool having more of the ball at Everton's ground, and nothing in the news changes it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. I lean slightly higher: Liverpool had four players booked at Palace, including Ronald Araujo and Alexis Mac Allister, and a derby adds edge on both sides. Five or six bookings would fit.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, a lot for a derby. I lean slightly lower: Everton's last away win was a 1-0 at Newcastle, which suggests Moyes is happy to keep games tight, and Liverpool may be without Szoboszlai.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Isak, Wirtz and Mac Allister all scored at Palace, and Barry is in form for Everton, so the figure looks fair.

401879231.overall: Early view: Brighton are second after a 1-0 win at Manchester City and a 2-0 home win over Brentford, while Newcastle are 12th under Matthias Jaissle and have won one of their last five. Brighton are also in the Champions League, so their squad will be stretched, and Newcastle face Arsenal first.

goals.text: The numbers say 3 goals. I lean slightly lower: Brighton's last two league games were clean-sheet wins, 1-0 and 2-0, and Newcastle have scored only once in their last two league matches.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners. Brighton should have more of the ball at the Amex, but nothing in the news moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Brighton had four players booked against Brentford, though that was a heated game against ten men, and Newcastle had two late bookings at Fulham. I keep the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 27 shots, 17 of them Brighton's. That fits Brighton's control at home, but a Champions League week could bring some rotation, so I stay with the numbers.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Brighton are without Mitoma and Ferguson, which trims their threat a little, but Newcastle are short of bodies too with Livramento and Joelinton out. I stay with the site.

401879230.overall: Early view: Palace are bottom and may have a new manager by then, with one report saying Pierre Sage is on the brink and Thomas Frank is favourite to replace him. Jean-Philippe Mateta's three-match ban covers this game too. Hull are 13th with three draws in their last five and a long injury list.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly lower: Palace have scored once in four league games and will still be without Mateta, while Hull have drawn three of their last five and held Arsenal to a single goal.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, 5.5 for Palace. Palace at home should push, and Hull's deep defending concedes corners, so I keep the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards, 2.6 of them Hull's. I lean higher: Hull had six names in the book at Arsenal, and a home game for a bottom side under this much pressure adds tension. Five bookings would not surprise me.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, 15.7 of them Palace's. I lean lower: Palace's attack without Mateta and Ismaila Sarr has barely produced, and Hull's block limited Arsenal to one goal.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I lean lower for the same reasons: Palace lack a reliable finisher with Mateta banned, and Hull's deep defending blocks a lot of efforts.

401879228.overall: Early view: Bournemouth are seventh and on a long winning run, while Fulham are unbeaten in four league games under Arbeloa. Bournemouth are also in the Europa League, where they beat AC Milan 3-0, so rotation could matter on a Sunday afternoon. Alex Toth is out for months, and Tom Cairney is missing for Fulham.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Bournemouth's attack, led by Evanilson, is scoring well, but Fulham's last two games both ended 1-1, so the two trends cancel out and I keep the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, split evenly. Both sides play with wide forwards, Iwobi and King for Fulham, Tavernier and Kluivert for Bournemouth, and nothing in the news changes the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean slightly lower: Fulham were not booked at all against Newcastle, and Bournemouth's three bookings at Ipswich came in a tight away game. Nothing points to an especially heated meeting.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots. I lean slightly lower: if Bournemouth rotate after European football their tempo may drop, and Fulham's recent games have been tight, with two 1-1 draws.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Bournemouth's forwards are finishing well, but a possibly rotated line-up adds doubt, so I stay with the site.

401879224.overall: Early view: Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 at the Stadium of Light before the break, but they are 19th, also playing in the Europa League, and Granit Xhaka's calf is a concern. Spurs lost 1-0 at Leeds and have a long injury list in attack. Both play on 21 November first, so this view will move with those results.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly lower: Sunderland's home win over Chelsea was a 1-0, and Spurs failed to score at Leeds with Simons, Odobert and Mudryk among the injured.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, 5.2 for Spurs. That fits Spurs having more of the ball away from home, and nothing in the news moves it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. I lean higher: Sunderland had six bookings against Chelsea, including Le Bris, and Spurs had three players and De Zerbi booked at Leeds. Both sides have been running up cards.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots. Sunderland's Europa League commitments may tire legs and hand Spurs more of the ball, but Spurs' injuries limit their attack, so I keep the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: neither attack is firing, with Spurs blank at Leeds and Sunderland's goal against Chelsea coming from a penalty.

401878753.overall: Early view: the leaders, on five straight league wins, host a City side that lost three league games in a row before the break and has worries at centre-back after Guehi and Gvardiol were forced off at Forest. Bukayo Saka is not expected back before December, so he is likely to miss this. Both clubs are in the Champions League, so the midweek before will matter for selection.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean slightly lower: Arsenal have been winning tight games, including 1-0 against Hull, and City have scored once in their last two league matches. Saka's absence also takes goals out of Arsenal's attack.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Both teams like to control the ball and neither will sit back for long, so the site's even split looks fair.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. A top-of-the-table game adds some edge, but Arsenal kept their discipline against Hull, where all six bookings went to the visitors. The referee is not known yet, so I keep the site's number.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. Arsenal without Saka may create a little less, but City's need to respond after their losing run could open the game. I stay with the site.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Saka's absence takes away Arsenal's main wide threat, and City's attack has misfired lately, with one goal at Forest.

401879221.overall: Early view: a game between two promoted sides near the bottom, with Coventry two points above the drop zone and Ipswich only two points better off. Coventry lost 3-1 at Everton without the injured Haji Wright, and Ipswich lost 2-1 at home to Bournemouth with almost no open-play threat beyond Julio Enciso. Both defences leak goals, but nerves and two thin attacks argue for a tighter game than the numbers expect.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean a little lower: Coventry have scored only 10 in 10 games and are without Haji Wright (thigh), while Ipswich made just 0.30 expected goals from open play against Bournemouth. Both defences are poor (19 and 20 conceded), so goals will come, but 3.2 asks a lot of two blunt attacks in a nervy game.

corners.text: The site has 8.2 corners. I lean slightly higher because Ipswich play with wingers like Abdul Fatawu and Jaden Philogene, and Coventry play wide forwards such as Tatsuhiro Sakamoto and Yann Gboho. In a game where both sides need the points, I expect more pressure in wide areas than the figure suggests.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.0 cards. I lean higher: this is a relegation six-pointer between two sides in the bottom six, and Lampard was furious with the officials after the Everton game, which hints at a tense touchline. Low-card estimates usually hold for calm mid-table games, not this kind.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. I lean lower: Ipswich went most of the second half at Portman Road without a touch in the Bournemouth box, and Coventry lose a main striker in Wright. I still expect a fairly open game, but closer to the mid-20s.

shots_on_target.text: The site has 7.8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because both attacks depend on one or two players (Enciso for Ipswich, Yann Gboho and Taiwo Awoniyi for Coventry) and neither creates many clear chances. Around seven feels right.

401879222.overall: Early view: Chelsea under Xabi Alonso were beaten 1-0 at Sunderland and are fifth, while Palace are bottom after four straight league defeats and Pierre Sage is expected to be sacked, with Thomas Frank reported as the leading candidate. Palace also play Real Sociedad in the Europa League on 26 November. A new Palace manager by early December could make them harder to break down, but Chelsea at home are still the clear favourites.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: Chelsea looked blunt at Sunderland and are without Joao Pedro (quad), and a new Palace manager usually starts by tightening the defence. Palace have conceded 24 in 10, so Chelsea should score, but a 2-1 or 2-0 type game fits better than a high-scoring one.

corners.text: The site has 10.8 corners, 6.8 for Chelsea. I lean higher: Palace have conceded six non-penalty set-piece goals, the second-most in the league, so Chelsea will push for corners, and a bottom side defending deep at Stamford Bridge tends to concede a lot of them.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards, most of them for Palace. I agree: a struggling side chasing the ball usually picks up bookings, and Adam Wharton was sent off in the Europa League this month. Nothing in the news points clearly higher or lower.

shots.text: The site has 25.7 shots. I lean slightly higher because Chelsea should have a lot of the ball against the bottom side, and Sage himself says Palace create chances but do not finish them, so they will get some shots too. Mid to high 20s looks likely.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Chelsea lost 63% of first-half duels and produced little at Sunderland, Alonso admitted they 'didn't produce enough', and Joao Pedro is out. Plenty of shots, but fewer on target than the figure.

401879220.overall: Early view: Hull have drawn three of their last five and defended compactly for over an hour in a 1-0 defeat at Arsenal, but key creator Mohamed Belloumi is injured and the squad has a long injury list. Forest, under Oliver Glasner, just beat Manchester City 3-1 with a hard-running pressing game. Two sides separated by two points makes this a cagey, low-margin game.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, and I agree. Hull's games average just over two goals and Belloumi, involved in five of their 11 league goals, has not trained since the Ipswich draw; Forest have scored only nine in 10. Liam Delap's two goals against City are the one sign Forest's attack is waking up.

corners.text: The site has 9.4 corners. I agree: Hull sit deep in a back five and invite crosses, while Forest's wide players like Neco Williams and Dan Ndoye supply them. Nothing points clearly either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. I lean higher: Forest's press, led by Ryan Yates and Xaver Schlager, is built on duels and fouls in midfield, and a close game between two sides near the bottom tends to be scrappy. Four bookings looks more likely than three.

shots.text: The site has 26.9 shots, with 16.9 for Forest. I lean lower: Forest won at the City Ground by running and pressing rather than by piling up shots, and Hull were hard to break down at Arsenal. This looks like a low-chance game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower because Hull are missing Belloumi and several midfielders, including Hidemasa Morita and Darko Gyabi, and Forest have been blunt for most of the season. Around seven on target fits.

401879219.overall: Early view: Liverpool under Andoni Iraola are fourth after winning 3-1 at Palace, but they have scored only four league goals in five games at Anfield and could not land a shot on target at home to Arsenal. Sunderland beat Chelsea 1-0 last time out and play in the Europa League on 26 November. Liverpool should control this, but their home finishing is the big question.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean lower: Liverpool's home attack has been weak, with four goals in five Anfield league games, and Hugo Ekitike is out with an Achilles injury. Sunderland have scored only eight all season, so a 1-0 or 2-0 home win looks more likely than a goal-fest.

corners.text: The site has 9.9 corners. I lean higher: Liverpool tend to camp in the opponent's half (17 efforts against Arsenal), and Sunderland under Regis Le Bris will defend deep at Anfield. Sustained pressure against a low block usually brings plenty of corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I agree: Sunderland will pick up some bookings while defending for long spells, and their physical, intense approach beat Chelsea, but Liverpool should have so much of the ball that they will have little reason to foul. Nothing points strongly either way.

shots.text: The site has 32.4 shots, which is very high. I lean lower: Liverpool will take a lot of shots, but 21.5 for them plus 10.9 for a Sunderland side with eight goals in 10 games is too many. High 20s fits better.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Liverpool forced no saves at home to Arsenal despite 17 efforts, and the analysis of Iraola's side says Isak gets little service. Plenty of shots, but many from distance or blocked.

401879218.overall: Early view: City won their first seven games and then lost three in a row, the last a 3-1 defeat at Forest where Enzo Maresca said they did not match the intensity. Marc Guehi and Josko Gvardiol came off with knocks and City host Napoli in the Champions League on 24 November. Leeds under Daniel Farke are a tight side (10 scored, 8 conceded) who just ended a winless run against Spurs.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly lower: Leeds' games have averaged under two goals, and they defend in a compact back three with James Trafford in good form. City have conceded from transitions lately, but Leeds rarely commit enough men forward to exploit that.

corners.text: The site has 9.5 corners. I lean higher: City will have most of the ball against a deep Leeds block, and the more City are held up, the more they work it wide to Jeremy Doku and others. Corners for City should pile up.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I agree: Leeds can be physical, with Jayden Bogle lucky to escape a red against Spurs, but Leeds will spend most of the game defending in shape and City, with the ball, have less need to foul. Around four is fair.

shots.text: The site has 24.8 shots, only 15.6 for City. I lean higher: after three defeats City will come out hard at home, and a Leeds side that sits deep tends to give up many low-quality shots. City in the high teens looks realistic.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. I agree: more City shots should come, but Leeds block a lot and Haaland may be crowded out. Antoine Semenyo is targeting a return from a knee injury around this time, which would add another threat if he makes it.

401879223.overall: Early view: two of the league's in-form sides. Bournemouth under Marco Rose have won eight straight in all competitions and Evanilson has scored in five league games in a row, while Brighton are second with 26 goals scored and only seven conceded. Bournemouth also play Celta Vigo in the Europa League on 26 November, which adds to an already busy run.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: Brighton average 2.6 goals a game and Bournemouth score freely in a high-intensity style, so both sides should find chances. Brighton's defence is the best in the league on goals conceded, which keeps me from going further.

corners.text: The site has 10.1 corners. I agree: Bournemouth's direct, wide attacks earn corners, and Brighton had almost 80% of the ball in the second half against Brentford, which also pins teams back. Both effects roughly balance the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards. I lean lower: Brighton under Fabian Hurzeler keep the ball for long spells, which limits the stop-start fouling that brings cards, and neither club has a disciplinary problem in the news. A fast, open game between two good sides does not usually produce many bookings.

shots.text: The site has 26.1 shots. I lean higher because both teams want to attack: Bournemouth press and break quickly, and Brighton create a lot even without Kaoru Mitoma and Evan Ferguson. A busy game for both goalkeepers looks likely.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.1 shots on target. I lean higher: Brighton have scored 26 in 10 and Evanilson is in a hot streak, so the chances in this game should be good ones. Nine on target fits better.

401878751.overall: Early view: Villa are 10th and conceded four at Old Trafford, with Amadou Onana and Matteo Ruggeri out, and they host Galatasaray in the Champions League on 24 November. Everton under David Moyes are sixth after wins at Newcastle and at home to Coventry, driven by Thierno Barry's 10 league goals. A compact Everton against a leaky Villa defence is the key contrast.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly higher: Villa have conceded 17 in 10 and let in four goals at Manchester United, while Barry scores almost every week with headers from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's crosses. Moyes' sides are tight, but Villa's defence looks the weaker part of this match.

corners.text: The site has 10.4 corners. I agree: Villa will have more of the ball at home, and Everton work it wide for crosses toward Barry, which keeps corners coming at both ends. Nothing points far from the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, 2.8 for Everton. I agree: Moyes' Everton defend physically and will foul to stop Villa breaks, and Unai Emery's side has been on edge after the 4-4 draw. Around four or five looks right.

shots.text: The site has 28.3 shots. I lean lower: Everton under Moyes keep a low block and limit chances (only 10 conceded in 10), and their own attack is built on a few crosses rather than volume. A mid-20s total fits better.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I agree: Villa's attack with Nicolas Jackson and Alysson is in form after four goals at Old Trafford, and Barry turns chances into shots on target. No clear reason to move.

401878750.overall: Early view: Arsenal lead the league with 27 points from 10 games, seven clean sheets and a string of 1-0 wins, including at Anfield. Brentford lost 2-0 at Brighton after Igor Thiago was sent off by VAR for an arm to the face of Chema; a straight red for violent conduct usually brings a three-match ban, which would rule him out of this game, though I did not find the ban confirmed. Bukayo Saka is out with a quad injury, while William Saliba is back in training.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean lower: Arsenal have scored only 15 in 10 games and won 1-0 in both of their last two league games, and Brentford are likely without Thiago for this one if the standard three-game ban applies. A low-scoring Arsenal win looks most likely.

corners.text: The site has 9.9 corners. I agree: both sides are dangerous from set pieces and will look to win corners, while Arsenal usually have more of the ball. Nothing in the news moves this far.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. I lean higher: Brentford have had two players sent off this season (Yehor Yarmoliuk and Thiago), and Keith Andrews complained that opponents provoked both incidents, which hints at a side that gets drawn into battles. A physical game against the leaders could add bookings.

shots.text: The site has 25.0 shots. I lean lower: Arsenal control games and defend deep when ahead, as they did at Liverpool and Hull, and Brentford without Thiago lose their focal point. Fewer shots than the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.2 shots on target. I lean lower: Arsenal did not allow a single shot on target at Anfield, and they missed the target with big chances against Hull, Mikel Arteta said. Six or so on target fits better.

401879217.overall: Early view: two big clubs in a bad way. Newcastle under Matthias Jaissle were booed off after losing at home to Everton, and Manchester United are in the relegation zone, without a league win since August, with Michael Carrick expected to stay for now. United also play Sporting in the Champions League on 25 November and have a long injury list, including Benjamin Sesko, Marcus Rashford and Carlos Baleba.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I agree: United have conceded more than any side in Europe's top five leagues in all competitions and just drew 4-4 with Villa, which points up, but Newcastle's attack has been flat and their first shot on target against Everton came after 85 minutes, which points down. Those two forces roughly cancel out.

corners.text: The site has 10.0 corners. I agree: Newcastle attack down the flanks with Anthony Elanga and Harvey Barnes, and United will press forward if they fall behind. No strong reason to move the figure.
