shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. Milan had 15 shots against Ferencvaros, so volume is not their problem; quality is, which keeps me close to the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean lower because both sides have been wasteful: Milan put two of 15 shots on target against Ferencvaros, and Sunderland drew few saves in their home loss to Zagreb.

401915488.overall: Early view: Bournemouth have won all four league-phase games, the latest a 3-1 comeback win at Sparta Prague under Marco Rose, and sit level on 12 points with Benfica and Ferencvaros. Viktoria Plzen picked up their first points with a 1-0 win at Lillestrom after three defeats. A home win would push Bournemouth towards a top-eight place.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. Bournemouth scored three in Prague with 20 shots and nine on target, which fits the site's view; Plzen's 1-0 at Lillestrom shows they can keep games tight, so I stay with the number rather than push it higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. I lean higher: Bournemouth won ten corners in Prague, and Plzen are likely to defend deep at the Vitality Stadium, which tends to push the home side's corner count up.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Plzen took four yellows at Lillestrom while Bournemouth had two in Prague, so the mix roughly matches the site's split; nothing points clearly either way until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.3 shots. Bournemouth's 20 shots in Prague and Plzen's 15 at Lillestrom suggest the site's figure is about right.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target. Bournemouth put nine on target in Prague, in line with the home split here; Plzen managed four at Lillestrom, so there is no clear reason to move.

401915492.overall: Early view: Leverkusen lost their unbeaten league-phase record with a 1-0 home defeat to Marseille, and Besiktas, under Vincenzo Italiano, lost 3-2 at Celtic after leading twice. The sides are close in the table (7th and 8th), so both have something to play for in the race for the top eight.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Leverkusen were blunt against Marseille with ten shots and no goal, but Besiktas' 3-2 at Celtic shows their games can open up, so the two pull in opposite directions.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Leverkusen won six corners against Marseille with 58 percent possession, and Besiktas earned seven at Celtic, so nothing points away from the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards. Besiktas picked up two late bookings at Celtic, and the referee for this game is not known yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots. I lean slightly lower: Leverkusen's game against Marseille produced only 18 shots in total, and they tend to keep the ball rather than shoot often.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. Besiktas put four of 15 on target at Celtic; with no team news yet I see no clear reason to move.

401915491.overall: Early view: Benfica top the league phase on goal difference after a 3-1 home win over Lech Poznan, their fourth win from four. OFI Crete are 16th after a 2-0 win over Hapoel Be'er Sheva and could still finish in the play-off places, which gives them a reason to defend carefully in Lisbon.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. Benfica scored three against Lech from 24 shots, while OFI kept a clean sheet against Be'er Sheva, so the site's figure is a fair middle.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners. I lean slightly lower: Benfica created a lot against Lech but won only six corners, and OFI took two in their last game, so the total may not climb as high as the site expects.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Benfica's game with Lech had three yellows and OFI's had four, both close to the site's number; the referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.9 shots. Benfica's 24 shots against Lech and OFI's 11 at Be'er Sheva support a high total, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.1 shots on target. Benfica put 12 on target against Lech on their own, which backs the site's figure.

401915486.overall: Early view: Ferencvaros are unbeaten in 20 games under Balazs Borbely and won 2-0 at San Siro, while Lech Poznan are 35th with one point after a 3-1 defeat at Benfica. The numbers make Lech slight favourites at home, which sits awkwardly with the current form of both sides.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Lech scored at Benfica but conceded three, and Ferencvaros created 3.1 xG at Milan, so there should be chances at both ends; nothing points clearly away from the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners. Lech won three corners at Benfica; with home advantage they should see more of the ball, so I stay near the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Ferencvaros will be without Bamidele Yusuf after his red card at Milan, which two reports confirmed; that does not change much on its own and the referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots. I lean slightly lower: Lech managed only six shots at Benfica, and Ferencvaros' win in Milan came from 12 shots, so neither side has been piling up attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target. Lech's five on target at Benfica from six shots and Ferencvaros' efficiency in Milan point to accuracy rather than volume, so I stay with the number.

401915510.overall: Early view: Levski Sofia have won their last two European games under Julio Velazquez, 2-1 at Viktoria Plzen and 1-0 at home to Jagiellonia, and sit 10th. Lillestrom are 34th with one point after a 1-0 home defeat to Plzen, and need a result to keep play-off hopes alive.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly lower: Levski's last two games ended 1-0 and 2-1, Lillestrom scored none against Plzen with one shot on target, and Levski have been winning tight games.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners. I lean lower: Levski's last two European games had nine and five corners, and Lillestrom's home game with Plzen had nine.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean higher: Levski's win over Jagiellonia had six yellows and Lillestrom's game with Plzen also had six, both above the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Levski's last two games produced 19 and 23 shots in total, which points slightly below the site's number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. I lean lower: Levski's last two European games had five and seven shots on target in total, and Lillestrom managed one against Plzen.

401915485.overall: Early view: Lyon drew 1-1 at Real Sociedad, with Corentin Tolisso scoring, and sit 13th. Union Saint-Gilloise are fourth after a 2-1 win at Celta Vigo, where Besfort Zeneli scored twice, and are pushing for a top-eight place.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Both teams' last games ended with three goals or fewer, and nothing in the news points clearly either way.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lyon took six corners at Real Sociedad; Union won only one at Celta while sitting deeper, which fits the site's home-heavy split.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards. I lean higher: Lyon picked up four yellows at Real Sociedad, and Union's style of defending deep and countering tends to bring fouls. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Lyon's game in San Sebastian had 23 shots and Union's in Vigo had 28, which brackets the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Lyon's last game had eight on target in total and Union's had seven.

401915489.overall: Early view: Both sides are on four points and in poor form: Salzburg lost 2-0 at Anderlecht and Sparta Prague lost 3-1 at home to Bournemouth after Tobias Guddal's red card. Both need points to stay in the play-off race, which should make this an open game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Salzburg failed to score in Brussels with three shots on target, but Sparta conceded three at home, so the two weaknesses roughly cancel out.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Salzburg's game at Anderlecht had nine corners in total; nothing points clearly away from the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. I lean higher: Salzburg committed 20 fouls and took three yellows at Anderlecht, and Sparta had a player sent off and two more booked against Bournemouth, with Guddal now suspended.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots. I lean lower: Salzburg managed only eight shots at Anderlecht despite more of the ball, and their game had 20 shots in total.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Salzburg's game at Anderlecht had ten on target and Sparta's with Bournemouth had 12, so I stay with the number.

401915490.overall: Early view: Real Sociedad drew 1-1 with Lyon and sit 20th with five points, so a home win over Torreense matters. Torreense beat Ararat-Armenia 3-2 with two stoppage-time goals despite playing most of the game with ten men after Jorge Aguirre's red card, and will be without him here.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, which looks high. Real Sociedad scored once from 11 shots against Lyon, and while Torreense concede chances, a total above four needs a lot to go right for the home side.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.1 corners. Real Sociedad took five corners against Lyon, but a deep-sitting Torreense side at Anoeta should give them more; I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards. Real Sociedad picked up three yellows against Lyon, and Torreense's game with Ararat had a red card and eight yellows, so the high figure is supported.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots. I lean slightly lower: Real Sociedad took only 11 shots against Lyon, and Torreense's last game had 31 shots mostly because Ararat had an extra man for over an hour.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Torreense's game had 13 on target in total, though helped by the man advantage; nothing else points clearly either way.

401915795.overall: Early view: AGF are still looking for a first league-phase win (lost 1-0 at Gent, 1-1 with Egnatia, 0-0 with Braga), while John van den Brom's Twente have won all three (1-0 Thun, 4-1 Lincoln, 3-1 Pafos). Twente need the points to stay in the top eight, AGF need them to get into the top 24. No injury news for this game yet; it is refreshed with team news the day before.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: AGF have scored two goals in three European games and kept Braga out in a 0-0, and Twente dominated possession against Pafos but struggled to create in the first half before winning 3-1 against ten men.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, with Twente taking most of them. Twente's control of the ball should push AGF back and win corners, which fits the estimate, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Nothing in the news points to a heated game or a strict referee yet; the referee is not known, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots, nearly 23 of them from Twente. That is a lot for an away side; Twente's first half against Pafos was slow for clear chances and AGF created the better first-half openings against Braga, so I lean a bit lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. AGF goalkeeper Mads Hedenstad was busy against Braga and Twente have Wout Weghorst and Daouda Weidmann testing keepers, so I see no reason to move off the estimate.

401915732.overall: Early view: a meeting of two unbeaten sides near the top. Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton have 7 points (4-0 Kauno Zalgiris, 0-0 at Jablonec, 1-0 at Getafe) and Monaco have won all three (2-1 at CSKA Sofia, 3-0 Freiburg, 2-0 Nordsjaelland). The site makes Brighton strong favourites, but Monaco's form says this should be closer than that.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals. I lean lower: Brighton have kept clean sheets in 10 of their 13 European games and found it hard to break down Jablonec and Getafe, while Monaco have conceded once in three games and won at home against Nordsjaelland with few chances in a cagey first half.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, most for Brighton. With Brighton at home and likely to have more of the ball, that split looks fair and I have nothing to move it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. The referee is not known yet and neither side has shown a discipline problem in the competition, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, with Brighton on 19. Brighton had plenty of efforts at Getafe (Jaouen Hadjam hit the woodwork twice) but Monaco are a stronger side than the 8.4 shots they are given suggests, so the total looks about right even if the split is more even.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: in their last European games Brighton needed one goal and a lot of misses at Getafe, and Monaco needed only one shot on target to go ahead against Nordsjaelland.

401915629.overall: Early view: Egnatia, who lead the Albanian league, drew their first two games (1-1 with Midtjylland and at AGF) and then lost 2-0 at Universitatea Craiova with ten men. Kauno Zalgiris are bottom with no points, one goal scored and eleven conceded. Egnatia need a win to stay in the race for the top 24.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean a little lower: Egnatia have scored two goals in three games and sat in a five-man defence at Craiova, and Kauno Zalgiris have scored once in three games. Kauno do leak goals (4-0 at Brighton, 1-4 v Brann, 3-0 at Lugano), so Egnatia should score, but not freely.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners, more for Egnatia at home. Nothing in the reports points away from that, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Eneo Bitri was sent off at Craiova after reacting to provocation, and Kauno picked up two bookings at Lugano, so cards are a real feature, but the estimate already covers that. On Bitri: if it was a one-match ban he should serve it against Lincoln on 26 November, so he may be back here; that needs checking nearer the game.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots, with Egnatia on 16. Egnatia should have more of the ball at home than they did in Romania, and Kauno started brightly at Lugano before fading, so I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I found nothing that moves it either way, so the view rests on form here.

401915794.overall: Early view: Thun, coached by Gian-Luca Privitelli, got their first league-phase win by beating Hearts 3-1 on their artificial pitch after defeats to Twente and Hajduk. Rik De Mil's Gent have won once in their last five games and drew 0-0 at KuPS. Both sides sit mid-table and need points for the top 24.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean a little lower: Gent have not scored away in the league phase (0-2 at Braga, 0-0 at KuPS), though Thun's Brighton Labeau and Furkan Dursun both scored against Hearts, so a home goal is likely.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Gent's best moments at KuPS came from Hyllarion Goore's runs down the right, which can win corners, but nothing points clearly off the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. The referee is not known and there is no history of bad feeling between the clubs, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots. Gent had no shots on target in the first half at KuPS but dominated after the break, and Thun take their chances at home, so nothing moves me off the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Gent have been short of quality in the final third and Thun were sharp against Hearts; those roughly cancel out, so I stay with the estimate.

401915792.overall: Early view: Hajduk beat Ajax and won at Thun, then lost 1-0 in Gibraltar to Lincoln Red Imps, with no shot on target until the 85th minute. Nordsjaelland are winless in Europe (two draws and a 2-0 loss at Monaco) but scored six at Randers in the league on 8 November. Hajduk are on six points and one more win would put them close to the top 24.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. Hajduk were blunt in Gibraltar and missed Adrion Pajaziti, Leander Dendoncker, Roko Brajkovic and goalkeeper Ivica Ivusic, while Nordsjaelland managed one attempt at Monaco but score freely at home in Denmark. Those pull in different directions, so I stay with the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. Nothing in the reports points away from that, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, already high, which fits a loud Poljud and a home side under pressure after the Lincoln defeat. The referee is not known yet, so I do not push it higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. Hajduk took plenty of long-range shots through Dalisson in Gibraltar, which keeps shot counts up even when chances are poor, so I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Hajduk had one shot on target in 90 minutes against Lincoln, with Dalisson and Soticek missing the target, and Nordsjaelland did not test Lukas Hradecky at Monaco.

401915793.overall: Early view: Hearts have one point from three games and lost 3-1 at Thun with ten players injured, captain Stephen Kingsley going off hurt as well. Wouter Vrancken said a league game mattered more than the next European tie, a sign of where Hearts' priorities are. Borac beat KuPS at home but lost at Panathinaikos and Mjallby, and have lost 14 of their last 20 European away games.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Hearts have conceded seven in three European games and their defence is stretched by injuries, but Borac were muted after going behind at Mjallby and rarely score away. I stay with the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, seven of them for Hearts. Hearts at Tynecastle should have territory against a Borac side that struggles away, so the split makes sense even with a weakened squad.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Borac started aggressively at Mjallby, but there is nothing on the referee yet, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.4 shots. Borac took several long-range shots early at Mjallby without testing the keeper, and Hearts should be on the front foot at home, so the estimate looks fair.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. How many of Hearts' injured players return by December matters most here; until that is known I stay with the estimate.

401915628.overall: Early view: Mjallby are unbeaten in Europe (2-0 Inter Escaldes, 1-1 at Iberia, 2-0 Borac), the first Swedish side since Ostersund in 2017 to do that in the first three main-draw games. Pafos are on a six-game winless run and lost 3-1 at Twente after Lele's goal and later red card. A win would all but put Mjallby in the top 24.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals, already low. Nine of Mjallby's last 11 competitive games had fewer than three goals and they won 2-0 against Borac with a goal from a defensive error, so I agree with a low total.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, mostly for Mjallby at home. Their best first-half chance against Borac came from a corner (an Axel Noren header), so set pieces matter for them, but nothing moves the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. Lele was sent off for a second booking for a cynical foul at Twente; that one-match ban should be served against Midtjylland on 26 November, so he is likely back here. The referee is not known, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots. Mjallby did not dominate the first half against Borac and are patient rather than shot-heavy, but they have the home edge, so I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. I found nothing that moves it either way.

401915630.overall: Early view: Sint-Truiden are unbeaten in the league phase (2-0 Iberia, 1-0 at Midtjylland, 1-1 Brann) and have conceded once. Ajax lost at Hajduk on the first night but then beat Atalanta 2-0 and won 6-1 at Midtjylland, with Tolu Arokodare scoring twice. Little recent Sint-Truiden news was found, so their side of this view rests on results.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Ajax are scoring freely under Michel, but Sint-Truiden have let in one goal in three games; those cancel out, so I stay with the estimate.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners. Nothing in the news points either way, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. The referee is not known and there is no history between the sides, so I stay with the estimate.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with Ajax on only 12. I lean a little higher: Ajax created a lot in their last two European games and now have Arokodare, Oscar Gloukh and Marcos Leonardo all scoring, which should lift their share. They were without Sofyan Amrabat and Julian Brandt at Midtjylland, and Kasper Dolberg hurt his knee in October.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target. Ajax's finishing has been sharp, but Sint-Truiden have kept things tight, so I stay with the estimate.

401888364.overall: Early view: a meeting of two first-time Süper Lig sides. Amed SFK under Besnik Hasi are 3rd and only had an eight-match unbeaten run ended by a 4-3 defeat at Galatasaray on 7 November; Çorum FK took 9 points from Burak Yılmaz's first four games after he replaced Uğur Uçar in late September, then lost 0-5 at home to Fenerbahçe. Team news is a month off and this view will be refreshed nearer kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.6 goals, which is very high. Çorum's five league games under Burak Yılmaz (3-0, 2-1, 0-2, 3-1, 0-5) averaged 3.6 goals, and Amed's goals against were low early in the season before the 4-3 at Galatasaray. I expect goals, but nearer three or four than five.

corners.text: The numbers say 8 corners, split evenly. I found nothing on either side's wide play or set-piece habits that points away from that, so I stay with the site's figure for now.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards. The referee is not known yet and there is no derby or bad blood between these promoted clubs that I could find, so I stay level until the appointment is out.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.6 shots. Both teams play openly, Amed having scored three at Galatasaray and Çorum three on two of their away trips under Yılmaz, which fits a busy game, but nothing I read points clearly above or below the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. With attacking players like Cengiz Ünder and Moukoko scoring for Çorum and Amed finding the target freely in Istanbul, I stay close to the site's number until team news is known.

401884704.overall: Early view: Hamburg have turned their season around under Merlin Polzin after losing their first three games, swapping possession play for a compact, low-possession set-up, though captain Nicolai Remberg is out long term after ACL surgery. Schalke sit 17th, lost in Hoffenheim on 8 November after a Loris Karius error, and lost Robin Gosens to a knee injury and Timo Becker to a foot injury; this is refreshed with team news the day before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.0 goals. I lean slightly lower: Hamburg under Polzin have won games with around 35-37% possession and tight margins (1-0 against Stuttgart), and Schalke have scored little lately (0-0 at Köln, 0-2 at home to Leipzig, one late goal at Hoffenheim).

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners with Hamburg taking most of them. I lean a little lower because Polzin's Hamburg have been happy to sit compact without the ball, which tends to limit their own corner count at home against a side that may need to attack.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. Schalke's position near the bottom adds some edge, but there is no referee named yet and nothing in the news points clearly up or down, so I stay with the number for now.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.5 shots. Hamburg's low-possession approach and Schalke's blunt recent attack both suggest a slightly quieter game than that, so I lean a touch lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. With Schalke scoring once in their last three league games and Hamburg winning tight, low-margin games, I lean a little lower.

401874775.overall: Early view: Udinese are bottom with 5 points, sacked Kosta Runjaic on 2 November after one point from eight games, and lost 2-1 at Venezia in Paolo Zanetti's first game. Frosinone are 6th and in form, with Antonio Raimondo among Serie A's top scorers after the 5-1 win over Lecce; Gabriele Bracaglia is banned. This is refreshed with team news the day before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, which is already high. Frosinone's direct, wide attacking (five against Lecce) and Udinese's leaky run support goals, but a new coach like Zanetti usually tightens the defence first, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, split evenly. Frosinone use wide attackers a lot, which can push their share up, but Udinese at home under a new coach should also push forward, so I see no clear reason to move off the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards. I lean higher: Udinese are in a relegation fight under a new coach and will be chasing points at home, and Frosinone already have a player (Bracaglia) out on a five-yellow ban, which hints at a side that picks up bookings.

shots.text: The numbers say 36.4 shots, which is very high for a Serie A game. I lean lower simply because that is far above normal, and Zanetti's first job at Udinese is likely to be making them harder to play through.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target. Frosinone have been clinical, with Raimondo on eight league goals by late October, but I trim nothing firm until team news is in, so I stay with the number.

401876375.overall: Early view: Auxerre are 14th and lost 1-0 at home to Paris FC on 7 November, with a Cameron Archer goal ruled out and Kevin Trapp denying Archer later on. Toulouse are 12th and beat Strasbourg 3-1 on 6 November, with two goals coming from corners. I found little team news yet, so this rests mostly on form and is refreshed the day before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. I lean slightly lower: Auxerre were held scoreless at home by Paris FC and their attack leans heavily on Archer, while two mid-to-lower sides with little separating them often produce a cagey game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Toulouse won seven corners against Strasbourg and scored twice from set pieces, but one game is not enough to move off the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. The Toulouse-Strasbourg game had plenty of fouls and a confrontation involving Tapé, but with no referee named yet I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.4 shots. Toulouse had only 10 shots against Strasbourg even while winning 3-1, which fits an efficient rather than high-volume side, so I lean a touch lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target. Toulouse put 5 of 10 on target in their last game, which offsets the lower shot volume, so I stay with the number.

401885375.overall: Early view: two of the surprise packages meet level on 20 points. Promoted Académico de Viseu, coached by Bruno Pinheiro, have had a historic run in their first top-flight season in 37 years with keeper Ewerton and striker André Clóvis key, and draw some of the league's best crowds at the Fontelo. Arouca under Vítor Severino lost late at Famalicão before the break after wins over Alverca and Nacional; this is refreshed with team news the day before kick-off.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Both sides are in good form and attack with intent, but Viseu's goalkeeper Ewerton has been making a lot of saves, so nothing points clearly either way yet.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners. Viseu like to play out from the back rather than go wide and long, which fits a modest corner count, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards, which is high. I lean slightly lower: there is no particular rivalry here and both sides are comfortable in the table, though Arouca did have a player sent off against Alverca, so this is a mild lean only.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots with Arouca taking more. Ewerton was averaging about 4.5 saves a game early in the season, which suggests Viseu do allow shots, so the number looks reasonable.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Nothing in the news moves this yet, so I stay with the number until team news arrives.

401888221.overall: Early view: Erzurum, back in the top flight after six years, started well but have lost their last two, while 5th-placed Kasimpasa have lost once in 11 games. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.7 shots on target. Neither side has much cutting edge, which matches the low figure, so I stay with it.

401883092.overall: Early view: Córdoba (11th) under Iván Ania play open games (22 scored, 22 conceded) and have improved recently, with Percan their main scorer on six goals. Second-placed Castellón under Pablo Hernández have the best defence in the league (5 conceded in 12) and a game in hand against Eibar that was postponed after the death of Jesús de Miguel and still has no date, which could add December fixtures. Matías Orozco's ban from his red card will be served well before this date.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Córdoba's matches are open, but Castellón have let in only five all season, so I lean a little lower and expect something closer to two or three goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. Córdoba at home should push forward and Castellón are comfortable defending, which fits the number, so I have no reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.2 cards. That is already a high figure and the referee is not known yet, so I stay with it.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.9 shots. Córdoba create plenty at home and Castellón's attack, with Adam Jakobsen and Orozco, is one of the best, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Castellón's defence and goalkeeper Romain Matthys have kept most sides to very few clear chances, so I lean slightly lower.

401883091.overall: Early view: fourth-placed Eibar (23 pts from 12) host seventh-placed Sporting (22 pts from 13) in a play-off-race game. Eibar's league game at Castellón and their Copa del Rey tie in Pamplona were both postponed, so they may face a crowded December. Sporting under Nicolás Larcamón have had a long injury list (seven out in early November) and Juan Otero's red-card ban should be served long before this match.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Eibar score well at Ipurua (21 in 12) while Sporting have scored only 14 all season, so a moderate total fits and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Nothing in the news points either way, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. Sporting have the most yellow cards of the two by a distance (37 to Eibar's 24), and with play-off places at stake I lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.8 shots. Both sides have taken almost the same number of shots this season (121 and 122), and I see no reason to move away from the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. Iván Gil and Gorka Guruzeta lead Eibar's scoring and Sporting's goals are spread thin, so I stay with the number.

401882289.overall: Early view: a relegation-zone game between Eldense (15th) under Javi Calleja and Andorra (19th) under Carles Manso. Andorra's goalkeeper Jesús Owono was sent off after the collision in which Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel was fatally injured, and the club has had a hard month; the bans listed for Owono, Lautaro De León, Efe Akman and Eldense's Juan Larios should all be served before mid-December. Eldense have struggled to score (Jorge Rastrojo top scorer with three) while Andorra's games are open.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Andorra's matches average over three goals but Eldense have scored only 13 in 13, so the two pull in opposite directions and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Under Calleja Eldense keep the ball and push players into the box late on, and Andorra push their lines high, so I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.5 cards. It is a game between two sides near the bottom, but no referee is known yet, so I stay with the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.1 shots. Eldense took 13 shots with 59% of the ball against Granada and Andorra leave space, so I lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Eldense's finishing has been poor, which offsets the volume, so I stay with the number.

401883090.overall: Early view: Granada under Pacheta had won five league games in a row (15 of 15 points) going into November, with efficient counter-attacks rather than control of the ball. Girona under Quique Álvarez score freely at Montilivi but have been missing Bryan Gil, Javi Boñar and Jastin García with no return dates given, and lost at Real Sociedad B after an early red card. The numbers favour Girona, but Granada's form makes this closer than that.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Granada win tight games and Girona have both a strong attack and a shaky defence, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners. Granada are happy without the ball, which keeps corner counts down, and that is already in the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. Nothing in the news points either way and the referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Granada beat Eldense with only 8 shots and let opponents have the ball, so I lean slightly lower on total shots.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Granada make few but good chances and Girona create a lot, so I stay with the number.

401883301.overall: Early view: Las Palmas are on their third coach of the season, Albert Sánchez, who arrived from Dunkerque at the end of October after Rubén de la Barrera left and an interim spell; results have picked up (last five LLWWW). Celta Fortuna (16th) had lost four straight away from Balaídos and arrived at Burgos with five injured players. The three yellow-card bans in the brief will be long served by mid-December.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. Las Palmas have conceded 21 and Celta Fortuna 25, so both defences leak, which fits a high total; I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Celta Fortuna tend to drop deep once ahead or under pressure, and Burgos forced 10 corners to 1 against them, so I lean higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards. Nothing in the news points either way and the referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.8 shots. Burgos had 19 shots to 6 against Celta Fortuna in November and Las Palmas should have most of the ball at home, so I lean a little higher.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Las Palmas's finishing under a new coach is still an open question, so I stay with the number.

401883089.overall: Early view: a relegation game between two clubs with new coaches. Leganés (18th) appointed Luis Carrión in October to replace Rubén Albés and had not won since 20 September; Ceuta (22nd, 5 pts, 30 conceded) replaced José Juan Romero with Sergio Lobera on 8 November after a 3-0 loss at Córdoba. Francisco Montero's ban from the brief should be served long before this match.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Ceuta have the worst defence in the league but Leganés have scored only 11 all season, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Leganés had nearly two-thirds of the ball against Albacete, which fits the figure, and nothing else points either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards. A direct relegation game between two sides at the bottom, both trying to show a reaction for new coaches, makes me lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.2 shots. Leganés took 17 shots against Albacete and Ceuta concede plenty, so a high total fits and I stay with it.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.5 shots on target. Leganés's finishing, led by Álvaro Morata, has been poor, which offsets Ceuta's weak defence, so I stay with the number.

401883088.overall: Early view: Mallorca (6th, 15 scored, 7 conceded) under Luis García are hard to beat at Son Moix, with Adrián Fuentes scoring seven of their 15 goals. Burgos (3rd) under Sergio Francisco have the best home record in the division but have taken far fewer points away. Mallorca's league game at Andorra was postponed and still needs a date, which could crowd their December.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.8 goals. Mallorca concede very little and Burgos are much less dangerous away than at El Plantío, so a low total fits and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Mallorca attack down the flanks with crosses from Álex Sala and Zito Luvumbo and kept up pressure on Cádiz until late, so I lean slightly higher.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards. Sergi Darder was close to a red against Cádiz, but nothing else points either way and the referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.2 shots. Mallorca should have most of the ball and Burgos will look to stay compact away, which fits the figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.5 shots on target. Nothing in the news points either way, so I stay with the number.

401882288.overall: Early view: Real Oviedo (9th) under Julián Calero won 2-1 at Cádiz in November with Estanis Pedrola and Ilyas Chaira back from injury, but have taken most of their points away (13 of 21) rather than at the Tartiere. Striker Chris Ramos is out for at least the rest of the calendar year with a torn cruciate ligament, and Dani Calvo went off injured at Cádiz with no timeline yet. Real Sociedad B (17th) under Jon Ansotegi are a young side fighting relegation.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Oviedo lose Chris Ramos's goals, but Real Sociedad B have conceded 22, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.4 corners. Nothing in the news points either way, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards. Real Sociedad B committed 27 fouls and took six yellow cards against Girona, a sign of how this young side defends, so I lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.2 shots, which looks high. Oviedo have been less convincing at home than away and are without Chris Ramos, so I lean lower while still expecting a busy game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Nothing in the news points either way, so I stay with the number.

401883087.overall: Early view: Real Valladolid (12th) under Fran Escribá score freely at the José Zorrilla (5-0 against Albacete, 4-3 against Leganés) but were missing Juanmi Latasa, Guille Bueno, De Rooij and Dani Pérez in November with no return dates given. Tenerife (14th) under Álvaro Cervera are drawing a lot (LDDDD) and are dealing with the death of striker Jesús de Miguel after the match against Andorra. The bans listed for Iván Alejo and Dani Martín should be served before mid-December.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Valladolid's home games have been high-scoring and Escribá expects open matches, so I lean slightly higher despite Tenerife's run of draws.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Nothing in the news points either way, so I stay with the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards. Nothing in the news points either way and the referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. Cervera likes three central midfielders to keep games tight, which fits a moderate total, so I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Whether Latasa is back will matter for Valladolid, so this is one to revisit with team news.

401874821.overall: Early view: two of the league's form sides meet in a top-eight game. Como (5th, Cesc Fabregas) won six in a row before a 2-0 defeat at Inter, and play in the Champions League at Real Betis on Wednesday 9 December, three days before this. Bologna have won five straight under Raffaele Palladino, who took over mid-season, and have no European game that week.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Both sides are scoring and winning, but Como may rotate after the trip to Seville and Bologna's recent wins were mostly narrow (2-1 against Monza and Parma), so nothing pushes this away from the site's figure.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners. Bologna under Palladino push teams back: they had 69% of the ball and 33 shots at Parma, albeit against ten men, and a fresher Bologna should keep pressing a Como side coming off a midweek away game, which tends to produce corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. There is no derby edge or known referee yet, and neither side has a recent discipline story, so I stay with the site's number until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.7 shots. Bologna's shot volume has been very high in their winning run and Como create a lot at home, so I lean slightly higher, with the caveat that Fabregas may rotate after the Betis game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.9 shots on target. More shots do not always mean more on target, and Bologna had 10 on target from 33 attempts at Parma, so I keep this one level.

401875007.overall: Early view: a Rome derby between the top three, with Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio (1st, unbeaten, best start in their history) hosting Gian Piero Gasperini's Roma (3rd, also unbeaten in the league). Roma play Sporting in the Champions League on Tuesday 8 December, while Lazio have no European games. One report says Lazio ultras are boycotting home games in protest at owner Claudio Lotito, which could change the usual derby atmosphere.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. With top spot at stake, I expect a cagey game: Lazio faded and settled for 1-1 at Napoli after going ahead, and both sides have plenty to lose here. Roma's attack has been prolific (5-2 at Udinese), so this is a mild lean, not a strong one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners. Lazio attack down the flanks through Isaksen and Noslin, but Nuno Tavares and Zaccagni were injured in early November and their availability is unclear, so I stay with the site's number for now.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.9 cards, already high because it is a derby. The stakes support a busy card count, but the referee is not known yet, so I keep to the site's figure.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots. Roma's Gasperini style produces lots of shots, but a tight, high-stakes derby can cut that, so these two points balance each other out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. If the game is as cagey as I expect, clear chances should be rarer, and Roma were missing Paulo Dybala to injury in October, with no update found since.

401874766.overall: Early view: Cristian Chivu's Inter (2nd, one point off the top) should be strong favourites at home to mid-table Torino. The main question is rotation, since Inter play at Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Wednesday 9 December. Torino under Ignazio Abate press high but have been caught on second balls and in transition.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Inter's counter-attacking (they beat Como 2-0 by breaking quickly) suits Torino's high press and weak transitions, but some rotation after Dortmund could take the edge off, so I stay close to the site's figure.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Inter should have most of the ball, but Chivu's side has scored on the break rather than through long spells of pressure, so I have no reason to move off the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.7 cards, which is low. Abate has said he wants Torino to be 'dirtier' and read the game better, he took off two booked players against Frosinone, and a pressing side chasing the game at San Siro tends to collect fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots. Inter's home dominance supports a high total, but rotated legs after Dortmund could lower the tempo, so I stay with the site's figure.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Inter have been clinical (Pio Esposito and Thuram against Como), but nothing in the news moves this either way yet.

401874761.overall: Early view: a relegation six-pointer between 16th-placed Parma (8 points) and 15th-placed Fiorentina (9 points), neither of whom has a European game that week. Alberto Gilardino's Parma won 3-0 at Atalanta but then lost 2-1 to Bologna after Abdoulaye Ndiaye was sent off in the 9th minute. Fiorentina drew 2-2 with Juventus to climb out of the bottom three.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Stakes like these often make for nervy games, but Fiorentina have been scoring (Alieu Njie has three in three games) and conceding from errors, so I stay with the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners. Fiorentina scored from a corner against Juventus and conceded from one, but nothing suggests the count itself will be unusual.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Two struggling sides with a lot to lose should mean more fouls and stoppages, and Parma were reduced to ten men last time out. Ndiaye's ban for denying a goal-scoring chance should be served long before this match, so it does not affect the lineup here.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.5 shots, which looks high for two low-scoring bottom-half teams. Parma defended deep and managed 11 shots against Bologna, and Gilardino's side tends to play on the counter, so I lean lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Parma may be without goalkeeper David Romero, who appeared to dislocate a shoulder against Bologna, but there is no confirmed timeline, so I keep this level for now.

401875028.overall: Early view: Massimiliano Allegri's Napoli (10th, winless in three) host Ruben Amorim's Milan (4th) on a Sunday night. Napoli have had an injury crisis, including muscle problems for Di Lorenzo and Olivera in early November, and play Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday 8 December. Milan host Sunderland in the Europa League on Thursday 10 December, so they will have only three days to recover.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Allegri has switched to a back three to cope with injuries, Napoli have won only two of their last eight games, and Milan arrive on short rest after a Thursday game, so I lean lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Napoli's wing-backs push on in Allegri's 3-4-2-1, but Milan's quick turnaround makes the game's shape hard to read this far out, so I stay with the site's number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, which is low for a big game between two clubs under pressure. Napoli had Luca Marianucci sent off at Juventus, and a tired Milan side may have to foul more to slow Napoli down at the Maradona.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots. Milan's legs after the Sunderland game and Allegri's cautious approach point to a slower game with fewer attempts.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. For the same reasons I expect fewer clear chances, though De Bruyne and Hojlund being fit for Napoli by then would change this.

401876376.overall: Early view: two sides near the bottom, Angers 16th on 8 points and Strasbourg 13th on 10, so this is close to a relegation six-pointer. Angers have scored only 9 goals in 10 games and lost 0-2 at home to Nice last time out, while Strasbourg's games have been open (18 scored, 22 conceded) and reports say the club is worried about Hugo Oliveira after three wins in ten. Neither side is in Europe, so both should be fresh.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Angers struggle to score but Strasbourg's young side leaks goals (22 conceded, a 5-1 win and a 4-0 defeat in the same autumn), so the two pull in opposite directions. Nothing clear points away from the number a month out.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners. Angers rarely pen teams in and Strasbourg have not dominated many games either, so I stay near the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. With both clubs near the drop zone in mid-December, and Strasbourg's coach under pressure after a public row with forwards Conrad Harder and Martial Godo, I expect a tense, scrappy game and lean a little higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.3 shots. Strasbourg should have more of the ball, while Angers' attack has been one of the weakest in the league; the two balance out near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Angers created little in home defeats to Lille and Nice, but Strasbourg's defence gives chances away, so I stay with the number.

401876374.overall: Early view: Brest are 9th and in good form under Julien Lachuer, beating Angers 5-1 and Lyon 2-0 at home, while Troyes are 17th with only 7 goals in 10 games. Brest are without Raphael Le Guen (fractured fibula, out for months) and Brendan Chardonnet's return has been delayed. Neither side plays in Europe that week.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Brest score well at home and Ludovic Ajorque is in form, but Troyes add almost nothing at the other end, so most goals should come from one side. That keeps me near the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners, with Troyes given 4.8. Troyes have lost six of ten and spend long spells defending, so I doubt they win that many corners away from home and lean slightly lower.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. Troyes are fighting to stay up and may defend deep and foul on the break, but nothing in the news points clearly either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.2 shots. Brest had 13 shots against Lyon with only 31% of the ball, and should shoot more at home to a weak side, while Troyes' attack is limited. I stay with the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.5 shots on target. Brest put 6 of 13 on target against Lyon; Troyes have scored only 7 goals all season. That fits the number.

401876373.overall: Early view: Le Havre are bottom with 2 points and five straight defeats, and Didier Digard was removed at the end of October with academy director Jair Karam in interim charge. The club says a new coach should be in place from late November (one report names Valerien Ismael), so this could be one of his first home games. Le Mans, promoted and 15th, have drawn five of ten, including 1-1 with Monaco last time.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. These are two of the weaker attacks in the league (9 and 12 goals), Le Mans have been drawing games, and a new Le Havre coach is likely to start by tightening the defence. I lean slightly lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.3 corners. Le Havre should push at home, but nothing in the news points away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards. A December game between the bottom side and a promoted team fighting to stay up should be tense and stop-start, so I lean higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, most of them from Le Havre. A home side desperate for a first win should shoot plenty, but Le Mans are compact; I keep the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. Neither side finishes well, but the home side should get enough efforts on goal to land near the number.

401876371.overall: Early view: Nice under Olivier Pantaloni have won four of their last five and Wahi has 6 league goals, while Lens are in turmoil after a 9-1 Champions League home defeat to Como, three straight defeats and the sacking of Yannick Cahuzac, their second coach change of the season. Lens host Bodo/Glimt in the Champions League on the Wednesday before this Saturday game, while Nice have no European football.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. Lens' defence has collapsed (12 goals conceded in their last three games in all competitions, with centre-back Ismaelo Ganiou injured), and they arrive on three days' rest. Nice score regularly at home, so I lean higher.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. Nice should have more of the ball at home, but nothing points clearly away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. A Lens side under a new coach may be more disciplined early on; nothing points either way yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.3 shots. A tired Lens side may create less, but Nice should take more shots; the two balance near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. With Lens' defence in poor shape and playing three days after a Champions League game, Nice should get clear sights of goal, so I lean slightly higher.

401876372.overall: Early view: Lille are 2nd with the best defence in the league (7 conceded) and won 2-1 at Rennes last time; Lorient are 10th, have conceded only 8, and won 2-0 at Le Havre. Lille play in Stuttgart in the Champions League on the Wednesday before this Sunday lunchtime game, so some rotation and tired legs are possible.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Lorient's games have averaged under two goals (9 scored, 8 conceded) and Lille's about two (14 and 7), and Lille come off a Champions League trip to Stuttgart. I lean lower.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Lille should have more of the ball, but nothing points clearly away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Nothing in the news points either way at this distance; the referee will matter more.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. Both sides play tight, low-event games, and a Lille team coming off a midweek away trip may control the ball rather than chase, so I lean slightly lower.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.6 shots on target. Two of the stingiest defences in the league should keep clear chances scarce, so I lean slightly lower.

401876369.overall: Early view: Rennes and Monaco are level on 16 points in 8th and 7th. Franck Haise's Rennes score plenty (21) but concede as many, including 13 goals in their last three away league games, while Monaco have not won in five league games (last 5 DLDLD). Both play in Europe on the Thursday before: Rennes at home to Dinamo Zagreb in the Europa League and Monaco away at Brighton in the Conference League, so both arrive on short rest.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Rennes' games have been wild (42 goals in ten), but Monaco's have been tight (24 in ten), and Thursday games for both may slow things down. That points to the number rather than past it.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Rennes at home should press, but nothing points clearly away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Tired legs after Thursday games can mean late challenges, but nothing in the news points clearly either way.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots. Rennes shoot a lot at home and Monaco need a win, but fatigue after European games may trim the total a little; I stay near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Nothing points away from the number at this stage.

401876368.overall: Early view: the Olympico, with Marseille 4th on five straight league wins and Lyon 5th after losing 2-0 at Brest. One report says Lyon were about to name a new coach (Carlos Vicens) right after that defeat, so this may be one of his first big games. Both play Europa League home games on the Thursday before (Lyon v Union SG, Marseille v Celta), so both arrive on short rest.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Marseille's games have produced 36 goals in ten and they have scored in every recent win, but Lyon were toothless at Brest (10 shots, 2 on target) and a new coach may start cautiously. I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Lyon keep a lot of the ball and Marseille shoot often; nothing points clearly away from the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.8 cards. This is a heated rivalry and the number already allows for that; tired legs after Thursday games could add a booking or two, but I stay near it until the referee is known.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots. Marseille had the second-most shots in the league before matchday 10, while Lyon have struggled to turn possession into chances. That balances out near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Nothing points clearly away from the number a month out.

401875515.overall: Early view: two sides near the bottom half meet in Zwolle, with PEC 13th on 12 points and Excelsior 15th on 11 after five straight league defeats. Neither club has a European fixture that week, so both should be close to full strength, and the stakes are about pulling clear of the relegation places. I found little fresh team news for either club, so this view rests mostly on form and the table.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. I lean a little lower: PEC have scored few this season (goal difference of minus 11 after 12 games) and a match between two nervous lower-table sides often turns cautious. Excelsior's losing run does suggest they can be opened up, which keeps this from being a strong lean.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. I found nothing on either team's style or line-ups that points away from that, so I stay with the site's figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.6 cards. I lean slightly higher because this is a direct game near the drop zone and Excelsior, on five straight losses, may play with more edge. The referee is not known yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 26 shots. With no injury or tactical news found for either side, I see no reason to move off the site's number this far out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean slightly lower in line with my goals view: two struggling attacks in a tense relegation-zone game tend to produce plenty of shots but fewer clean chances.

401875514.overall: Early view: leaders PSV host Telstar, who are 16th on 10 points. I lean a little higher: Bayern will have two extra days of rest over a Hoffenheim side coming back from Anderlecht with a patched-up back line, which usually means long spells of Bayern pressure and lots of attempts. Hoffenheim should still get chances on the break.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.3 shots on target. That already reflects Bayern's attacking level, and losing Gnabry and Saibari trims their options a little. I stay with the number.

401884702.overall: Early view: Bremen (6th) and Leverkusen (5th) are one point apart in the race for Europe. Daniel Thioune's Bremen lean on an in-form Niclas Füllkrug but are without Mitchell Weiser (thigh) for an unknown period, while Carles Martinez's Leverkusen have leaked goals in the league and host Besiktas in the Europa League on the Thursday before this Sunday evening game.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals. I lean slightly higher: Leverkusen have conceded 17 in 9 league games, including 3-0 at Hoffenheim and 4-2 at home to Stuttgart, and Bremen's games have been open too (17 scored, 15 conceded). Füllkrug scored in seven league games in a row before the break.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners. Leverkusen create lots of attacks, but Bremen lose a key crosser on the right if Weiser is still out. Nothing points clearly either way yet.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. A home game with European places at stake should be competitive, but neither side has a notable discipline problem in what I found. I stay with the number until the referee is named.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.2 shots. I lean a little higher: Leverkusen lead the Europa League for shots and xG, and their games this autumn have been open at both ends. Rotation after the Thursday game against Besiktas is the main risk to this.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. That already fits two attacking sides, and Moussa Diaby's return from his thigh injury (one report expects him back after the November break) is still to be confirmed. I stay with the number for now.

401882776.overall: Early view: third-placed Atlético (four wins in their last five) host a Valencia side 19th on 9 points and fighting relegation under Javier Aguirre, who took over in October. Atlético play at PSV on the Wednesday before, so some rotation is possible. José Gayà's red card against Real Madrid should be served long before 13 December; the date may still move.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly lower: Aguirre has set Valencia up with a back five and a deep block, and they scored only once in their last two league games. Atlético may also manage the game after the trip to Eindhoven.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. I lean a little higher: against a Valencia back five Atlético should have long spells of pressure in wide areas, which tends to push the home corner count up.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. I lean slightly higher: a relegation-threatened Valencia defending deep for long periods means plenty of tactical fouls, and Valencia need points badly.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.7 shots. I lean a bit lower: Valencia's attack is weak (only 3 goals at Mestalla per one preview) and expecting almost 10 shots from them away at Atlético looks generous.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Nothing clear points either way this far out: Atlético should create plenty, but a packed Valencia box usually blocks a lot of efforts.

401882774.overall: Early view: a mid-table meeting between promoted Deportivo (9th) and Athletic (7th), separated by one point. Athletic are without their main strikers, Gorka Guruzeta (knee ligament, out until May) and Maroan Sannadi (hamstring, out until late December). I found little other news for this match, so the view rests mostly on form and those absences.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. I lean slightly lower: with Guruzeta and Sannadi both out, Athletic lose their focal points up front, and both sides have drawn often recently (two draws each in their last five).

corners.text: The numbers say 11.0 corners. Nothing in the news moves this: Athletic still have Nico Williams and Berenguer out wide per the probable line-ups, and Deportivo at Riazor tend to play on the front foot.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. No derby or high stakes and no referee yet, so I see no reason to move away from the model.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.7 shots. Neither side has a European game that week, so both should be fresh; I see nothing pushing this either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. I lean a little lower because Athletic are missing their two main centre-forwards, which should cut the quality of their finishing more than their volume of shots.

401882773.overall: Early view: Elche, 18th under Martín Anselmi, host a Sevilla side 6th but inconsistent (one win in five). Elche had not won at home this season as of early November and need points badly. Thomas Lemar (Elche) and Peque (Sevilla) are expected back from injury by late November.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. I lean lower: Elche have kept the ball under Anselmi but created little at home (they lost 0-1 to Valencia after a goalless first half), and earlier kept three clean sheets in four games.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners. I lean slightly higher: Anselmi wants an attacking, front-foot side, and in the Valencia game Elche had more of the ball and pushed hard late, which drives corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards. A relegation-threatened home side against a mid-table Sevilla fits this number, and with no referee named yet I stay with it.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots. Neither club is in Europe, so no rotation, and nothing in the news points either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. I lean a little lower, in line with Elche's poor chance creation at home despite having more of the ball.

401882772.overall: Early view: Espanyol (13th) are now coached by Eder Sarabia, who replaced the sacked Manolo González in late October and wants a possession and pressing game. Celta (11th) play away at Marseille in the Europa League on the Thursday before this Sunday trip, so fatigue and rotation are likely. Espanyol striker Kike García is out until around December.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals. Two things pull in opposite directions: Celta's tired legs after Marseille could open the game, but Espanyol may still lack Kike García's goals. I stay with the model.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.6 corners. I lean higher: Sarabia's sides keep the ball and push full-backs high, and a Celta side coming off a Thursday away game is likely to spend long spells defending.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Nothing specific points either way; no referee yet and no particular rivalry.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.5 shots. I lean slightly higher: Sarabia's pressing should give Espanyol more shots at home than under the previous coach, especially against a Celta side short of rest.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. More Espanyol shots may not mean better ones while their main striker is still returning, so I stay with the model.

401882771.overall: Early view: two struggling sides, Levante 17th and Alavés 12th but without a win in five. Alavés have lost Facundo Garcés and Mikel Rodríguez to knee ligament injuries until April. I found little other news for this match, so the view rests mostly on form and those absences.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. I lean slightly lower: both teams are low on confidence and near the bottom, which often makes for a cautious game, and Alavés have not won in five.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. I found nothing on either side's style that moves this, so I stay with the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. I lean a little higher: with both sides near the relegation places in December, I expect a tense, scrappy game with more fouls than usual.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.5 shots. Neither team is in Europe, so both should be fresh, and nothing in the news points clearly either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.6 shots on target. No clear reason to move away from the model this far out.

401882770.overall: Early view: bottom-placed Málaga (5 points, no league win yet) host leaders Barcelona (33 points, 48 goals in 12 games). Coach Juanfran Funes is under pressure and reports name possible replacements, though no change had been made as of early November. Barcelona host Manchester City in the Champions League five days earlier, so some rotation is possible; Adam Aznou's ban should be served well before this game.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.2 goals. I lean slightly lower: Barcelona play Manchester City on the Tuesday and may rotate or ease off once ahead, and Málaga have scored only 9 goals all season, so most of the total relies on Barcelona alone.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners. Barcelona should dominate the ball against a deep Málaga, but a rotated side may be less relentless; I see no strong reason to move.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards. Málaga will defend a lot and may pick up fouls, but one-sided games often stay calm; I stay with the model.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots. Barcelona's volume should hold even with changes, and nothing in the news points either way.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.6 shots on target. I lean a little lower: expecting 4 on target from Málaga looks generous for a team averaging under a goal a game, and Barcelona may rotate after City.

401882775.overall: Early view: fourth-placed Betis host promoted Racing (10th), who came from behind to win at Málaga in their last game. Betis host Como in the Champions League on the Wednesday before, so rotation is possible. Cucho Hernández (Betis) and Andrés Martín (Racing) should be back from injury by then; Racing's Álvaro Mantilla is out for the season.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, which is high. I lean lower: Betis may rotate after the Como game four days earlier, and Racing have shown they can stay in games, including a comeback win away at Málaga.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners. Betis' wide play (Ezzalzouli and Antony in the probable line-ups) supports a high count, so I stay with the model.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. No referee yet and no rivalry; Racing's 3.0 expected cards already reflects a side defending a lot away from home.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.7 shots. I lean slightly lower for the same reason as goals: a possible rotated Betis after the Champions League may not keep up a 20-shot pace.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.9 shots on target. Nothing specific moves this beyond the rotation risk already reflected in shots.

401882769.overall: Early view: José Mourinho's Real Madrid (2nd, five straight league wins) host Osasuna, 16th with one win in five. Madrid play at Arsenal in the Champions League on the Wednesday before, so rotation is likely. Rodrygo and Raúl Asencio are working back from injury, and one report says Aurélien Tchouaméni had a groin problem with France on 10 November.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. I lean slightly lower: with a midweek trip to Arsenal, Madrid may rotate and ease off once ahead.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Madrid should have most of the ball against a deep Osasuna; I see nothing pushing this either way.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards. Osasuna usually defend with intensity away at big sides, which the model already reflects; Jon Moncayola's ban should be served well before this game.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots. A rotated Madrid still usually produces volume at the Bernabéu, so I stay with the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target. With Mbappé, Bellingham and Güler likely involved in some form, nothing points away from the model.

401882768.overall: Early view: Real Sociedad (5th, four wins in five) host Getafe (15th). Both play at home in Europe on Thursday 10 December, Real Sociedad against Torreense and Getafe against Inter Escaldes, and Getafe then go to Ajax a week later, so both are likely to rotate. One October report said José Bordalás had a public row with Getafe's president over squad planning.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals. I lean slightly lower: Getafe sit 15th and are likely to rotate, and both sides have only two days' rest after Thursday's European games.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Real Sociedad should have most of the ball, which the model already expects; nothing moves this.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean a touch higher: the model already expects a high count, and tired legs after Thursday games add late fouls. Nemanja Gudelj's ban should be served by then.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. I lean slightly lower: two rotated sides on short rest point to a slower game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Already a modest figure; I see no reason to move it.

401882767.overall: Early view: Villarreal (8th, mixed form) host Rayo Vallecano (14th), whose coach Beñat San José was under pressure after fan protests in October. Villarreal host Sabah in the Champions League on the Tuesday before, leaving five days' rest. Rayo are without goalkeeper Augusto Batalla (until January) and centre-back Luiz Felipe (long term).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals. I lean slightly higher: Rayo are missing their first-choice goalkeeper and a starting centre-back, and Villarreal at home with five days' rest should create plenty.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners. I found nothing on either side's style or team news that moves this, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards. Rayo's 2.7 expected cards already reflects an away side under pressure; Renato Veiga's ban should be served well before this game. No referee yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots. Nothing in the news points either way; Villarreal's midweek game is at home and gives them five days to recover.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target. I lean a little higher, in line with goals, given the gaps in Rayo's defence.
